1903.key_title: main groups of plants in Victoria

leads.lead_text: Mature plant reproducing by minute spores; spores produced in capsules
Mature plant reproducing by seeds formed following pollination; seeds produced in cones or in fruit derived from a flower ovary

Spore capsules (sporangia) borne on the undersides or margins of fronds or in the axils of modified leaves or scales, sometimes aggregated into cone-like strobili, often with a band of differentiated cells with thickened cell-walls (annulus), rarely fused to form bi- or trilocular synangia, indehiscent or dehiscing with a single slit to one side; spores germinating into short-lived gametophytes that give rise to much larger and independant sporophytes that live on after gametophyte senescence

Spore capsules often borne on an elongate stalk (seta) or sometimes sessile or embedded in the plant, indehiscent or dehiscent by 2–7 slits or an operculum; spores germinating into ephemeral to long-lived gametophytes that give rise to dependant, continually attached and often smaller sporophytes comprising the capsule and if present the seta
Capsules elongate, horn shaped and without a seta, frequently produced; photosynthetic organ a pad-like thallus; photosynthetic cells with one or two chloroplasts

Capsules not elongate and horn-shaped, often with an elongate seta; photosynthetic organs leaves clearly differentiated from a stem or if a thallus then photosynthetic cells usually with many more than two chloroplasts

Photosynthetic organ a pad-like thallus or leaves clearly differentiated from a stem; leaves when present arranged in two or three ranks, simple, divided apically into lobes or with adaxial or abaxial lobules, never with a costa but rarely with a unistratose line of elongate cells along centre; leaf cells usually with non-green, usually grey, brownish or hyaline oil body organelles in addition to green chloroplasts when fresh

Photosynthetic organs leaves clearly differentiated from a stem, never a pad-like thallus; leaves arranged in two, three or multiple ranks, often spirally arranged along stem, simple, never divided apically into lobes, rarely with a lobe attached along the midline of the leaf (vaginant lamina), often with a multistratose costa along midline of leaf; leaf cells without visible organelles other than chloroplasts
Plants with flowers; ovules enclosed within carpel(s); leaves simple or compound
Plants usually without flowers; ovules naked on scales typically aggregated into woody or fleshy cones; leaves simple (sometimes very small)
Leaves usually with net-like venation; flower parts usually in whorls of 4 or 5 (rarely 3, 6 or more); taproot present at least at seedling stage; embryo (and usually seedling) with 2 cotyledons
Leaves usually with parallel venation; flower parts usually in whorls of 3 or 6 (rarely 2 or 4); roots fibrous; embryo (and usually seedling) with 1 cotyledon
Plants without flowers; cones woody; trees or shrubs, often producing resin
Male flowers producing anthers; cones fleshy; non-resinous shrubs or subshrubs
[link through]
Plants free-floating or sometimes on soil around water seeps; sori produced on submerged leaves or submerged leaf axis
Plants anchored to substrate
Leaves basal, linear, terete (often grass-like)
Leaves borne on stem, or if basal, flattened and narrowing towards base
Leaves flattened at base; sporangia solitary, enclosed within swollen leaf-bases
Leaves rounded at base; sporangia grouped, not enclosed in swollen leaf-bases
[link through]
Leaves stout, fleshy; sporangia borne in small cone terminal on leafless fleshy stalk
Leaves slender, coiled when young; sporangia enclosed in hard, globular structure attached to rhizome
Lamina divided into 4 leaflets (clover-like); sporangia in hard, globular or bean-shaped structure attached to rhizomes (aquatic or at edge of water)
Lamina variously divided or undivided, not as above; sporangia not inside hardened structure
Sporangia borne in axils of leaves; leaves sparse or crowded along stem, usually spiralled (but flattened into one plane in Lycopodium scariosum and Selaginella kraussiana)
Sporangia borne on margin or lower surface of lamina or fertile spike; plants bearing fronds
Sporangia in fused groups of 2 or 3, borne in axil of forked leaf
Sporangia borne in small cones (strobili) or singly in axils of normal leaves
Leaves without ligule; spores of one kind
Leaves ligulate; spores of 2 kinds, larger and smaller (megaspores and microspores)
[link through]
Sporangia borne on a spike or long-stalked, comb-like structure
Sporangia scattered or aggregated into groups on undersurface of lamina, not as above
Fronds divided from near base into distinct vegetative and fertile structures; sterile lamina broad and leaf-like
Fronds bearing comb-like sporangial structures or sterile, narrow and wiry throughout
[link through]
Fronds with paired branches forking several times, with (usually dormant) buds within the angle of each fork; pinnules narrowly oblong or semicircular
Fronds variously divided or entire, but not as above
Lamina delicate, translucent, only 1 cell thick for the greater part; sori borne in tubular, funnel-shaped or roundish 2-lipped indusia (epiphytes or on rocks)
Lamina membranous to leathery, opaque; sori with or without indusium; indusi variously shaped
Ferns with trunk of any sort
Ferns without trunk
Lamina once pinnate
Lamina 2-several times pinnate
Primary and secondary rachis grooves confluent
Primary and secondary rachis not confluent, or rachis not grooved
Lamina 2-pinnate
Lamina 3-pinnate
Stipe and rachis with numerous soft scales; sporangia small, grouped into circular sori with round, centrally stalked indusium
Stipe and rachis without scales; sporangia large, in masses on undersurface of leaf, without indusium
[link through]
Frond bases rough or spiny, with narrow scales; sori between midvein and margin, with or without indusium
Frond bases smooth, with fine hairs; sori marginal, with 2-lipped indusium
[link through]
Fronds simple
Fronds once to several times pinnate, or variously lobed
Fertile and sterile fronds not markedly different, never almost terete; lamina glabrous or with stellate hairs
Fertile and sterile fronds dissimilar, the fertile narrow and almost terete, sterile fronds broader and flat; lamina glabrous
Fronds once pinnate; sori linear to oblong, either discontinuous or continuous, in 1 or more rows parallel to midvein, if marginal then pinnae narrowed and almost covered by sori
Fronds once to several times pinnate or variously lobed; sori round or, if linear or oblong, either oblique to midvein or marginal on unspecialized frond
Lamina pinnately lobed (i.e. pinnae not divided to rachis)
Lamina once to many times pinnate
Stolons producing globular tubers; lamina once pinnate, pinnae oblong or lanceolate, not further lobed;  indusium reniform or round
Plants not producing tubers; lamina not as above; indusium shape variable or absent
[link through]
Sori marginal
Sori on lamina surface
Indusia opening away from the centre of the pinnae
Indusia or modified pinnae margin opening towards the middle of pinnae (but may be towards the margin of individual lobe in Asplenium)
Indusia pouch-shaped, opening at one end only; rhizome long-creeping over substrate
Indusia round or elongate, attached along one side only; rhizome subterranean
[link through]
Sori protected by spherical indusium and recurved pinnae lobetogether creating cup-like structure (although indusium may be hidden in mature sori)
Sori protected by narrow and flap-like indusium, attached along one edge
[link through]
Rhizome creeping or semi-erect, covered in scales, unbranched, if branched fronds less than 100 cm long
Rhizome long-creeping, covered with hairs, or if with scales rhizome branched and fronds 60–200 cm long
Sori not protected by indusium or modified leaf margin, even when immature
Sori protected by indusium or modified leaf margin, at least when immature
Mature fronds less than 30 cm tall
Mature fronds more than 30 cm tall
Lamina sparsely to (usually) densely covered in colourless to rust-coloured hairs
Lamina glabrous
Fronds delicate, erect, 5–12 cm tall; sporangia clustered irregularly along veins; annuals
Ferns firm in texture, often pendent, 5–25 cm long; sporangia grouped into oval sori which are arranged in a single row either side of midvein; perennials
Lamina 3–4-pinnate
Lamina 1–2-pinnate
Lamina 2-pinnate; sporangia not arranged in sori, clustered around veins; widespread in gullies and along streams, usually with a thick fibrous butt
Lamina once pinnate to almost 2-pinnate; sporangia arranged in round sori; rare, on limestone in south-west of State
[link through]
Indusium elongate, attached along one edge to lateral nerve, oblique to midvein
Indusium hemispherical, pouch-shaped, kidney-shaped or ovate, attached centrally or at base, or united with lamina along both sides and opening terminally
Rhizome scales with netted pattern; major vein(s) usually raised on upper surface of pinnae
Rhizome scales without netted pattern; major vein(s) not raised on upper surface
Undersurface of rachises with scales, bristles or hairs
Undersurface of rachises without scales or hairs
Fronds 2–4-pinnate; rachis groove flanked by prominent ridges
Fronds once pinnate (but deeply lobed to almost 2-pinnate); rachis groove not flanked by 2 prominent ridges
Lamina membranous and dull, 1–2-pinnate; rhizome short, subterranean, fronds clustered near tip
Lamina shiny and stiff, 2–3-pinnate; rhizome long-creeping along surface of substrate, fronds distant
[link through]

breadcrumbs.key_title: Key to the main groups of plants in Victoria

leads.lead_text: Leaves scales or needle-like, alternate, opposite or whorled, rarely flat; cone woody
Leaves flat, oblong-linear, alternate; seed subtending fleshy, berry-like structure
Leaves needle-like, rarely flattened, mostly greater than 15 mm long, solitary or in clusters of 2–5 or densely whorled, free from stem; female cones mostly greater than 30 mm long
Leaves scale like, mostly opposite or whorled and less than 10 mm long (rarely flat, 2-ranked and up to 30 mm in Sequoia), appressed to stem; female cones less than 30 mm long
[link through]

breadcrumbs.key_title: Key to the main groups of plants in Victoria

leads.lead_text: Aquatic plants, floating free on or near the water surface, not rooting in substrate
Land or aquatic plants, if aquatic and with floating leaves then rooting in substrate

Plant consisting of small (less than 1 cm long) flat or flattened ovoid leaf or thallus, with or without simple roots from undersurface; plants readily reproducing vegetatively by lateral buds; flowers produced in small pits on upper surface, microscopic and rarely observed
Plants conspicuous, with leaves c. 5 cm long or more, the petioles much inflated and spongy, roots abundant, feathery; flowers conspicuous (c. 5 cm diam.), mauve, produced in spikes
Marine aquatics, or aquatics of non-marine habitats with leaves permanently submerged, but inflorescence sometimes emergent from water
Terrestrial or semi-aquatic plants, or aquatics with leaves floating or emergent from water
Plants of marine or brackish habitats
Plants of fresh water
Leaves ligulate
Leaves without ligules
Plants of brackish habitats (including estuaries, rarely extending to the intertidal zone); leaves 1 mm wide or less; flowers unisexual, solitary or clustered in axils
Marine plants of deep waters and rock-pools; leaves at least 4 mm wide
[link through]
Leaf blade and sheath shed leaving a circular scar; flowers unisexual, enclosed within leaf-sheaths
Leaf blade shed but sheath persistent and fibrous; flowers bisexual, in several terminal spikes
[link through]
[link through]
Leaves elliptic to ovate, c. 1 cm wide or more; flowers with perianth (males with 3 segments, females with 6)
Leaves narrow linear, to 1 mm wide; flowers without perianth
Flowers bisexual, borne at the end of a long, spirally coiled peduncle
Flowers unisexual, in short spikes, remaining enclosed in sheathing leaf-bases
Flowers bisexual, in emergent spikes; perianth segments 4
Flowers unisexual, remaining submerged; perianth segments 0, 3 or 6
[link through]
Leaves ovate to linear, mostly much more than 1 mm wide, but if ever less, then with finely toothed margins
Leaves narrow-linear, less than 1 mm wide, with entire margins
[link through]

Flowers lacking perianth, packed in thickish spike, subtended and partially enclosed by a tubular bract (spathe), margins overlapping or connate at base; apical part of spike male only or with a sterile appendix, lower part of spike female or bisexual; fleshy usually rhizomatous herb, usually near swamps or watercourses
Flowers with a perianth or if perianth lacking, flowers not arranged in spatheate spikes
Flowers unisexual
Flowers bisexual

Flowers inconspicuous, often minute, subtended (and often enclosed by) paired or solitary, overlapping bracts or scales, in heads or spikelets; perianth absent or of 1–8 scales or bristles, usually concealed within bracts
Flowers conspicuous (but not always coloured), or if inconspicuous at least with distinct perianth parts
Male and female flowers small, mixed in spherical heads 2–8 mm diam., lacking conspicuous bracts; mostly marsh or aquatic plants
Flowers in spikelets surrounded by glume-like bracts
[link through]
Wiry plants with jointed stems; leaves reduced to sheathing bracts (bracts overlapping at base); male and female plants separate (except sometimes in Lepyrodia)
Leaves well developped, or if ever reduced to sheathing bracts then these fused at the base and plants with both male and female flowers or flowers bisexual
Tiny, tufted annuals; male and female flowers mixed in terminal heads subtended and exceeded by 2–6 equal or subequal bracts
Habit various; if inflorescence ever a terminal head then flowers bisexual
Inflorescence green or greenish, with a pair of prominent, erect sheathing bracts enclosing the flowers and their small, membranous, subtending bracts
Inflorescence red, flower cluster subtended by 4–6 more or less equal sheathing bracts, individual flowers (ovaries and stamens) not subtended by bracts
[link through]

Flowers arranged in cylindric or distichous spikelets or spikes (rarely 1-flowered), rarely subtended by a pair of sterile bracts; individual flowers subtended by a solitary bract (glume); leaf-sheath usually with fused margins; stems cylindric, flattened or 3-sided, with solid internodes (sedges)

Flowers arranged in distichous (sometimes 1-flowered) spikelets, usually subtended by a pair of sterile bracts (glumes); individual flowers enclosed by a pair of bracts (lemma and palea), or if ever only one bract present, then fertile flowers only 1 per spikelet; leaf-sheath usually with free margins; stems usually cylindric, with hollow internodes (grasses)
Plants monoecious, male flowers borne above females in inflorescence; aquatic or semi-aquatic plants
Plants dioecious; mostly terrestrial
Perianth segments not petaloid; flowers sessile, in spikes or globular clusters; leaves linear, flattened or triangular in cross-section
Perianth segments in 2 distinct whorls, the outermost petaloid; flowers pedicellate, whorled; at least the emergent leaves with a distinct ovate to sagittate blade
Climbers, usually with retrorse spines along stems; leaves ovate, with prominent reticulate venation; eastern Victoria only
Non-climbers, or, if plants every climbing then venation linear, lacking prominent reticulate venation
Leaves well-developed; perianth segments more or less membranous or somewhat fleshy; fruit containing 1–few seeds
Leaves reduced to sheathing bracts; perianth segments scarious; fruit containing many small seeds
Carpels not fused or shortly united at base only
Carpels united for the greater part or carpel solitary
Tufted annuals or perennials, less than 10 cm high; land plants (but often growing near water)
Perennials, more than 10 cm high; aquatic or marsh plants
Inflorescence green or greenish, with a pair of prominent, erect sheathing bracts enclosing the flowers and their small, membranous, subtending bracts
Inflorescence red, flower cluster subtended by 4–6 more or less equal sheathing bracts, individual flowers (ovaries and stamens) not subtended by bracts
[link through]
Flowers borne in once-forked spikes; perianth of a single white segment; anthers 6–12, purple; carpels 3–6
Flowers borne in simple spikes or panicles; perianth of 3 or more segments (but inconspicuous in Juncaginaceae)
[link through]
Perianth segments, stamens and carpels each 4
Perianth segments, stamens and carpels not each 4
[link through]
Perianth segments in 2 distinct whorls, the outermost petaloid; at least the emergent leaves with a distinct ovate to sagittate blade
Perianth segments all similar, not petaloid; leaves linear, terete or strap-shaped
Ovary superior or perianth of petals and/or sepals absent
Ovary inferior, perianth well-developed

Flowers inconspicuous, often minute, within imbricate bracts or scales (glumes), in spikelets; perianth absent or of 18 scales or bristles, usually concealed within bracts (chiefly grasses and sedges)
Flowers conspicuous (but not always coloured), or if inconspicuous at least with distinct perianth parts rather than scales or bristles

Tiny, tufted plants; male and female flowers mixed in terminal heads subtended and exceeded by 2–6 equal or subequal bracts; individual flowers sometimes separated by a minute membranous bract; fruit a dehiscent, 1-seeded capsule
Plants various, if ever male and female flowers mixed in heads then bracts (glumes) separating individual flowers conspicuous; fruit indehiscent, 1-seeded
Inflorescence green or greenish, with a pair of prominent, erect sheathing bracts enclosing the flowers; individual flowers separated by a minute membranous bract
Inflorescence reddish, with 2 or 3 pairs of equal sheathing bracts enclosing the flowers; individual flowers not subtended by bracts
[link through]

Flowers arranged in cylindric or distichous spikelets or spikes (rarely 1-flowered), rarely subtended by a pair of sterile bracts; individual flowers subtended by a solitary bract (glume); leaf-sheath usually with fused margins; stems cylindric, flattened or 3-sided (sedges)

Flowers arranged in distichous (sometimes 1-flowered) spikelets, usually subtended by a pair of sterile bracts (glumes); individual flowers enclosed by a pair of bracts (lemma and palea), or if ever only one bract present, then fertile flowers only 1 per spikelet; leaf-sheath usually with free margins; stems usually cylindric, with hollow internodes (grasses)
Perianth segments 4 (inner pair small); stamen 1; uncommon yellow-flowered, tufted semi-aquatic
Perianth segments 6
[link through]
Leaves compound; stems massive, woody, erect and undivided (palms)
Leaves simple or absent
Perianth sepaloid (green, brown or translucent)
Perianth petaloid (white or coloured), but sometimes segments small
Carpels fused; style solitary, with 3 stigmas
Carpels free or nearly so; stigmas sessile
Stamens 3
Stamens 6 (sometimes 3 much longer than others)

Rhizome bright red; leaves tufted, linear, to 1.2 m long, plicate; scape up to 2.5 m tall; inflorescence a dense cylindircal panicle, with numerous yellow flowers; style and lowermost anther turned sideways
Rhizome absent or not conspicuously bright red, but if ever somewhat reddish, neither with leaves long and plicate nor with scape approaching 2 m high
[link through]
Inner perianth segments united; flowers short-lived with yellowish, tissue-like petals; inflorescence a dense spherical head on an undivided, wiry scape
Inner perianth segments free; other features in combination not as above
[link through]

Tufted plants, stems commonly annual, or if prostrate, scrambling or twining, then either leafless or leaves sessile; rhizomatous or with a bulbous or cormous rootstock; inflorescence a raceme or panicle, not subtended by spathe-like bracts

Prostrate, scrambling, much-branched plant with perennial, succulent stems; leaves ovate with sheathing petioles; rooting readily from nodes; inflorescence of 1ew flowers subtended by a single or pair of spathe-like bracts
Aquatic plants; flowers mauve and yellow in a terminal spike-like raceme; leaf-blade ovate, on long petiole
Land plants, rarely growing in marshy situations and then with features not as above

Tufted plants, stems commonly annual, or if prostrate, scrambling or twining, then either leafless or leaves sessile; rhizomatous or with a bulbous or cormous rootstock; inflorescence a raceme or panicle, not subtended by spathe-like bracts

Prostrate, scrambling, much-branched plant with perennial, succulent stems; leaves ovate with sheathing petioles; rooting readily from nodes; inflorescence of 1-few flowers subtended by a single or pair of spathe-like bracts
Flower lacking labellum; stamens 3 or 6, not assoicated with the style
Flower usually with distinct labellum; stamens 1, united with style or style held between anther locules
Aquatic plants with leaf-blades ovate, floating on water surface; flowers emergent or floating, showy, whitish with red-purple blotch at base; submerged cleistogamous flowers also produced
Terrestrial plants, or if semi-aquatic, then leaf blades more or less linear and emergent from water
Stamens 3
Stamens 6
Mostly leafy herbs, always with chlorophyll (i.e. some parts green), growing and flowering above ground level
Leafless herbs without chlorophyll (i.e. with no green parts), growing and flowering within leaf-litter layer of wet, shaded forests
Flowers zygomorphic, perianth tubular, externally tomentose; inflorescence a one-sided raceme
Flowers actinomorphic, or if zygomorphic then features not as above
[link through]
[link through]
Labellum derived from modified perianth segment; stamen and style united, with stamen distal to style
Labellum derived from staminodes; style held between anther locules, the style extending beyond the anther
[link through]

breadcrumbs.key_title: Key to the main groups of plants in Victoria

leads.lead_text: Aquatics with all leaves permanently submerged and divided into numerous filiform or linear segments, often rapidly shrivelling upon exposure to air (but inflorescences sometimes emergent)
Land plants or semi-aquatics, with at least the terminal leaves (when present) normally exposed to the air (but leaves sometimes lying flat on water surface)
Leaves whorled; flowers minute, inconspicuous
Leaves alternate or opposite; flowers conspicuous
Leaves pinnately dissected; flowers in a terminal spike; perianth present
Leaves dichotomously forked 1–3 times; perianth absent
Leaves opposite; flowers with dark red or blackish perianth segments
Leaves alternate; flowers with yellowish segments
Plant free-floating; leaves interspersed with bladders; flower zygomorphic, conspicuously spurred, emergent on erect peduncle; fruit a capsule, ripening in the air
Plant rooted in mud; bladders absent; flower actinomorphic, barely emergent; pedicel recurving in fruit (head of achenes ripening under water)
Herbs lacking chlorophyll (stems brownish or yellowish); leaves reduced to scales, or absent; fruit a capsule
Green plants; if ever leaves absent at maturity, then plants woody; fruit various
Slender, twining, stem-parasites; flowers actinomorphic, minute, usually in globoid clusters
Stout, erect, root parasites; flowers zygomorphic, conspicuous, more or less tubular, arranged in spikes
Leafless, twining, stem-parasites, rooted only in juvenile phase; flowers 3-partite; fruit a drupe with viscid flesh
Plants rooted at maturity, or if stem-parasites then not twining, leaves normally present and flowers 4–5-partite
Shrubs and trees with jointed, grooved, filiform branchlets; leaves present as whorls of 5 or more minute teeth, encircling branchlet joints; infructescence a woody cone
Plants not combining the above features
Perianth of 2 (rarely more) distinct whorls (sepals and petals), differing from each other in shape, size or colour (calyx or corolla sometimes deciduous at anthesis)
Perianth absent or of 1 whorl, or of 2 or more similar whorls (sometimes falling off as an operculum at anthesis)
Petals free to base (rarely shortly united near the tips)
Petals all united (or rarely with 1 free petal), at least at the base, the tubular part sometimes short
Ovary inferior or semi-inferior
Ovary superior (but sometimes closely surrounded by a narrow calyx-tube)
Apparent petals (petaloid staminodes) numerous, brightly coloured or white; succulents
Petals 2–9
Stamens numerous (more than 10)
Stamens 10 or fewer
Leaves lacking stipules, entire, aromatic with translucent oil dots
Leaves with stipules, or if stipules lacking, then leaves entire, usually non-aromatic but never with oil dots
Leaves opposite, trifoliolate (sometimes apparently whorled)
Leaves alternate
Leaves without stipules; rare evergreen rainforest trees of far east
Leaves with stipules; herbs or shrubs, if ever small trees, then garden-escapes and often deciduous

Aquatic herbs (sometimes growing on mud), usually with most leaves submerged and pinnately divided into filiform segments; flowers in terminal spikes projecting above the water's surface, often unisexual
Terrestrial plants, or if aquatic, submerged leaves not pinnate, and flowers bisexual
Trees or shrubs (sometimes climbing)
Herbs (sometimes semi-woody in garden-escaped Fuchsia)

Flowers sessile or subsessile, clustered into a head, surrounded by an involucre of 4 spreading creamy-white bracts, each 2.5–3.5 cm long; fruit a pinkish globular fleshy head c. 1–3 cm diam.; garden-escaped shrub or small tree
Plants not combining the above features
Flowers in umbels (simple or compound), usually small and greenish; ovary 2-carpellate
Flowers not in umbels (but sometimes clustered in cymes); ovary various
Fruit dry; leaves commonly ternately or pinnately divided, rarely 2 cm long
Fruit succulent, berry-like, leaves variously pinnate, palmately divided or entire, or if fruit dry, then leaves entire, linear, and usually more than 2 cm long
Branch-parasites; leaves entire; fruit a succulent drupe with sticky flesh
Non-parasitic plants, rooted in soil or mud
Spiny shrubs
Shrubs or herbs without spines; fruit non-succulent
Leaves alternate, palmately lobed; fruit a succulent, many-seeded berry c. 2 cm long
Leaves and spines opposite (leaves usually present only on younger stems); fruit a 3-partite capsule
Leaves simple and entire (if ever toothed, then bearing stellate hairs); sepals 5
Leaves either compound, or simple and toothed, never stellate-hairy; sepals 4 or 6–8
Leaves glabrous, aromatic, with translucent oil dots; style simple
Leaves hairy (often with stellate hairs), neither aromatic nor oil-dotted; style 3-branched
Leaves trifoliolate; sepals 6–8; fruit a 2-locular capsule
Leaves simple; sepals 4; fruit a 1-seeded nut or nutlet
Shrubs or climbers growing at margins of rainforest; leaves opposite, ovate, 1.5–4 cm wide; petals minute or apparently absent, distinctly smaller than sepals
Plants not containing the features above
Perianth whorls green and sepaloid (petals absent, epicalyx sometimes developed); fruit an achene, commonly with barbed spines or prickles at the apex; flowers in spikes, heads, clusters or corymbs
Inner perianth whorl petaloid, sometimes small, epicalyx absent; fruit not spinose or prickly
Flowers in umbels or sessile in heads; petals 5; styles normally 2; plants often aromatic (includes Hydrocotyle and Trachymene which are now included in Araliaceae, see note under family description)
Flowers not in umbels or heads; petals 4 or 5; styles 1–4; plants not aromatic
Style single, stigma lobed; ovary elongate; seeds numerous; petals conspicuous
Styles 2–4, stigmas usually plumose; ovary short and broad; seeds 1–4; petals often minute
Carpels and styles free, or the carpels shortly united near the base
Carpels and/or styles distinctly united for the greater part, or ovary consisting of a single carpel
Sepals and petals each 2 or 3
Sepals and petals more than 3
Small herbs; leaves opposite, succulent
Shrubs or vines; leaves alternate, not succulent
Montane to alpine shrubs with aromatic (peppery to the taste), oblong to oblanceolate leaves
Vine or liane of lowland forests and rainforests; leaves broadly ovate, cordate at base
Stamens more than twice as many as petals
Stamens not more than twice as many as petals
Herbs, lacking stipules; perianth segments inserted below carpels
Herbs with stipules, or shrubs; flowers various
Montane to alpine shrubs with aromatic leaves (peppery to the taste); sepals 2–4
Leaves not aromatic; herbs or shrubs; sepals 5
Perianth segments inserted below ovary (hypogynous); shrubs or twiners with showy, yellow, usually emarginate petals
Perianth segments inserted on short tube or rim extending above the ovary base (perigynous); herbs with stipules, or shrubs with entire, non-yellow petals
Small annual herbs or succulent perennials
Perennial shrubs or trees
Receptacle elongate, with numerous (usually more than 100) carpels; non-succulent herbs
Receptacle short, carpels 4 or 5; more or less succulent herbs
Leaves simple, sometimes shallowly toothed, under 10 cm long; shrubs or twiners with rather showy, yellow, bisexual flowers
Leaves pinnate, longer than 20 cm; trees with small, unisexual flowers
Flowers distinctly zygomorphic
Flowers actinomorphic or very nearly so
Stamens more than twice as many as petals, always more than 6, or both stamens and petals numerous
Stamens no more than twice as many as petals, or petals 2 and stamens 6
Stamens all united into a single tube or column, free part of filaments short to long
Stamens all free, or clustered into bundles
Leaves linear, with revolute margins; flowers unisexual, petals white, much exceeding sepals; ovary 3-locular
Leaves otherwise; flowers bisexual or if ever unisexual, then petals hardly exceeding sepals
Leaves bipinnate; flowers in short spikes; ovary 1-locular
Leaves not bipinnate; flowers solitary or in cymes; ovary 2-many-locular
[link through]
Plants aquatic, with long-petiolate leaves floating on or shortly emergent from water surface, suborbicular, more or less peltate; petals in several whorls
Plants terrestrial; leaves basally attached; petals in 1 (rarely 2) whorls

leads.lead_text: Sori forming continuous band; pinnae finely serrate or entire
Sori discrete; pinnae with strongly curved teeth
Fertile and sterile fronds similar; lamina extending well beyond sori; pinnae attached by broad bases and not markedly reduced in size towards base
Fertile and sterile fronds markedly different; lamina hardly extending beyond sori
Fronds undivided, strap-like, or with few irregular, long lobes
Fronds regularly pinnate, with numerous pinnae
Sterile fronds with some pinnae shortly stalked or narrowed at base almost to midrib; adjacent pinnae usually separated along rachis
Sterile fronds with all pinnae attached by wide bases; most adjacent pinnae close-set, or contiguous
Lower pinnae shortly stalked, the remainder sessile; rachis with numerous scales and hairs; sterile fronds normally forming flattened rosette, fertile fronds erect
Most pinnae shortly stalked (only few near apex sessile); rachis bare or with scattered scales; sterile fronds generally erect
Lower pinnae greatly reduced and widely separated; frond texture variable
Lower pinnae not markedly shorter than upper pinnae; fronds harsh
Sterile fronds with pinnae less than 1 cm long, straight, apices blunt; rhizome creeping; fertile frond longer than sterile one and pinnae shorter and curved; alpine
Sterile fronds with pinnae more than 1 cm long, straight or curved, apices acute or rounded; rhizome short, fronds tufted
Sterile fronds with lower pinnae not reduced in length; lowermost pair curved and slightly deflexed
Sterile fronds with lower pinnae reduced and rounded, not deflexed
Stipe pale to brown; pinnae of sterile fronds falcate, tips toothed; fertile fronds flaccid with narrow, wiry pinnae
Stipe shiny, black; pinnae of sterile fronds linear, tips entire; fertile fronds erect with coarse pinnae
Pinnae sessile, bases flanged, except for an isolated pair of shortly stalked pinnae at base (which may be absent in some specimens); stipe and rachis rough, with black scales
Pinnae in lower part of lamina shortly stalked or with basal margins approaching midvein at least on upper side, separate
Pinnae stalked in lower half of lamina; fertile fronds longer and more erect than sterile ones; most mature sori usually confluent, laterally and/or across midvein of pinna

Pinnae stalked for less than lower one-third of lamina (pinnae bases in middle region of lamina may be narrowed (more so on upper side) but not stalked); fertile fronds similar to sterile ones or else (when growing among rocks) longer and with pinnae more separated; mature sori usually discrete, rarely laterally confluent, but never confluent across midvein of pinna

Leaf-blades hollow and transversely septate (though the partitions sometimes difficult to see in fine-leaved species such as J.bulbosus); leaf-sheath margins produced at the apex into small auricles that meet towards the middle of the leaf in a sinus (or auricles absent in J. ensifolius)
Leaf-blades terete and pungent; inflorescence appearing lateral to an erect bract
Leaf-blades flat or channelled, not pungent; inflorescence appearing terminal
Mature capsules 4–6 mm long, about twice the length of the tepals, usually golden-brown coloured, slightly darker in the upper half; seeds 1.3–2 mm long, with conspicuous hyaline appendages

Mature capsules 2.5–3 mm long, slightly exceeding to slightly shorter than the tepals, usually dark reddish-brown to almost black (occasionally golden-brown); seeds 0.5–1 mm long, lacking appendages or with short inconspicuous appendages
Tufted non-rhizomatous annual; outer tepals twice as long as the capsule
Tufted or rhizomatous perennials (occasionally annual in J. planifolius); outer tepals slightly shorter to slightly longer than the capsule

Outer tepals (3.2–) 3.5–5.5 mm long, with a broad, minutely scabrous midrib; leaves grey-green, junction of blade and sheath often in an ± inconspicuous membranous lobe on one or both sides; plants with long, tough scaly rhizome
Outer tepals 1.5–3.5 (–4) mm long, with a smooth midrib; leaves green, junction of blade and sheath without lobes; plants with or without a rhizome

Dwarf alpine plant forming cushions or sparse mats with leaves to 3 cm long and 2 mm wide; inflorescences a solitary 1–5-flowered cluster on stems subequal to or exceeding the leaves by less than 2 cm

Tufted plants of lower altitudes with at least some leaves greater than 3 cm long or 2 mm wide; inflorescences usually consisting of more than one flower cluster, but if all reduced to a solitary cluster then at least some of the clusters with more than 5 flowers and/or on stems exceeding the leaves by more than 2 cm

Stamens 6; leaf-blades to 2.5 mm wide (when flattened), channelled (except for the tip); tepals 2.2–3.2 mm long; anthers subequal in length to filaments; primary inflorescence bract usually exceeding the flower cluster(s)

Stamens 3, very rarely 4–6; leaf-blades 1–11 mm wide, flat or channelled; tepals 1.5–2.5 mm long; anthers shorter than filaments; primary inflorescence bract usually shorter than the flower cluster(s)
Leaf-blades pluritubulose, with transverse septa extending across the width of the individual longitudinal tubes
Leaf-blades unitubulose with transverse septa extending across the whole width of the blade, and/or blades less than 1 mm wide and number of longitudinal tubes difficult to discern
Basal leaves with setaceous, usually bitubulose blades 0.3–0.6 mm wide; cauline leaves terete to slightly compressed, ± unitubulose, less than 1.5 mm wide
Leaf-blades strongly laterally compressed, 1.2–5.5 mm wide, with several longitudinal tubes
Leaf sheath margin without auricles; capsules 2.5–3.2 mm long, subequal to or slightly exceeding the tepals, with a subacute, shortly mucronate apex
Leaf sheath margin with distinct obtuse auricles; capsules 4–5 mm long, distinctly exceeding the tepals and tapering gradually to an acute-acuminate apex

Plants with a tuft of setaceous, inconspicuously bitubulose (microscopic examination often necessary) basal leaves 0.3–0.6 mm wide that are sometimes withered in old plants; plants ± bulbous at base, with or without very short rhizomes, often spreading vegetatively by layering of proliferous shoots that arise from nodes of the culm and from the inflorescence; capsules subequal to or slightly exceeding the tepals, with an obtuse shortly mucronate apex
Not combining the above characters
Stamens 3
Stamens 6
Capsules golden-brown to slightly reddish-brown; seeds 0.3–0.4 mm long; outer tepals 2.5–3.5 mm long; anthers shorter than or occasionally equal to filaments
Capsules dark red-brown at least in the upper half; seeds 0.4–0.6 mm long; outer tepals 3.1–4.5 mm long; anthers longer than or equal to filaments
Mature capsules dark brown, dark reddish-brown or almost black throughout or in the upper part; tepals usually strongly tinged red-brown
Mature capsules green, light brown or golden-brown throughout, without a strongly contrasting darker apex; tepals ± tinged red-brown (often only towards the apex)
Mature capsules equal to or distinctly exceeding the tepals, with an acute and mucronate or beaked apex; seeds 0.4–0.6 mm long
Mature capsules shorter than the outer tepals, with a broadly obtuse-truncate and mucronate apex; seeds 0.3–0.4 mm long
Capsule tapering rather abruptly to a beak 1–2 mm long; anthers 0.8–1.5 mm long
Capsule tapering gradually or rather abruptly to a distinct mucro not exceeding 0.8 mm long; anthers 0.5–0.9 mm long
Tepals 2–3 mm long; fruit clusters usually less than 8 mm diam
Tepals 3.1–4.5 mm long; fruit clusters mostly 8–10 mm diam

Inflorescence of many discrete clusters of flowers, each cluster clearly separated; inflorescence 5–20(–30) x 2–15 cm; flower-head peduncles 0.4 mm thick or thinner; tepals soft-textured, outer tepals longer than inner; capsule often obovate, subequal to inner tepals; seeds ellipsoid 0.4–0.5 mm long x c. 0.2 mm wide

Inflorescence of few to many clusters of flowers, at least some clusters not well separated; inflorescence 2–10 x 2–4 cm; flower-head peduncles 0.45 mm thick or thicker; tepals rigid, outer and inner subequal; capsule ± ovoid, shorter than tepals; seeds broadly ellipsoid 0.3–0.4 mm long x c. 0.2 mm wide

Leaves 0.3–1 (–1.5) mm wide, the transverse septa often inconspicuous; inflorescences with 1–5 flower clusters; culms to 14 cm long but often much shorter; higher altitudes or intermediate altitudes in cold-air basins
Leaves 0.5–4 mm wide, when less than 1 mm wide transverse septa conspicuous; inflorescences with up to 75 flower clusters; culms usually more than 14 cm long; various altitudes

Mature capsules (2.5–) 3–4.6 mm long, exceeding tepals by 1–2 mm, tapering gradually or slightly contracted below the acute-acuminate apex; tepals 1.8–3 mm long; flower clusters composed of up to 10 flowers
Mature capsules 2.3–2.5 mm long, exceeding tepals by less than 0.8 mm, contracted rather abruptly to an acuminate apex; tepals 1.8–2.3 mm long; flower clusters composed of up to 3 flowers
Rhizome long-creeping, stout (c. 2-5 mm diam.); outer tepals shorter than inner; tepals with long-acuminate apices reflexed at maturity

Rhizome absent,  or short and slender (< 2 mm diam.), plants usually tufted (or at times with stems submerged or buried in sand and rooting at proximal nodes in Juncus articulatus); tepals of  ±  equal length or outer ones longer; tepals with acute to obtuse or acuminate apices erect or only slightly reflexed
Capsule tapering rather abruptly to a beak 1–2 mm long; anthers 0.8–1.5 mm long
Capsule tapering gradually or rather abruptly to a distinct mucro not exceeding 0.8 mm long; anthers 0.5–1 mm long

Outer tepals 2–3 mm long; inner tepals ovate, obtuse to acute, equal to or shorter than the outer tepals; anthers equal to or longer than the filaments; fruiting clusters 5–9 mm wide; plants commonly forming swards or sometimes tufted

Outer tepals 3–4.5 mm long (rarely to 2.5 mm); inner tepals narrowly ovate, acute-acuminate, equal to or longer than the outer tepals; anthers shorter than the filaments; fruiting clusters 6–14 mm wide; plants tufted
Capsule exceeding the tepals by 1 mm or more at maturity, 3.5–6.7 mm long, gradually tapered to an acute apex
Capsule not exceeding the tepals or exceeding the tepals by less than 1 mm at maturity, 3–4.5 mm long, contracted rather abruptly or rarely tapered gradually to an acute apex

leads.lead_text: Inflorescence umbellate, with 3 or more stalked clusters (sometimes the stalks very short in putative hybrids involving L. novae-cambriae)
Inflorescence of a single cluster or of several close-spaced, sessile clusters, or with one or two stalked clusters

Leaves thin-textured, flat, usually with 3–5 longitudinal veins clearly visible on upper surface; fibrous leaf remnants lacking or persisting for about one year only; plants commonly bulbous; tepals and capsules pale to dark brown (mostly pale in alps); caruncle about one-third as long as seed; mostly lowland to montane sites

Leaves rather thick, channelled, with obscure venation; fibrous leaf remnants of several seasons usually persisting at base; plants not bulbous; tepals and capsules usually dark brown or blackish; caruncle about one-eighth as long as seed; alpine or subalpine, typically of exposed, rocky sites
Plants rhizomatous; alpine plants
Plants tufted; lowlands to alps
Leaves channelled, 1–2 mm wide; tepals and capsules dark brown or blackish; tepals with narrow margins
Leaves flattish, 3 mm wide or more; tepals and capsules pale to mid-brown (rarely deep reddish-brown), tepals with rather broad pale margins

Anthers 0.8–1.3 mm long; inflorescence often consisting of 2–4 sessile or subsessile clusters on stem up to c. twice as high as leaves; at least the young leaves acute-tipped, distinctly ciliate at base; fibrous leaf remnants of leaves often persisting as a thick basal stocking

Anthers about 0.5 mm long; inflorescence a single globose cluster on stem much more than twice as high as leaves; leaves glabrous or only sparsely ciliate near base; fibrous leaf remnants not persisting at base of plant
Leaves distinctly channelled, 1–2 mm wide
Leaves flat or slightly channelled, 2–7 mm wide
Anthers about 1 mm long; tepals with narrow margins
Anthers about 0.5 mm long; tepals with rather broad, pale margins
Inflorescence typically spherical to ovoid; leaves flaccid; caruncle of seed about one-third seed length; body of seed about 0.8 mm
Inflorescence typically oblong or conical in outline; leaves thickish; caruncle of seed minute, about one-eighth seed length; body of seed about 1.3 mm long

Leaves rather sparsely hairy along margin; plants rarely bulbous at base; tepals and capsules yellowish to mid-brown; inflorescence not infrequently reduced to a single cluster
Tepals c. 3 mm long; anthers c. 1 mm long; capsule subequal to tepals
Tepals 2–2.5 mm long; anthers 0.4–0.5 mm long; capsule often shortly exceeding tepals

leads.lead_text: Spikelets with several to many flowers producing nuts, usually only 1 to 2 lowest glumes empty
Spikelets or pseudospikelets with 1 to 2 flowers producing nuts, usually several to many empty glumes at the base of the spikelet or pseudospikelet
Culms noded and leafy; hypogynous bristles or scales present; robust perennials
Culms nodeless, leaves all basal (except occasionally in weak, branched, aquatic Isolepis species); hypogynous bristles or scales present or absent
Spikelets 1–2.5 cm long; inflorescence branches not scabrous; hypogynous bristles shorter than or equalling nut
Spikelets less than 1 cm long; inflorescence branches scabrous; hypogynous bristles much longer than nut
Style-base enlarged and persistent on nut; inflorescence not subtended by leafy bracts; leaves reduced to sheaths, glabrous; hypogynous bristles usually present
Style-base enlarged or not, but not persistent on nut
Hypogynous bristles present
Hypogynous bristles absent

Nuts smooth, epidermal cells isodiametric to narrowly oblong; rhizome elongate, creeping or ascending; glumes entire or minutely notched, or emarginate to bifid at the apex; hypogynous bristles present; culms solitary or a few-fascicled, nodeless above the base; perennial

Nuts smooth or transversely rugulose to sharply ridged, epidermal cells narrowly oblong to linear; rhizome very short and hidden among the culm-bases, or shortly lying, or elongate and creeping; glumes entire at the apex; hypogynous bristles present or absent; culms tufted or solitary, nodeless or 1(–3)-noded above the base; annual or perennial
Style based enlarged
Style based not enlarged
Style 2- fid
Style 3-fid
Glumes distichously arranged in spikelet
Glumes spirally arranged in spikelet (distichous in Isolepis levynsiana)
Involucral bracts glume-like or leaf-like, from shorter than inflorescence to twice as long as it (to 1.5 cm long); spikelets 2–8 mm long
Involucral bracts culm-like, usually at least 4 times as long as inflorescence (to 25 cm long); spikelets 5–15 mm long
Glumes distichously arranged in spikelet (spirally arranged in Cyperus hamulosus, and then plant curry-scented)
Glumes spirally arranged in spikelet (distichous in Isolepis levynsiana); plant not curry-scented
Nuts transversely wrinkled and/or stout perennials
Nuts variously marked but never transversely wrinkled; small annuals or perennials
Rhizomatous perennial with thick and woody rhizome to 1 cm diam.  (Ficinia nodosa) or small tufted annual (Ficinia marginata); nut with a small, sometimes deciduous, basal lobed disk
Tufted annual or perennials, rhizome absent or filiform; nut without a basal disk
Female flowers enclosed in sac-like utricle
Flowers not enclosed in a utricle

Inflorescence a sessile ovoid or hemispherical head of pseudospikelets; female flowers apparently terminal, always only 1 per pseudospikelet (floral unit) with 10–25 stamen-subtending or sterile glumes below it
Inflorescence not as above; female or bisexual flowers lateral and axillary, one to many in a spikelet, often with a few stamen-subtending or sterile glumes above or below them
A hypogynous disk or 1 or 2 hyaline scales or 2–6 hypogynous bristles or scales present at base of nut (not always falling with nut)
Hypogynous bristles, scales and disk absent
Nut more or less enclosed in 2, or occasionally 1, hyaline scales; small annual with inflorescence of 1–4 ovoid clustered heads with numerous spikelets
Nut without hyaline scales; inflorescence various
[link through]
Style simple or 2-fid
Style 3- to 8-fid
Style-base not differentiated or enlarged or persistent; leaves with a membranous ligule; dry forests or woodlands of the far east
Style-base differentiated, enlarged, and persistent; leaves without a ligule; damp sites in the north-east only
[link through]
[link through]
Hypogynous disk present at base of nut
Hypogynous bristles or scales present at base of nut
[link through]
Upper internodes of rachilla prominently zigzagged
Upper internodes of rachilla straight
Hypogynous scales 3, flat, antrorsely plumose below, apex with 1 long bristle-like lobe, often with 2 smaller flat lateral lobes; both aerial and basal spikelets produced
Hypogynous scales or bristles 2–6; if scales, flat but not plumose or 3-lobed; spikelets aerial only
[link through]
Style-base persistent, often enlarged in fruit
Style-base deciduous
Inflorescence head-like, globose, terminal on long, wiry culm, and plants forming large tussocks or inflorescence head-like, hemispherical to obovoid and plants < 40 cm high
Inflorescence panicle-like, umbel-like, or spike-like
Large tussock-forming perennial; culms often > 1 m long; ligule membranous and ciliate; inflorescence globose; hypogynous bristles 2 or 3, filiform, antrorsely scabrous
Small tufted perennial; culms 14–40 cm high; ligule absent; inflorescence condensed-compound and appearing head-like, hemispherical to obovoid; hypogynous bristles 6, plumose
[link through]
[link through]
Hypogynous bristles 6, as long as, or longer than the nut and falling with it
Hypogynous bristles 2–4, much shorter than the nut, not falling with it
[link through]
Inflorescence condensed-compound and appearing head-like, hemispherical to obovoid; hypygynous bristles flat and not inflated, plumose
Inflorescence panicle-like, umbel-like, spike-like or consisting of a single spikelet; hypygynous bristles or scales inflated (in Lepidosperma) or flat and not inflated, glabrous, scabrous or ciliate
[link through]
Glumes spirally arranged in the spikelet; hypogynous scales inflated
Glumes ± distichously arranged in the spikelet; hypogynous scales flat, not thickened
Hypogynous scales persistent on rachilla after nut falls; leaf with pseudopetiole; alpine, wet heaths and bogs
Hypogynous scales falling with the nut; leaf without pseudopetiole; lowland heaths and woodlands
[link through]
Style simple or 2-fid
Style 3- to 8-fid
Style-base enlarged, persistent
Style-base not enlarged or persistent
[link through]
Upper internodes of rachilla zigzagged
Upper internodes of rachilla straight
Annual; inflorescence of 1–4 ovoid clustered heads with numerous spikelets
Perennials; inflorescence panicle-like, spike-like, or occasionally reduced to a few clustered spikelets
[link through]
Leaves reduced to blades no more than 1 cm long
Leaves with well-developed blades to 1 m long or more
Persistent style-base not separated from body of nut by a constriction
Persistent style-base separated from body of nut by a constriction
Leaves without a ligule
Leaves with a ligule
[link through]
Leaves 2-ranked, flattened laterally (strictly isobilaterally)
Leaves 3-ranked, flattened dorsiventrally
Nut borne on inconspicuous hypogynous disk (disk may stay on rachilla rather than fall with nut)
Nut not borne on a hypogynous disk
[link through]
Spikelets disarticulating as a unit from axis at maturity
Spikelets persistent, nuts falling separately from glumes at maturity
Leaves with a ligule
Leaves without a ligule

Inflorescence narrow-ovoid to ovoid (rarely globose), with core not or scarcely raised, oblong to ovate; main involucral bract ± sheathing sides of inflorescence, red-dotted; culms usually minutely warty as well as longitudinally ridged
Glumes ciliate, sometimes minutely so, towards apex; leaves and involucral bract pluritubular
Glumes glabrous; culms, leaves and involucral bract unitubular (culms often pluritubular below)
Culms, leaves and involucral bract pluritubular, grey-green; nut minutely papillose when viewed with hand lens
Culms unitubular, yellow-green; leaves and involucral bract pluritubular, yellow-green; nut not minutely papillose when viewed with hand lens

leads.lead_text: Inflorescence head-like or consisting of only 1–5 spikelets in 1 or 2 small clusters
Inflorescence elongated, with spikelets clustered at several often distant nodes

Small, soft-textured leafy, tufted annuals, or small, mat-forming or decumbent perennials, or submerged aquatics; if erect, culms no more than 12 cm long; mouth of leaf-sheath and margins of glumes always glabrous
Erect perennials, ± rigid, shortly rhizomatous or tufted; culms mostly more than 12 cm high, if less then mouth of leaf-sheath and/or margins of glumes hairy
Fertile glumes 5–9 mm long
Fertile glumes less than 5 mm long
Submerged aquatic or occasionally small, tufted plant on margins of water; nut smooth or minutely reticulate
Dryland tufted or very shortly rhizomatous plants; nut not smooth
Inflorescence head-like; plants annual, forming small tufts; nut reticulate-pitted to trabeculate, glabrous
Inflorescence of 1–3 spikelets
Perennial, very shortly rhizomatous, forming low, deep-rooted tussocks or mats; nut transversely wrinkled, pubescent near apex
Annual, tufted; nut reticulate-pitted, glabrous
Tufted annuals
Small mat-forming or decumbent perennials
Hypogynous bristles absent or several, minute
Hypogynous bristles 5 or 6, from shorter than nut to slightly exceeding it (nut faces evenly trabeculate or reticulate)
Nut faces reticulate-pitted
Nut faces with 2 central columns of large pits and laterally smooth or minutely trabeculate
Anthers 1.0–3.2 mm long; nut reticulate-pitted to trabeculate; glumes red-brown to blackish
Anthers 0.5–0.8 mm long; nut coarsely and strongly reticulate; glumes straw-coloured to dark red-brown
Leaves much exceeding culms; culms erect, no more than 2.5 cm long; damp alpine and subalpine sites
Leaves shorter than culms; culms erect or decumbent, usually more than 3 cm long; plants of lowlands or margins of mountain streams, but never alpine
Anthers 0.8–1.0 mm long; hypogynous bristles 3–6, not plumose, shorter than nut; culms decumbent, leafy at nodes
Anthers 1.5–1.7 mm long; hypogynous bristles 6, plumose, about as long as nut; culms erect, nodeless
Inflorescence a single spikelet
Inflorescence a head-like cluster of spikelets (rarely a second smaller cluster in S. ericetorum)
Mouth of leaf-sheath ciliate or woolly
Mouth of leaf-sheath glabrous
Spikelet 8–22 mm long; fertile glumes 8–16 mm long; hypogynous bristles scale-like
Spikelet 3–5 mm long; fertile glumes 2.7–4 mm long; hypogynous bristles plumose
Involucral bracts at least twice as long as inflorescence, to 8 cm long
Involucral bracts less than twice as long as inflorescence (often shorter than it), to 2.5 cm long
Stamens 4–6; nut 1.9–2.5 mm long
Stamens 3; nut 1.3–1.5 mm long
Mouth of leaf-sheath long-ciliate; glumes 6–11, lowest 4–8 empty
Mouth of leaf-sheath glabrous or sparsely and minutely ciliolate; glumes 5–7,lowest 3–5 empty
Small, soft-textured leafy, tufted annuals, or small, mat-forming or decumbent perennials; if erect, culms no more than 10 cm long
Rigid, erect perennials (or S. apogon annual), shortly rhizomatous or tufted; culms mostly 10–125 cm high, if less then culms scabrous (S. moorei) or leaves very numerous and filiform (S. tesquorum)
Decumbent or loosely mat-forming slender perennial; nut surface faintly pitted or reticulate or smooth
Erect, tufted annuals; nut surface pitted, reticulate, or trabeculate
Anthers 0.5–0.7 mm long; nut faces with 2 central columns of large pits, laterally smooth or trabeculate
Anthers 1.0–3.7 mm long; nut faces evenly reticulate-pitted or trabeculate

Hypogynous bristles 5 or 6, setaceous, shorter than or equalling nut; inflorescence with a head-like cluster of 6–16 spikelets at uppermost node with 1–4 smaller clusters below; glumes red-brown to blackish
Hypogynous bristles absent or several, minute; inflorescence with 2–4 distant clusters of 1–5 spikelets; glumes straw-coloured to red-brown
Leaves obvious, leaf-blades well-developed, to 30 cm long
Leaves not obvious, leaf-blades to 3 cm long or reduced to small bracts on sheaths
Nut transversely wrinkled, hairy; culms scabrous; possibly not in Victoria, see note under genus description
Nut smooth or minutely pitted-reticulate or longitudinally striate and trabeculate, glabrous; culms smooth
Annual, leafy but without numerous filiform leaves at base; hypogynous bristles 5 or 6, shorter than to equalling nut
Perennial, with numerous filiform leaves at base of plant; hypogynous bristles several minute or absent
Mouth of leaf-sheath villous or woolly
Mouth of leaf-sheath glabrous
Leaf-sheaths very dark red-brown to black, minutely scabrous; glumes 7–11 per spikelet
Leaf-sheaths yellow-brown to red-brown, smooth; glumes 4–6 per spikelet
Glumes glabrous; nut smooth to faintly reticulate, white to grey
Glumes ciliate or woolly at least near apex; nut papillose or wrinkled, red-brown
Glumes 7–9 per spikelet; fertile glumes 7–10 mm long; nut wrinkled; mouth of leaf-sheath with margins not overlapping
Glumes 5 or 6 per spikelet; fertile glumes 5–7 mm long; nut papillose; mouth of leaf-sheath with margins overlapping

Culms terete, or compressed so as to be oval in cross-section or irregularly angular, sometimes grooved, or more or less biconvex with 1 flat acute margin and the other rounded to broad-acute (L. semiteres)
Rachis straight or scarcely curved
Rachis flexuose (usually strongly so)
Inflorescence blackish or very dark red-brown; fertile glumes 5–7 mm long; culms 20–60 cm high, 0.5–1 mm diam
Inflorescence pale red-brown to pale grey-brown; fertile glumes 7–11 mm long; culms 30–200 cm high, 0.7–2 mm diam

Hypogynous scales 3, plus 3 similarly swollen stamen filaments; leaf-sheaths very dark red-brown to dark grey-brown, straw-coloured above; fertile glumes scarcely longer than basal sterile glumes; nut 4–5 mm long
Hypogynous scales 5 or 6; stamen filaments not swollen; leaf-sheaths straw-coloured to reddish; fertile glumes to twice as long as sterile glumes; nut 2.8–4 mm long
Spikelets in dense clusters
Spikelets loosely arranged along spike-like branches of inflorescence
Culms subterete with 1 acute, flat margin, or irregularly angular, or biconvex with 1 acute margin and 1 rounded
Culms terete or slightly compressed but without acute margins
Leaf-sheaths blackish or very dark red-brown; spikelets appressed to rachis
Leaf-sheaths straw-coloured, reddish, or dark yellow-brown; spikelets more or less spreading from rach
Leaf-sheaths dark yellow-brown to dark grey-brown, occasionally dark reddish near apex; spikelets 5–7 mm long; fertile glumes 5–6 mm long
Leaf-sheaths straw-coloured to reddish; spikelets 6–10 mm long; fertile glumes 7–9 mm long
Culms rather spongy, compressible, strongly biconvex
Culms tough, not or scarcely compressible, flat to biconvex
Inflorescence with loosely arranged spikelets and/or small inflorescence with few spikelets
Inflorescence with densely clustered, numerous spikelets
Inflorescence with long, at least somewhat spreading, branches, 7–65 cm long
Inflorescence spike-like or with short branches more or less appressed to main axis, 0.8–8 cm long
Culms with margins scabrous, usually viscid, often ciliate
Culms with margins smooth or scabrous but not viscid or ciliate
Culms biconvex, or margins flat with central biconvex ridge, or strongly convex on 1 face and flat on the other, 70–180 cm high, 5–15 mm wide
Culms flat, or slightly convex on 1 face, or concavo-convex, 30–100 cm high, 2–8 mm wide
Rachis flexuose
Rachis straight or scarcely curved
Leaves exceeding inflorescences (to twice as long)
Leaves shorter than inflorescences
Spikelets mostly 3.5–4 mm long; culms usually biconvex
Spikelets mostly 5–8.5 mm long; culms usually flat or concavo-convex
Culms strongly biconvex in cross-section, with finely scabrous, extremely sharp and cutting margins; convined to swampy heathlands of the far east (near Genoa)
Culms flat, plano-convex, weakly biconvex or with a pronounced central biconvex ridge; margins smooth or scabrous but not extrememly sharp
Margins scabrous
Margins smooth
Culms with central biconvex ridge, 5–20 m wide; mostly confined to coastal dunes and headlands
Culms flat, plano-convex or concavo-convex, 3–7(–10) mm wide; mostly lowland heaths and woodlands

Nut (including hypogynous scales) >3 mm long, minutely hispid at apex; inflorescence dense or somewhat diffuse, but spikelets not usually aggregated in distinct clusters; bracts (other than main inflorescence bract) usually not obvious

Nut (including hypogynous scales) <3 mm long, glabrous throughout; inflorescence typically of distinct clusters, each usually with a prominent subtending bract (but these sometimes breaking off before maturity)

Leaf-blades terete or oval in cross-section (rarely somewhat angular or flattened at apex)
All leaves reduced to flattened mucros; culms 1–3-noded
Basal leaves well-developed (cauline leaves reduced if present); culms nodeless or 1-(rarely 2)-noded
Leaves square to rhomboid (occasionally narrowly so) in cross-section, faces concave or occasionally flat
Leaves flattened (at least near apex in B. rubiginosa) or narrow-rhomboid, faces flat or convex
Leaves scabrous, with raised'midrib'even if otherwise flat
Leaves smooth, without a raised 'midrib'
Spikelets 1-flowered; glumes 3 or 4; inflorescence 2–6 cm long (rarely to 14 cm), no more than 1 cm dia
Spikelets 2–5-flowered; glumes 4 or 5; inflorescence usually 15–40 cm long (occasionally as short as 7 cm), 1–2.5 cm dia
Nut straw-coloured to red-brown; culms nodeless; leaves flat throughout; spikelets ± few, spread out on long branches
Nut bright orange (paler red-brown when immature); culms 1–2-noded (rarely nodeless); leaves often terete near base; spikelets numerous, in dense discrete clusters
Leaves hollow, perfectly transversely septate
Leaves pith-filled, occasionally irregularly transversely septate
Spikelets few, not in dense clusters, 1-flowered; glumes 2–4 (mostly 3)
Spikelets numerous, often clustered, 1–4-flowered; glumes 4–6

Nut straw-coloured to whitish, with acute apex, triquetrous, 2.0–2.5 mm long, 1.0–1.3 mm diam.; spikelets spaced ± evenly along branches; leaf-blades and involucral bracts terete and obviously transversely septate when dry

Nut pale red-brown to bright orange at maturity, with obtuse apex, obscurely trigonous, 2.2–4.0 mm long, 1.2–2.0 mm diam.; spikelets usually in dense, discrete clusters on inflorescence branches; leaf-blades and involucral bracts flattened at least at apex, not appearing septate when dry

leads.lead_text: Ligule chartaceous or membranous, narrow, glabrous or fimbriate on upper margin (hairs 0.1 mm long or less)
Ligule long-ciliate or woolly
Lowest 7–12 glumes of spikelet much shorter than upper glumes (less than one-third length of spikelet), so that nut-bearing spikelet is pyriform or clavate
Glumes similar in length or 1–2 lowest or uppermost shorter than the rest;nut-bearing spikelet not pyriform or clavate
Stamen filaments to 8 mm long; nut 2.5–3.0 mm long, orange to red, with apex obtuse to broad-acute, umbonate
Stamen filaments to 20 mm long; nut 3.0–4.5 mm long, red-brown to dark brown, with apex acute
Mature spikelets yellow-brown or red-brown
Mature spikelets dark grey-brown to black
Culms to 45 cm high, 1–2 mm diam.; spikelets 2-flowered, with 6–9 glumes; leaves about as long as culms
Culms to 125 cm high, 2–5 mm diam.; spikelets 1-flowered (rarely 2-flowered in G. trifida), with 2–6 glumes; leaves longer than culms, often longer than inflorescences
Involucral bracts leaf-like, longer than inflorescence; culms 4–5 mm diam.; anthers 0.9–1.3 mm long (including apical appendage 0.2–0.3 mm long); chiefly rainforest areas of the far east

Involucral bracts not leaf-like, shorter than inflorescence; culms 2–4 mm diam.; anthers 1.8–2.3 mm long (including apical appendage 0.4–0.5 mm long); mostly near-coastal, usually in saline or brackish swamps, often fringing saltmarsh

Nut ± linear to very narrow-ovoid, triquetrous, 5.0–6.0 mm long, 1.0–1.5 mm diam., with surface very finely granulate, glistening; spikelets with 2–3 glumes; leaves and leafy bracts smooth to finely scabrous

Nut narrow-obovoid to narrow-ellipsoid, trigonous, 2.0–2.6 mm long, 0.8- 1.0 mm diam., with surface smooth and reticulate, shining; spikelets with 3–6 glumes; leaves and leafy bracts coarsely scabrous
Nut red to orange (yellowish when immature)
Nut straw-coloured to dark brown, grey or black
Nut 2.5–4.0 mm long; anthers 2.7–3.2 mm long (including apical appendage 0.3–0.5 mm long); culms 5–12 mm diam., hollow; forming big tussocks to 3 m high; widespread in lowlands, rare in montane areas
Nut 4.0–4.5 mm long; anthers 1.9–2.5 mm long (including appendage c. 0.2 mm long); culms 3–5 mm diam., solid; forming small tussocks to 125 cm high; montane swamps in east and rare
Culms to 45 cm high, 1–2 mm diam.; spikelets with all glumes subequal; basal leaves numerous; dry, often rocky areas
Culms to 70 cm high, 2.5–5 mm diam.; spikelets with uppermost 2–3 glumes much shorter than the lower 2–4; basal leaves rather few; chiefly inhabiting poorly drained sites
Leaf apex uncinate; base of plant dull; Grampians only
Leaf apex straight, pungent; base of plant ± shining; mallee areas

Leaves scabrous; glumes very long-mucronate, ± densely woolly on margins; stamens 4–7 (The 1964 specimen from near Dadwells Bridge is considered to have been mislabelled, and therefore the species is excluded from the Victorian flora.)
Leaves ± smooth; glumes acuminate to long-acute, glabrous; stamens 3

Style 2-fid; nut lenticular, biconvex, plano-or concavo-convex
Dwarf annuals, curry-scented (at least when dried)
Annuals or perennials but not curry-scented
Spikelets ± angular, with glumes arranged spirally; nut c. two-thirds as long as glume
Spikelets flattened, with glumes arranged distichously; nut from one-third to two-thirds as long as glume
Spikelets arranged spicately along the rachis of the ultimate branches of the inflorescence, in the form of very short to elongated spikes

Spikelets digitately or subdigitately clustered, in clusters sometimes dense on a much reduced rachis, sometimes very few in number or solitary and then often appearing lateral when the lowest bract is erect

Rachilla not winged or with very narrow wings
Spikelets fewer than 20 per spike
Spikelets usually more than 20 per spike, numerous to very numerous

Glumes remote (i.e. with glumes not or scarcely overlapping the glume immediately above on the same side of the rachilla); spikelets 1–1.5 mm diam., flattened to terete; rhizome, if present, not tuber-bearing

Glumes overlapping at least one-quarter of the length of the glume immediately above on the same side of the rachilla; spikelets more than 1.5 mm wide in side view, ± flattened; plants with tuber-bearing rhizomes

Culms terete below, trigonous near the apex; leaves rarely half as long as culms; lowest involucral bract erect, very much exceeding the inflorescence, usually pushing it to one side; nut when mature 2–3 times as long as broad; freely fruiting

Culms trigonous or triquetrous throughout their length; leaves mostly from one-half to three-quarters as long as culms; inflorescence symmetrical; nut either c. 1.5 times as long as broad or rarely maturing

Glumes yellow to dark golden brown, 3-nerved on each side; spikelets more or less parallel-sided and with obtuse apex, mostly 5–15 mm long; rachis of spikes mostly finely hispid; tubers globose to ovoid, with fine greyish tomentum at maturity; rhizomes yellow-brown

Glumes pale red-brown to orange-brown or very dark red-brown, 1–3-nerved on each side; spikelets tapering gradually to an acute apex, mostly 15–30 mm long; rachis of spikes glabrous or rarely finely hispid; tubers ± ellipsoid, without tomentum; rhizomes purplish to dark brown

Lowest 1 or 2 involucral bracts much exceeding inflorescence; spikelets 2.5–3 mm wide in side view when mature; glumes very pale red-brown to red- or orange-brown, rarely very dark, midrib straight in side view from immediately above the base to apex; nut c. 1.5 times as long as broad, broad-obovoid; nuts freely produced; fibrous coats of tubers often persisting into the second year

Lowest 2–4 involucral bracts shorter or not much longer than inflorescence; spikelets 1.5–2.5 mm wide when mature; glumes usually dark red-brown, midrib faintly curved and recurved in side view from base to apex; nuts rarely maturing (2–3 times as long as broad if present, narrow-obovoid to ellipsoid); fibrous coats of tubers soon disintegrating, not usually persisting beyond the first year
Glumes 1–1.5 mm long
Glumes 2–6.5 mm long
Leaves not septate-nodulose; tufted perennial, often apparently annual, often without any rhizome
Leaves and bracts septate-nodulose when dried; robust, tussock-forming perennials
Glumes 2–2.5 mm long
Glumes 4–6.5 mm long
Leaves and bracts thin, flat or with revolute margins; lowest involucral bracts spreading; tufted perennial, often apparently annual and without a rhizome
Leaves and bracts leathery, flat or folded, margins and midribs scabrous; perennials, either long-rhizomatous with culms solitary, or robust and tussock-forming
Glumes obtuse in side view but sometimes apparently acute because of the presence of a short mucro; glumes 1.5–2.5 mm long; robust, tussock-forming perennial
Glumes ± acute in side view; glumes 2.5–4 mm long; slender rhizomatous perennial with solitary culms
Elongated involucral bracts 6–22
Elongated involucral bracts 1–5
Leaves reduced to sheaths
Leaves with well-developed blades

Glumes remote (i.e. with glumes not or scarcely overlapping the glume immediately above on the same side of the rachilla); spikelets 1–1.5 mm diam., flattened to terete; rhizome, if present, not tuber-bearing

Glumes overlapping at least one-quarter of the length of the glume immediately above on the same side of the rachilla; spikelets more than 1.5 mm wide in side view, ± flattened; plants with tuber-bearing rhizomes

Culms terete below, trigonous near the apex; leaves rarely half as long as culms; lowest involucral bract erect, very much exceeding the inflorescence, usually pushing it to one side; nut when mature 2–3 times as long as broad; freely fruiting

Culms trigonous or triquetrous throughout their length; leaves mostly from one-half to three-quarters as long as culms; inflorescence symmetrical; nut either c. 1.5 times as long as broad or rarely maturing

Glumes yellow to dark golden brown, 3-nerved on each side; spikelets more or less parallel-sided and with obtuse apex, mostly 5–15 mm long; rachis of spikes mostly finely hispid; tubers globose to ovoid, with fine greyish tomentum at maturity; rhizomes yellow-brown

Glumes pale red-brown to orange-brown or very dark red-brown, 1–3-nerved on each side; spikelets tapering gradually to an acute apex, mostly 15–30 mm long; rachis of spikes glabrous or rarely finely hispid; tubers ± ellipsoid, without tomentum; rhizomes purplish to dark brown

Lowest 1 or 2 involucral bracts much exceeding inflorescence; spikelets 2.5–3 mm wide in side view when mature; glumes very pale red-brown to red- or orange-brown, rarely very dark, midrib straight in side view from immediately above the base to apex; nut c. 1.5 times as long as broad, broad-obovoid; nuts freely produced; fibrous coats of tubers often persisting into the second year

Lowest 2–4 involucral bracts shorter or not much longer than inflorescence; spikelets 1.5–2.5 mm wide when mature; glumes usually dark red-brown, midrib faintly curved and recurved in side view from base to apex; nuts rarely maturing (2–3 times as long as broad if present, narrow-obovoid to ellipsoid); fibrous coats of tubers soon disintegrating, not usually persisting beyond the first year
Leaves all or mostly reduced to sheaths
Leaves with well-developed blades

Involucral bracts 2–4, usually less than 5 cm long, very rigid and pungent with incurved margins; inflorescence head-like or with 1–3 short branches to 2 cm long, bearing globose clusters of spikelets

Involucral bracts mostly 5–8 in number, always more than 5 cm and up to 15 cm long, flat, firm-textured, not pungent; inflorescence simple to compound with 4–12 branches to 6 cm long, bearing hemispherical clusters of spikelets, or occasionally loosely head-like
Glumes less than 2 mm long (excluding any long mucro)
Glumes 2 mm long or more (excluding any long mucro)
Glumes with sides evenly red-brown to dark red-brown or blackish (keels mostly green)
Glumes uniformly green or with sides hyaline, white, pale brown, yellow or golden brown, occasionally with a red-brown patch (keels mostly green)
Rachilla winged
Rachilla not winged
Spikelets few (1–12) in the loose, ovoid to hemispherical clusters
Spikelets numerous in the dense globose clusters
Glumes 0.6–0.9 mm long
Glumes 1.5–2 mm long
Glumes with 1 nerve or no nerves on each side
Glumes with 2–5 nerves on each side
Involucral bracts 2–4, erect to spreading; inflorescence with 1–25 spikelets; small perennial or annual; spikelets 2.5–4 mm wide in side view; nut pale brown
Involucral bract 1, erect; inflorescence of 1–4 spikelets; dwarf annual
Glumes at maturity with sides uniformly yellow to red-brown
Glumes at maturity with sides uniformly green, whitish, pale brown, or with red-brown patches
Glumes with keel about as wide as sides and with cell outlines larger than on sides, 1-nerved only at edge of keel
Glumes with keel much narrower than sides and with cell outlines similar to those of sides, with 2–4 nerves on each side
Leaves and bracts strongly curly at least near apex
Leaves and bracts straight to slightly curved
Leaf-sheaths pale yellowish with red-brown blotches; nut colliculate to smooth
Leaf-sheaths pinkish to purple-red; nut tuberculate or colliculate

Glumes 3.5–4 mm long, 1- or 2-nerved  either side of the keel (rarely a 3rd weak nerve visible), the nerves occupying less than half the width of each side of the glume membranous margin wider than the

Glumes under 3 mm long, or if ever approaching 4 mm (C. lhotskyanus), then distinctly 2–4-nerved per side and the nerves occupying most of the width of each side of the more-or-less firm-textured glume
Prickles on leaf margins antrorsely aculeate, more or less regularly spaced
Prickles on leaf margins mixed aculeate to papillose, antrorse to erect or flabellate, more or less irregularly spaced
Anthers 0.3–1.2 mm long; tufted perennial; plants occasionally viscid
Anthers 1.3–2.0 mm long; rhizomatous perennial, with culms usually solitary along rhizome; plants never viscid
Spikelets less than 2.5 mm wide in side view
Spikelets 2.5–5 mm wide in side view
Inflorescence simple to compound, with 3–8 primary branches and numerous spikelets in dense clusters
Inflorescence a single cluster of 1–14 spikelets
Glumes with keel about as wide as sides and with cell outlines larger than on sides, nerved only at edge of keel; plants never viscid
Glumes with keel much narrower than sides and with cell outlines similar to those of sides, with 2–4 nerves on each side; plants occasionally viscid
Culms 25–50 cm long; leaves mostly septate-nodulose; leaf-sheaths pale yellowish or straw-coloured with occasional red-brown patches
Culms 3–25 cm long; leaves not septate-nodulose; leaf-sheaths pinkish to purple-red near base
Spikelets several- to numerous-flowered; rachilla continuous, persistent; glumes individually deciduous at maturity
Spikelets 1-flowered, but sometimes with a second imperfect flower above; whole spikelet falling as a unit at maturity
Inflorescence pseudolateral, sessile; lowest involucral bract erect, appearing as a continuation of the rush-like culm; probably not in Victoria, see note after genus description
Inflorescence obviously terminal, branched or head-like; involucral bracts not as above
Nut dorsally flattened with a flat or concave face against the rachilla; inflorescence densely head-like, subglobose, with 5–7 or more involucral bracts exceeding inflorescence
Nut laterally flattened, with one edge against the rachilla; inflorescence loosely head-like or branched, with 1–4 involucral bracts exceeding inflorescence
Glumes with straight to excurved mucro 0.3–0.7 mm long; glume spacing 0.5–0.8 mm
Glumes not or scarcely mucronate; glume spacing c. 1 mm
Glumes incurved dorsally in side view, dark red-brown to blackish, often with a hyaline patch on sides
Glumes ± straight dorsally in side view, yellow to very dark yellow-brown, occasionally red-brown but never with a hyaline patch
Spikelets spreading widely, in loose, shortly spicate to subdigitate clusters; rachilla not winged
Spikelets suberect, usually densely crowded in obconical subdigitate clusters; rachilla narrowly winged
Inflorescence ± ovoid, dense, solitary or with 2 smaller ones at the base; spikelets numerous, sometimes 100 in number, 1-flowered; keel of glumes usually toothed; stamen 1 (rarely 2 or 3)

Inflorescence globose, loose, always solitary; spikelets not usually more than 50, a second imperfect flower often present; keel of glumes usually smooth or nearly so, rarely toothed; stamens 3 (occasionally 2)

Spikelet terete or somewhat flattened; glumes spirally arranged

Style 3-fid (rarely 2-fid in I. trachysperma)
