leads.lead_text: Spikelets  12–16 mm long; glumes 9–12 mm long; lemma 7–11 mm long, lemma pointed at apex; tussock-forming rhizomatous grass of coastal sand dunes
Spikelets 2.5–13 mm long; glumes 2.5–4 mm long; lemma 1.5–5 mm long, obtuse, truncate, or emarginate, sometimes pointed (in Poa trivialis and sometimes in Poa pratensis); habit and habitat various
Annuals with soft, bright green leaves; ligule conspicuous, thinly membranous; lemma with prominent, hairy nerves; web absent
Perennials; ligule and web various
Inflorescence remaining narrow, often almost spike-like; spikelets mostly more than 5-flowered; lemma 9–11-nerved; native species of dry north-west and south-west coast
Inflorescence finally ovate or triangular, with spreading branches; spikelets mostly 5- or fewer-flowered; lemma 5-nerved; widespread weeds
Spikelets mostly pedicellate; lemma more than 2.5 mm long; anthers 0.7–1.3 mm long
Spikelets often sessile or subsessile; lemma less than 2.5 mm long; anthers 0.2–0.5 mm long
Plants bulbous at base or with distinctly bead-like lower internodes; ligule prominent, thinly membranous
Plants not bulbous at base, lower internodes not or barely swollen; ligule various
Spikelets plump, almost as broad as long, often pendent; web absent or rudimentary; panicle rather sparse, with very fine, spreading branches; uncommon native grass of north-west
Spikelets distinctly laterally compressed, longer than broad; web well-developed; panicle moderately dense and contracted; introduced species
Plants bulbous (onion-like) at base from enlarged, fleshy basal sheaths; inflorescence very compact, less than 6 cm long; spikelets 3–6-flowered; mostly dry regions (Murray Mallee and Wimmera)
Plants with swollen lower internodes; inflorescence loosely contracted, mostly more than 6 cm long; spikelets commonly 2 (rarely 3)-flowered; mostly cool, high-rainfall areas
Ligule conspicuous, 1 mm long or more, thinly membranous to papery, virtually or quite glabrous
Ligule inconspicuous, rarely exceeding 1 mm (occasionally to 1.5 mm in P. clelandii), firm, usually minutely pubescent on the back and at the apex
Rhizomatous grass with stiff, glaucous blades and purplish sheaths; lemma entirely glabrous; apparently only Lake Omeo near Benambra
Features not as above
Tufted or shortly stoloniferous species, rarely with a short, oblique rhizome; ligule obtuse to acute or jagged at apex
Rhizome well-developed; ligule obtuse, entire at apex

Plants usually developing short, leafy stolons from base; web well-developed; lemma hairy at least along keel, often distinctly incurved near apex; sheaths usually purplish; exotic grass from well-watered, lowland sites
Plants tufted; web absent; lemma subglabrous to glabrous, not incurved toward apex; sheaths pale; native grasses, typically of high-altitude, usually rocky sites
Leaves fine and inrolled-terete, less than 0.5 mm diam.; panicle pyramidal, spreading at maturity; spikelets 2–5 mm long
Leaves flat or folded, 2 mm wide or more; panicle narrow and contracted with rather few, plump spikelets, mostly more than 5 mm long
Web well-developed; lemma membranous toward apex; glumes unequal, scabrous along keel; widespread exotic grass
Web absent; lemma rather firm throughout; glumes subequal, smooth along keel; native grasses of the west and north
Leaf-blades flat, thin-textured, scabrous, to 4 mm wide; spikelets to 11 mm long; glumes slightly shorter than lower lemma; heavy, seasonally inundated soils in the north
Leaf-blades folded, rather thick, smooth, to 2 mm wide; spikelets to 8 mm long; glumes as long as or slightly exceeding lower lemma; saline lakes of volcanic plain
Lower part of culms and lower (abaxial) surface of leaf-blades scabrous-pubescent to softly pubescent
Lower part of culms and lower (abaxial) surface of leaf-blades smooth to scabrous, but not pubescent

Plants stoloniferous (young plants tufted), often developing leafy aerial stems; leaves narrow, flaccid, blade flat to angular-terete, mostly c. 0.5 (rarely to 1.5) mm wide, usually with c. 5, raised, smooth or scabrous nerves; culms weak and slender; web absent; principally of damp, shaded situations in the south
Plants tufted or rhizomatous; if ever developing leafy aerial stems, other features not as above
Leaf-sheath red, connate when young; ligule 0.8–2.6 mm long; lemma glabrous between nerves; restricted to the Brisbane Ranges, and Werribee and Lerderderg Gorges
Leaf-sheath usually not red or connate; ligule 0.3–1.5 mm long; lemma with at least some hairs between nerves
Leaf-blades flat, weakly or closely folded when fresh, the margins often becoming inrolled on drying
Leaf-blades narrow and inrolled-terete or inrolled-angular in section
Rhizomes developed; lower leaf-sheaths usually distinctly purplish
Rhizomes not developed under normal conditions (but, in response to disturbance or in rocky sites, short rhizomes may be produced); lower leaf-sheaths generally pale

Culms and sheaths of culm-leaves distinctly compressed; leaves smooth and glabrous, apex keeled, abruptly tapered and often slightly incurved; usually in damper lowlands, but ascending to subalps in the Grampians
Culms and sheaths terete or weakly compressed; leaves scabrous or minutely hairy at least on upper (inner) surface; typically of mountain forests, subalps or alps
Leaves distinctly scabrous, blade flat or weakly folded, upper surface scabrous but lacking hairs; web usually well-developed; mainly mountain forests

Leaves smooth to slightly scabrous, blade generally folded with upper (inner) surface bearing short, fine, sparse to moderately dense hairs; web weakly developed or absent; alps and subalps (var. hothamensis)
Lemma glabrous, web reduced or absent (var. labillardierei - a form of the volcanic plains)
Lemma hairy at least along keel in lower part, web various
Culm and sheaths of culm-leaves strongly compressed; web absent
Culm terete or slightly compressed; web developed
Leaves smooth or very minutely scabrous; panicle contracted; mallee or coastal sands
Leaves distinctly scabrous; panicle spreading at maturity; rarely truly coastal and not in mallee
Leaves normally less than one-half height of plant; spikelets usually dappled purple; lemmas relatively broad, truncate or emarginate at apex; uncommon grass of the north-west
Leaves normally more than one-half height of plant; spikelets normally green or straw-coloured; lemmas narrow, usually rounded at apex; coastal and estuarine foreshores (var. poiformis)
Leaf-blades 3–8 mm wide; lemmas more or less lanceolate in profile; mostly occurring by streams above c. 1000 m
Leaf-blades 1–3.5 mm wide; lemmas usually more or less oblong in profile; mostly on alluvial soils below c. 1500 m (var. labillardierei)
Blades rigid, often sharp-pointed
Blades flaccid to firm, but neither rigid nor sharp-pointed
Sheaths purplish; blades distinctly scabrous; web well-developed; lemma hairy along the midvein and margins near the base but internerves glabrous; rare grass of subalps (var. acris)
Plant not combining features as above
Inflorescence narrow and contracted at maturity; web copious, or if lacking, lemma glabrous or subglabrous; plants of lowlands
Inflorescence pyramidal, with spreading branches at maturity; web not or rarely well-developed, lemma pubescent in lower half or entirely glabrous; alpine or subalpine grasses
Web absent or reduced to a very few hairs; lemma glabrous (var. labillardierei - a form of the volcanic plains)
Web well-developed; lemma usually hairy

Entire plant rarely more than 25 cm high; leaves fine (to 0.5 mm diam); inflorescence often almost spike-like, to 4 cm long; rhizomatous or sometimes stoloniferous or tufted; coastal, mostly on calcareous sands or sands overlying basalt

Plant generally exceeding 25 cm in height; leaves relatively coarse (>0.5 mm diam.); inflorescence open to contracted, but hardly spike-like, longer than 4 cm; plants normally tufted (but branching from the lower nodes in P. poiformis var. ramifer)
Leaves normally less than one-half height of plant; spikelets usually dappled purple; lemmas relatively broad, truncate or emarginate at apex; uncommon grass of north-west
Leaves normally more than one-half height of plant; spikelets normally green or straw-coloured; lemmas narrow, usually rounded at apex; coastal and estuarine foreshores (var. poiformis)
Leaves bright green; sheath not or rarely purplish; moister sites, including bogs and creek margins
Leaves slightly to strongly glaucous; sheath commonly red or purplish; mostly of drier sites
Lemmas distinctly hairy on the internerves in the lower half; plants sometimes shortly stoloniferous
Lemmas virtually or quite glabrous on the internerves throughout
Blades smooth to the touch, often curved, very stiff and sharp-pointed
Blades distinctly scabrous, not particularly stiff
Lemmas hairy along keel and often lateral nerves; web present or absent; strictly tufted; blades usually more than 15 cm long; Mt Buffalo

Lemmas entirely glabrous, occasionally the web very weakly developed; usually shortly stoloniferous with several-branched, ascending stems; blades not more than 15 cm long; Macalister and Howqua River catchments
Lemmas virtually or quite glabrous on the internerves throughout, sometimes with some hairs along keel and lateral nerves
Lemmas distinctly hairy on the internerves in the lower half
Blades scabrous; sea-level to alps
Blades smooth to the touch; alpine or subalpine grasses
Blades usually somewhat firm, bluish; at least some sheaths purplish; plants sometimes shortly stoloniferous
Blades very soft, bright green to somewhat grey-green but not bluish; sheaths not purplish
Leaves green to grey-green but not bluish; plants always tufted; very common, widespread (var. sieberiana)
Leaves distinctly bluish; plants sometimes shortly stoloniferous; montane to alpine areas
Sheaths purplish; ligule very short and inconspicuous; tussock often relatively slender; higher alps
Sheaths pale; ligule occasionally to c. 1 mm long; lemma sometimes sub-glabrous; tussock usually densely leafy; montane areas, mostly in northeast (var. cyanophylla)
Web present (var. labillaridierei)
Web absent (occasionally a few weak hairs present)

Blades smooth, usually bluish; sheaths purplish; junction of blade and sheath not produced into a knob-like swelling; ligules prominently ciliate; usually shortly stoloniferous with several-branched, ascending stems; Macalister and Howqua River catchments

Blades somewhat scabrous, rarely bluish; sheaths pale (or purplish in P. meionectes); junction of blade and sheath commonly produced into a distinct knob-like swelling; ligules microscopically ciliate only; tufted plants; mostly East Gippsland
Glumes relatively broad; lemmas 3–4.5 mm long; leaves often somewhat firm, not shining, nerves usually inconspicuous; highlands
Glumes narrow (relative to lemmas); lemmas 2–3.5 mm long; leaves very fine, often shining, with raised nerves; lowlands
Blades inrolled, terete or angular in section when fresh; hairs of uniform length
Blades flat to closely folded when fresh; hairs often of different lengths
Plants producing aerial stolons; blades very fine and thin-textured between the prominent nerves, angular in section
Plants tufted, rarely shortly rhizomatous; blades fine or rather coarse but firm-textured, terete or biconvex in section
Blades densely covered with soft, spreading hairs, often appearing whitish; sheaths purplish; rocky areas at high-altitude
Blades sparsely to densely pubescent, usually also somewhat scabrous, not or very rarely appearing whitish; sheath pale; lowlands or lower mountains
Hairs even, dense and spreading from surface
Hairs scattered, acutely inclined to surface or occasionally weakly spreading
Culms weak, usually lacking nodes between basal leaves and inflorescence, soon lain flat by wind; lemma glabrous between nerves; margins of salt lakes in south-west

Culms rarely, if ever, lacking nodes between basal leaves and inflorescence, remaining erect; lemma pubescent to some degree between nerves; widespread grasses, usually of dry forests, woodlands or grasslands (var. hirtella)
Plants distinctly rhizomatous; sheaths purplish; upper leaf surface sparsely pubescent with scattered fine hairs; montane forests (var. parviflora)
Plants tufted, rarely shortly rhizomatous; sheaths usually pale; upper leaf surface densely pubescent; mostly lowlands

leads.lead_text: Plants glandular, the glands appearing as raised pits along leaf-sheaths and margins of blades and yellowish bands or patches closely below the nodes on the culms
Plants lacking raised pits along leaf-sheaths and margins of blades (but sometimes, in E. leptostachya, with yellowish glandular bands below nodes)
Spikelets 2–4 mm wide
Spikelets less than 2 mm wide
Lemmas leaden grey-green, 1–1.5 mm long, lateral veins very indistinct; anthers c. 1 mm long; panicle axis and branches devoid of glands
Lemmas green or often purplish, 1.5–2 mm long, lateral veins distinct; anthers c. 0.3 mm long; panicle axis and/or branches with glands (often sparse)
Not as above
Erect, wiry, tufted, mallee grass to 60 cm high, with rigid, narrowly inrolled leaf-blades; base of plant somewhat thickened or knotty, and woolly; spikelets laterally compressed
Spikelets terete or strongly biconvex, the two rows of florets overlapping at their bases, remaining so at maturity, not separated by a central groove; grasses predominantly of the mallee
Spikelets laterally compressed, the two rows of florets often separated by a central groove or channel, becoming loose at maturity

Spikelets sessile or subsessile (pedicels, except those of terminal spikelets, less than 0.5 mm long), commonly clustered and curved to one side, green and/or pinkish; glumes and lemmas persistent; lemma with prominently thickened nerves, the lateral one midway between midrib and margin; culms often procumbent or only weakly ascending

Spikelets distinctly pedicellate, not or barely curved, usually dark purple at least initially; glumes and lemmas soon deciduous; lemma nerves not prominently thickened and the lateral nerves nearer to margin than midrib
Spikelets shining; lemmas acute to obtuse, the lowest lemma of spikelet to 1.4 mm long; anthers minute, almost circular, to 0.2 mm long
Spikelets dull; lemmas very broadly obtuse, truncate or broadly emarginate, the lowest lemma of spikelet 1.5 mm long or more; anthers c. linear, 0.4 mm long or more
Largest spikelets clearly more than 2 mm long and 1 mm wide
Spikelets to 2 mm long and 1 mm wide; panicle delicate, rather narrow but with spreading capillary branches
Lateral nerves on lemma conspicuous, ridged, approaching or reaching the margin
Lateral nerves indistinct, not or barely forming a ridge and usually not reaching beyond halfway to the margin
Pedicels without a yellow band below spikelet
Pedicels each with a yellowish band shortly below spikelet
Perennials; glumes persisting until all or most of the firm lemmas have fallen
Weedy annual; glumes falling before the membranous lemmas
Anthers 3; grain 0.7–0.8 mm long; inflorescence with branches finally spreading, the spikelets spaced along the branches
Anthers 2; grain 0.5 mm long; inflorescence remaining narrow and spike-like (but usually interrupted), the spikelets produced in close clusters
Rhizomatous and/or stoloniferous perennials, leaves mostly cauline; culms usually branched, wiry or cane-like; grasses of shallow lakes and overflows in the west and north of the State
Tufted annuals or perennials, leafy at base; culms rarely branched below inflorescence

Culms cane-like, to 5 mm diam., much-branched, but not producing stolons, usually prominently waxy at least along younger parts; lemma thinly membranous and obtuse or erose at apex; rare grass of far north-west

Culms wiry, to c. 3 mm diam., generally not much-branched, occasionally producing aerial stolons, not waxy; lemma membranous, more or less acute and entire at apex; occasional grass of heavy clay soils
Grain neither deep red nor ornamented; spikelets usually with more than 5 florets
Grain deep red, ornamented by a raised, honeycomb-pattern; spikelets rarely with more than 5 florets
Lemmas finely scabrous between dorsal and lateral nerve as well as the nerves themselves; grain slender, c. 1 mm long; annual; dubiously Victorian, known from a single 1898 Grampians specimen
Lemmas smooth, or scaberulous along dorsal nerve only; if grain ever slender and 1 mm long, then plants perennial
Neither basal sheaths hairy nor leaf tips very fine and curled; grain c. 0.5–0.7 mm long; annuals or perennials
Sheaths of lower leaves hairy at base; leaf tips usually very fine and curly; grain c. 1 mm long; perennials
Pedicels without a yellow band below spikelet
Pedicels each with a yellow band shortly below spikelet

Lowest panicle branches glabrous in axils or if with a few hairs, these much less than 4 mm long; lower glume more than 0.7 mm long; grain concave dorsally; plants annual or perennial, usually more than 50 cm high

Lowest branch(es) of panicle with a sparse tuft of fine hairs c. 4 mm long in axil (rarely the axils glabrous); lower glume less than 0.7 mm long; grain convex dorsally; plants annual, usually less than 50 cm high

leads.lead_text: Inflorescence of 1 to several spikes; rigid, strongly rhizomatous, usually semi-aquatic grasses of tidal mud-flats
Inflorescence a raceme or panicle (sometimes very contracted and appearing spike-like but spikelets at least shortly pedicellate); tufted or rhizomatous, terrestrial grasses

Spikelets (15–)16.5–25 mm long; anthers 7–13 mm long, usually fully exserted at maturity and distinctly dehiscing; pollen fertile; ligules 1–3 mm long; upper glumes 3–6-veined, 13–22 mm long; seeds produced; leaf blades often forming an angle of >45 degrees to culm

Spikelets 14–17.5 mm long; anthers 5–7(–8.5) mm long, not or incompletely exserted at maturity, indehiscent; pollen sterile; ligules 1–1.5 mm long; upper glumes 3-veined; seeds not produced; leaf blades generally forming an angle <45 degrees to culm
Inflorescence widely spreading with lowest branches whorled
Inflorescence narrow, with lowest branches solitary or paired
Upper glume more or less equal to spikelet
Upper glume usually about half (but up to two-thirds) as long as spikelet
Tufted or stoloniferous grass of north and north-west; leaves not distichous, sheath shorter than internodes; spikelets membranous, dull
Rhizomatous grass of near-coastal (and occasionally inland) saline environments; leaves distichous, sheath mostly longer than internodes; spikelets firm, shining
Inflorescence interrupted throughout, the spikelet-bearing branches mostly 1–3 cm long, the rachis clearly visible between the branches; spikelets mostly c. 1.5 mm long
Inflorescence continuous throughout (except sometimes at very base), the spikelet-bearing branches mostly less than 1 cm long and completely obscuring the rachis; spikelets c. 2 mm long
Spikelets 2–2.5 mm long; lowest branches of inflorescence appressed to main axis; widespread weed of southern Victoria
Spikelets 1.6–2 mm long; lowest branches of inflorescence sometimes spreading slightly from main axis; dubiously recorded from Horsham only

Lemma of lower (fertile) floret very obtuse to truncate, without a distinct tuft of cilia on the upper margin; spikes widely spreading in flower
Awn of spikelet about as long as spikelet or shorter
Awn of spikelet at least twice as long as spikelet
Lower floret subequal to upper glume, not strongly embracing the upper floret; widespread grass, particularly on basalt plains
Lower floret distinctly longer than upper glume, its lemma wrapping around the upper floret and almost entirely enclosing it; very rare grass of north-east and far east

Spikes 2–4, mostly less than 3 cm long; spikelets 2.5–3 mm long; lemma with dense, ± appressed, silky hairs along the keel; leaves with scattered, spreading, tubercle-based hairs in the lower half; rare, in the north-west only

leads.lead_text: Spikelet 6–8 mm long; glumes and sterile lemma woolly; panicle contracted; robust rhizomatous perennial
Spikelet less than 6 mm long; glumes and sterile lemma glabrous; annuals or perennials
Lower floret staminate
Lower floret neuter
Lower glume widely obtuse or truncate (sometimes with a short central point), distinctly less than half as long as spikelet
Lower glume acutish to acuminate, c. half as long to distinctly more than half as long as spikelet
Upper glume and lower lemma conspicuously 9–11-nerved
Upper glume and lower lemma up to 7-(rarely 9)-nerved, nerves usually inconspicuous
Panicle small, few-branched, usually c. 4–10 cm long; rare, East Gippsland only
Panicle (usually much) more than 10 cm long, with many capillary branches; widespread grasses

Palea of sterile floret present (c. half to three-quarters as long as its lemma); lower and upper glume shortly separated by development of rachilla; fertile lemma smooth or minutely roughened; annuals or perennials
Palea absent from sterile floret or much reduced (less than one-quarter as long as its lemma); rachilla not apparent between lower and upper glume; fertile lemma quite smooth; annuals
Plants perennial; leaves glabrous to moderately hairy with rather stiff hairs; callus of fertile lemma entirely basal, less than 0.5 mm wide
Plants annual; leaves with numerous, fine, spreading, tubercle-based hairs; callus of fertile lemma crescentic, extending upwards from base, more than 0.5 mm wide
Spikelet to 3.3 mm long
Spikelet 3.5–5 mm long
Leaves glabrous, margins flat; panicle soon exserted from upper sheath; internodes hollow; stoloniferous plants

Leaf-sheaths (and often blades) with spreading, tubercle-based hairs, margins often finely undulate; panicle enclosed within upper sheath until maturity; internodes of culm solid or pithy; tufted plants
Palea of lower floret absent or vestigial; nodes of culm hairy; decumbent perennial of wet areas
Palea of lower floret fully developed (c. two-thirds to three-quarters as long as its lemma); nodes of culm glabrous

Branches of inflorescence stiff, finally widely spreading from primary branches, mostly whorled at lowest node; rachilla apparent between upper and lower glume; robust native perennial, forming leafy, erect, blue-green tussocks

Branches of inflorescence pliant, remaining appressed to primary branches (rarely somewhat spreading, but still inclined to axes), mostly solitary at lowest node; rachilla apparent or not between the glumes; cataphylls present or absent; tussocks rather slender or loose, with spreading to ascending culms
Upper glume 7-(rarely indistinctly 9-)nerved; sheaths not or rarely purplish; cupular summit of pedicel not angular; uncommon native grass of the Murray floodplain between Albury and Swan Hill
Upper glume 9–11-nerved; sheaths often purplish; cupular summit of pedicel angular; widespread weedy grass
Plants annual; cataphylls absent; leaf margins smooth; currently known only from Harcourt area
Plants perenial; cataphylls present; leaf margins scabrous; collected from the vicinity of the Murray and lower Goulburn Rivers

leads.lead_text: Spikelets loose to crowded, but not distinctly ranked, hardly gaping at maturity; leaf-blades usually under 12 mm wide
Spikelets crowded, distinctly ranked in 4–6 rows along dense, compact panicle branches, very turgid and gaping at maturity; leaf-blades wider than 1 cm (often 2 cm or more)
Primary branches of inflorescence with bristles subtending all or most of the spikelets; spikelets longer than 3 mm; leaf-blades not regularly red-banded
Primary branches of inflorescence lacking bristles, or sometimes a few present toward base, not subtending spikelets; spikelets less than 3 mm long; leaf-blades typically red-banded
Inflorescence drooping with flexuous branches; at least some branches of inflorescence with secondary branching (usually toward base of inflorescence)
Inflorescences upright with straight branches; the branches without secondary branching
Panicle usually fully exserted from upper leaf-sheath at maturity; fertile lemma tapered abruptly to a short (less than 0.5 mm), membranous, often recurved or distorted apical point
Base of panicle usually remaining enclosed by upper leaf-sheath; fertile lemma tapered evenly to a firm (but not hardened) apical point
Spikelets 3.2–4.5 mm long; fertile lemma and palea pale to mid-brown at maturity
Spikelets 2.5–3.1 mm long; fertile lemma and palea white to pale yellow or greenish, not brown at maturity

leads.lead_text: Glume glabrous along and near margins (a rudimentary lower glume may be present); inflorescence usually with two branches arising close together, rarely a solitary branch below the terminal pair
Glume ciliate on margins (lower glume lacking); inflorescences with 3-many branches arising at different levels along axis
(Upper) glume surface hairy; veins of leaves minutely scabrous on upper surface
(Upper) glume entirely glabrous; veins of leaves smooth or papillate on upper surface
(Upper) glume and lower lemma membranous; cauline leaves abundant, distinctly distichous, veins papillate on upper surface; saline coastal or estuarine areas
(Upper) glume and lower lemma firm; cauline leaves few, not distinctly distichous, veins smooth on upper surface; non-saline sites away from the coast
Fertile lemma distinctly shorter than glume and sterile lemma
Fertile lemma as long as or subequal to glume and sterile lemma
Spikelets more than 2.8 long and 1.7 mm wide; inflorescence of 3–10 racemes
Spikelets smaller than 2.8 long and 1.6 mm wide; inflorescence of 12–20 racemes
Glume hairy dorsally and near margins; axes of racemes not winged
Glume glabrous dorsally (but silky-hairy near margins); axis of racemes distinctly winged

Bristles retrorsely scabrous
Lemma of upper floret smooth or granular but not boldly ridged, quite blunt
Lemma of upper floret boldly transversely ridged, tapered to a minute apical point
Panicle thicker than 1 cm (not including bristles), with branches of panicle developed, mostly 10–20 mm long; fertile floret separating from remainder of spikelet at maturity
Panicle thinner than 1 cm (bristles excluded), with branches not or hardly developed; spikelet falling entire at maturity
Perennial; leaves firm, mostly narrower than 4 mm; bristles generally about as long as spikelets
Annual; leaves flaccid, mostly wider than 5 mm; bristles generally considerably longer than spikelets

leads.lead_text: Fertile lemma with membranous margins, of distinctly thinner texture than lemma body, laying flat over palea and obscuring c. one-third of it or more; spikelets neatly and distichously arranged; racemes often longer than the axis internode and hence overlapping the base of the raceme above; locally abundant in flood-prone areas along Murray River and major tributaries downsream from Wodonga area

Fertile lemma with recurved margin, as thick-textured as body of lemma, exposing most of the palea beneath; spikelets generally not neatly and distichously arranged (except perhaps P. aversum); racemes shorter than the axis internode and not overlapping the base of the raceme above
Sterile lemma with palea c. half as long as lemma
Sterile lemma without a palea, or palea vestigial, less than one-quarter as long as lemma
Lower lemma rather thick-textured, opaque, veins inconspicuous; axis of inflorescence narrowly but distinctly winged
Lower lemma membranous, whitish-translucent except for distinct veins; axis of inflorescence not or barely winged
Lower glume shortly scabrous-pubescent; north-central to north-west Victoria, Werribee area and rain-shadowed upper Snowy River area in the east
Lower glume smooth and glabrous; only rain-shadowed upper Snowy River area in the east

Spikelets glabrous to shortly pubescent; panicle branches not stiff; annuals (or short-lived perennials) of disturbed or irrigated areas
Lower panicle branches whorled, devoid of spikelets in the lower 2 cm or more, widely spreading at maturity
Panicle branches not whorled, bearing spikelets virtually to base, remaining suberect at maturity
Spikelets 2–3 mm long; leaf margins strongly crimped
Spikelets 3–4.5 mm long; leaf margins plane or weakly undulate
Spikelets less than 2.5 mm long
Spikelets 2.6–3.7 mm long
Inflorescence not digitate, branches spaced along main axis; spikelets bearing short acute hairs (often obscure); native perennial
Inflorescence digitate or subdigitate; spikelets with club-shaped hairs; weedy annual
Inflorescence digitate, generally with 4–10 racemes; upper glume up to half as long as the  spikelet; common and widespread summer to early autumn-active weed
Inflorescence of 2 or 3 racemes (rarely more); upper glume as long as the spikelet; currently known from Mallacoota area only.

Inflorescence a panicle with spreading branches; spikelets mostly 4–7 mm long, detaching from panicle immediately below glumes; swamps and lagoons of northern part of State

Inflorescence reduced to one or a few spikelets, remaining enclosed within the uppermost leaf-sheaths; bristles of involucre shorter than spikelets; vigorous weed or lawn-grass, spreading extensively by rhizomes and stolons
Bristles of involucre scabrous
At least the inner bristles of involucre plumose
Bristles of involucre 20–35 mm long, purplish; spikelets separating from main axis with panicle branch (2–4 mm long) attached; main axis hairy
Bristles of involucre 10–15 mm long, straw-coloured; spikelet separating from main axis immediately below involucre; main axis smooth or scabrous
Inflorescence 8–30 cm long; bristles purplish; lemma of lower (sterile) floret 3-nerved, palea of lower floret lacking; robust, strongly tussock-forming

Inflorescence 3–10 cm long; bristles white or yellowish (rarely purplish); lemma of lower (staminate or sterile) floret 7–9-nerved, palea of lower floret fully developed; long-rhizomatous or weakly tussock-forming

Petal margins decurved, green to light brown, labellum tapered in distal half but not linear-filiform, apex acute to subacute
Sinus V-shaped when viewed from the front
Sinus flat or raised when viewed from the front, often with a central notch
Labellum not protruding from the sinus in the set position, apex obtuse, truncate or slightly notched
Labellum protruding from the sinus in the set position, apex long-acuminate
Flower about 1–1.5 cm long; Leptospermum lanigerum thickets
Flower 2 cm or more long; habitat not as below
Flower 2–3 cm long, galea with a short curve, labellum 12–17 mm long
Flower 4.5–7 cm long, galea with a long, sweeping shallow curve, labellum 18–24 mm long
Sinus abruptly protruding and platform-like when viewed from the side
Sinus flat or shallowly mounded or curved when viewed from the side, never platform-like
Distal third of labellum protruding from the sinus in the set position
Labellum tip just visible through the sinus in the set position
Flower bluish-green and white, strongly inflated at the base, labellum 15–19 mm long
Flower green and white with red-brown suffusions in the galea, not strongly inflated at base, labellum 11–13 mm long
Dorsal sepal with a short filiform point only slightly exceeding the petals; sinus of lateral sepals v-notched when viewed from the front; petals green; mostly coastal scrubs
Dorsal sepal with a filiform point significantly exceeding the petals; sinus of lateral sepals not v-notched when viewed from the front; petals red-brown; widespread, usually inland
Flower 3 cm or more long
Flower 1.5–2.5 cm long
Sinus scabrid, labellum protruding prominently from the sinus in the set position; East Gippsland
Sinus smooth, labellum tip just visible in the set position; western Victoria
Labellum tip just visible in the set position
Labellum protruding prominently from the sinus in the set position
Flower erect, free points of lateral sepals erect
Flower semi-nodding, free points of lateral sepals recurved or lax
Labellum tip visible through the sinus in the set position
Labellum tip not visible through the sinus in the set position
Dorsal sepal not scabrous
Dorsal sepal scabrous
Scape narrowest at the base, widening upwards; ovaries long and swollen; flowers entirely green and white; flowers appearing in spring and summer; swampy habitats
Scape of equal width throughout; ovaries short and not swollen; flowers entirely green and white or with brownish petals; flowers appearing in autumn and winter; dry habitats
Sinus v-shaped when viewed from the front
Sinus flat with a small median notch when viewed from the front
Plants bearing up to 20 flowers; flowers angular and narrow, appearing in summer
Plants bearing up to 12 flowers; flowers rounded and plump, appearing in autumn and winter; southern Victoria
Rosette leaves pale green, to 6 mm long and 7 mm wide; flowers green and white with a reddish brown apex; tip of dorsal sepal and petals sparsely scabrous; south-west Victoria
Rosette leaves bluish green, to 25 mm long and 18 mm wide; flowers green, white and dark brown; most of the dorsal sepal and petals densely scabrous; northern Victoria
Labellum lamina filiform with an apical knob and numerous long yellow hairs
Labellum lamina flat, lacking an apical knob and yellow hairs
Stem leaves poorly developed and tightly sheathing the peduncle, rosette leaves encircling the base of the scape, sometimes withered at flowering
Stem leaves well-developed and spreading, rosette leaves only developed on non-flowering plants
Connate part of lateral sepals wider than galea; labellum with a tail-like basal appendage; flowers predominantly reddish
Connate part of lateral sepals about as wide as galea; labellum with a basal mound and lacking a basal appendage; flowers predominantly green
Petals each with a prominent basal flange which block off the base of the galea, labellum emerald green or dark reddish-brown
Petals each with a poorly developed basal flange which do not meet and block off the base of the galea, labellum yellowish or wholly brown often with a dark brown to blackish central stripe
Galea 11–16 mm long; labellum 5.5–7 mm long; synsepalum broad-oblong–elliptic; north-west Victoria in mallee habitats and dry woodlands near Ararat
Galea 15–22 mm long; labellum 6–8 mm long; synsepalum oblong or narrow elliptic; habitats various, but not found in mallee
Labellum and tips of sepals deep reddish-brown
Labellum and tips of sepals green
Galea 15–18 mm long, pale translucent green with dark green lines; synsepalum narrow oblong
Galea 17–22 mm long, dark green with darker lines; synsepalum narrow elliptic
Synsepalum ovate; petals without basal flanges, the anterior margin broadly curved; eastern Victoria between Benambra and Wulgulmerang
Synsepalum elliptic; petals with small basal flanges, the anterior margin straight or shallowly curved
Labellum appearing hairy with transparent acicular hairs over most of its surface; known only from the Grampians
Transparent acicular hairs mostly confined to the labellum base or absent
Labellum wholly brown or blackish, central stripe inconspicuous; near-coastal, often granite areas of eastern Victoria
Labellum cream to pale yellow (rarely light brown) with a conspicuous blackish central stripe
Labellum with numerous acicular hairs at the base
Labellum with few acicular hairs at the base
Flowers dark green with bright orange-brown tips on the sepals; north-east Victoria
Flowers pale green with light-brown tips on the sepals; widespread
Labellum 5–6 mm long, widest towards the apex, light brown with a dark central stripe; north-east Victoria
Labellum 4–5 mm long, of equal width throughout, yellowish with a black central stripe; western Victoria between Ballarat and the Grampians
Labellum lamina glabrous, thin and membranous, with a well-developed basal appendage
Labellum lamina bearing hairs, not membranous, often fleshy, covered with transparent siliceous cells, basal appendage poorly developed or absent (except in P. woollsii)
Labellum appendage erect, central ridge produced into a beak-like structure
Labellum appendage recurved, central ridge not produced into a beak-like structure
Plants often robust, to 30 cm tall; flowers heavily striped bluish-green and white; alpine and subalpine meadows of eastern Victoria
Plants more slender, usually less than 15 cm tall; flowers mostly bright green, not heavily striped; not found in alpine or subalpine environments
Galea 6–8 mm long; flowers crowded and overlapping; rosette leaves 3–8 mm wide; extremely rare in stony rise grasslands of western Victoria
Galea 7–9 mm long; flowers uncrowded, not usually overlapping; rosette leaves 8–15 mm wide; widespread, but not usually in stony rise grasslands
Labellum basal appendage green, apex obtuse
Labellum basal appendage dark blackish green, apex truncate to emarginate
Flowers crowded and overlapping; scape 7–16 cm tall; extremely rare in stony rise grasslands of western Victoria
Flowers uncrowded, not usually overlapping; scape 15–35 cm tall; widespread, but not usually in stony rise grasslands
Plants often robust, to 30 cm tall; flowers widely spaced, not overlapping; woodlands and grassland
Plants usually shorter, to 16 cm tall; flowers crowded and overlapping; grasslands
Scape 3–4 mm thick; extremely rare (possibly extinct) species from near Sale
Scape 1–3 mm thick
Labellum lamina oblong to obovate; central ridge of labellum appendage thin and not raised above the marginal ridges; basalt plains grassland north and west of Melbourne
Labellum lamina elliptical; central ridge of labellum appendage thick and raised above the marginal ridges; montane grassland and herbfield of East Gippsland
Dorsal sepal with a filiform point 3 mm or more long; labellum ovate, ovate-oblong or obovate, 4–7 mm long
Dorsal sepal with a filiform point 3 mm long or less; labellum oblong, to c. 4 mm long
Basal lobe of the labellum c. 3 mm long, filamentous tips of lateral sepals c. 10 cm or more long
Basal lobe of the labellum to c. 1 mm long, filamentous tips of lateral sepals less than 4 cm long
Labellum fleshy, with or without two (rarely 4) prominent basal hairs
Labellum thin-textured with 2 or 4 prominent porrect basal hairs 2.5–6 mm long
Tips of lateral sepals hooked forwards
Tips of lateral sepals deflexed or curved gently forwards, usually not hooked forwards
Dorsal sepal with decurved filiform point; proximal flanges of petals meeting and blocking off the base of the galea; labellum not or only partially visible from the side
Dorsal sepal with upcurved filiform point; proximal flanges of petals not meeting, leaving a gap in the base of the galea; labellum wholly visible from the side
Conjoined part of lateral sepals very broad, transverse elliptic to suborbicular, base truncate with sides more or less horizontal
Conjoined part of lateral sepals relatively narrow, ovate, base obtuse with sides curved downwards
Labellum ovate to obovate, 4.5–5.5 mm long, 2–2.3 mm wide; hairs on base of lateral sepals short
Labellum ovate-oblong, 4–4.5 mm long, c. 1.6 mm wide; hairs on base of lateral sepals quite long
Flowers dark reddish brown to almost black, often nodding; lateral sepals deeply concave at base
Flowers reddish brown with some green on galea, usually porrect; lateral sepals shallowly concave at base
Lateral sepals with filiform points >15 mm long; labellum more or less ovate, widest near base; mallee scrub in far north-west Victoria
Lateral sepals with filiform points <15 mm long; labellum more or less oblong, widest near middle; Eucalyptus/Callitris woodland near Beechworth in north-east Victoria
Flowers with green and colourless transparent bands; marginal hairs on proximal half of labellum as long or longer than labellum
Flowers predominantly brown or a mix of brown, olive and/or green; marginal hairs on proximal half of labellum shorter than labellum
Basal mound of labellum  with dense small hairs; pigmented parts of galea dark reddish-brown; labellum ovate-oblong; filiform point on dorsal sepal 5–6 mm long;
Basal mound of labellum without a crown of dense small hairs, but sparse and/or longer hairs to 1.5 mm long may be present; pigmented parts of galea greenish
Labellum ovate, basal mound with scattering of 4 sparse hairs  to 1.5 mm long on prominent basal mound, stony rise grasslands of western Victoria
Labellum obovate, basal mound with few or no hairs
Plant  9 –20 cm tall; labellum 4.8–5.7 mm long, 1.2–2.1 mm wide
Plant  18–58 cm tall; labellum 6.2–7.9 mm long, 1.7–2.9 mm wide
Scape 8 cm long or less, flowers spreading to deflexed, the free points of the lateral sepals often touching the ground
Scape usually more than 10 cm tall, flowers spreading to obliquely erect, free points of lateral sepals hanging well clear of the ground
Flowers mostly with green markings and suffusions
Flowers brown or a mix of brown, olive and/or green;
Flowers usually a mix of brown, olive and/or green stripes with translucent white markings; labellum upturned at the tip, with translucent grooves longitudinally in distal half
Flowers mostly brown with some colourless 'windows' in the galea; labellum lacking translucent grooves, without a prominently upturned tip
Rosette leaves to 6 mm wide, labellum up to 3.5 mm wide; riverine woodlands with clayey soils dominated by Black Box (Eucalyptus largiflorens)
Rosette leaves to 18 mm wide, labellum 3.5–4.5 mm wide; habitat not as above, soils freely-draining
Conjoined part of lateral sepals more or less flat with incurved margins; rosette leaves prominently veined; petals attenuate at base, long-acuminate at apex; far western Victoria
Conjoined part of lateral sepals concave; rosette leaves not prominently veined; petals not as above; widespread
Lateral sepals c. 4 mm wide, green and light brown, dull, swept back
Lateral sepals >5 mm wide, reddish brown, shiny, deflexed
Labellum obovate; lateral sepals ending in filiform points often >10 mm long; Beechworth area
Labellum oblong; lateral sepals ending in filiform points <10 mm long; mostly western Victoria
Galea 13–16 mm long; conjoined part of sepals at the widest point as wide as or wider than the galea
Galea less than 13 mm long (usually c. 10 mm); conjoined part of sepals at the widest point narrower than galea
Galea c. 16 mm long including an apical tip c. 2 mm long; lateral sepals c. 6 mm across, similar in width to galea, free part c. 8 mm long;
Galea c. 13 mm long including an apical tip c. 1.5 mm long; lateral sepals c. 7 mm across, slightly broader than galea, free part c. 7 mm long
Plants mostly <15 cm tall; galea <30 mm long; dorsal sepal lacking a filiform point; labellum hairs very dense
Plants mostly >15 cm tall; galea >30 mm long; dorsal sepal with an upturned filiform point; labellum hairs moderately dense
Apical knob on labellum usually green; galea 35–40 mm long; plants to 35 cm tall; Anglesea area
Apical knob on labellum brown; galea usually <35 mm long; plants to 25 cm tall; widespread

Sepals less than 15 mm long, terminating in a shorter point; never thread-like; leaf not toothed
Petals spreading, not reflexed towards the ovary; dorsal sepal hooded closely over column
Petals reflexed towards the ovary; dorsal sepal not hooded closely over column
Dorsal sepal 6–8 mm long, usually somewhat warty; labellum all or mostly reddish-purple; north-east Victoria
Dorsal sepal 9–12 mm long, smooth or very nearly so; labellum wholly green or green and maroon; near-coastal far east Victoria
Labellum 6–7 mm long, ovate-cordate, base of lamina truncate to cordate
Labellum 3–5 mm long, oblong-ovate to ovate-lanceolate, base of lamina broadly wedge-shaped or squarish with rounded corners

leads.lead_text: Margins of labellum fimbriate or toothed (sometimes minutely); inner (upper) surface of labellum lamina clearly visible
Margins of labellum entire; inner surface of labellum lamina mostly or totally obscured by dorsal sepal
Labellum margin with long dark fringe
Labellum margin toothed
Labellum minutely glandular, with a purplish-red, entire boss; dorsal sepal as broad as labellum, not extending out beyond it; mostly coastal
Labellum with rough hairs, and a white, notched boss; dorsal sepal much narrower than labellum and extending out beyond it; montane forests
Dorsal sepal much reduced, less than half as wide as labellum, not hooded
Dorsal sepal broad, usually almost as wide as labellum and hooded over it
Margin of labellum incurved, forming a distinct inward-leaning rim, marginal teeth rather blunt, <1 mm long; central boss of labellum channelled at base
Margin of labellum not or barely incurved, marginal teeth acute, 1 mm long or more; central boss of labellum flat, convex or very slightly concave at base
Labellum  margin more or less erect near base and flared outward distally; rare hybrid between C. diemenicus and C. incurvus, currently only known from far south-west Victoria
Labellum margin more or less evenly flared outwards
Labellum lamina uniformly dark reddish brown, covered with short stiff hairs; auricles obscured by labellum lamina; found in Leptospermum lanigerum swamps
Labellum lamina maroon usually with a pale central boss, glabrous; auricles not obscured by labellum lamina; habitat not as above
Labellum margin flared widely; flowers >12 mm across; open forest and coastal scrub
Labellum margins flared slightly; flowers <12 mm across; mountain forests mostly on fallen logs and tree fern trunks
Dorsal sepal elliptic, strongly curved over entire labellum
Dorsal sepal broadly expanded at distal end and spoon-like, covering labellum but leaving small orifice in front
Leaf green below; labellum streaked red and white, with 5–7 rows of linear calli near orifice
Leaf red below; labellum wholly purplish, with only a central row of linear calli

leads.lead_text: Leaf flexuose or spirally twisting; flower usually solitary, deep purple to violet with prominent darker stripes
Leaf straight; flowers 1 to many, variously coloured
Lateral lobes of column absent or without hair-tufts
Lateral lobes of column with hair-tufts
Leaf ovate, less than 4 times as long as wide; flowers greenish-yellow with large reddish-brown blotches
Leaf lanceolate to linear, more than 4 times as long as wide
Lateral lobes of column rudimentary or absent; anther beak oblong, large and protruding; perianth yellow
Lateral lobes of column extended into distinct appendages; anther beak various; perianth various
Lateral lobes of column fleshy, suberect; anther beak obtuse
Lateral lobes of column ribbon-like;  anther beak acute or bifid
Mid-lobe of column absent; lateral lobes of column more than 3 mm long, held above column
Mid-lobe of column prominent; lateral lobes of column less than 3 mm long, protruding forwards
Lateral lobes of column red-brown, smooth; perianth yellow
Lateral lobes of column yellow to pink, crenulate to rugose; perianth usually shades of pink, red or violet
Lateral lobes of column ovoid, with finger-like papillae; perianth bright-pink to deep-violet
Lateral lobes of column oblong-lanceolate, crenulate to rugulose; perianth salmon-pink to reddish
Lateral lobes of column oblong, longer than wide, thickish, slightly toothed on margins; anther-point higher than mid-lobe; sepals not apiculate
Lateral lobes of column quadrangular, not much longer than wide, flattish, with fingerlike papillae outside; anther-point lower than mid-lobe; sepals apiculate
Labellum broadly obovate, different in shape from other perianth segments; lateral lobes of column twisted spirally, obtuse or lobed at apex; anther beak bifid

Labellum obovate to oblanceolate, not greatly different in shape from other perianth segments; lateral lobes of column straight or incurved, not twisted spirally, margins variously erose or toothed; anther beak acute

Lateral lobes of column somewhat concave on inner surface, often strongly incurved throughout, apices usually touching or overlapping;  perianth pale blue (rarely pink) inside, lacking obvious darker striations; moist sandy sites often around the edges of grasstree plains; far East Gippsland

Lateral lobes of column more or less flat, more or less parallel to weakly incurved, apices rarely touching;  perianth deep purplish blue with very strong darker longitudinal striations; mostly alpine and sub-alpine habitats; eastern Victoria
Mid-lobe of column a flap-like or semi-circular appendage or terminated in a variously crested and ornamented ridge
Mid-lobe of column forming a tubular hood over the anther
Perianth bright pink with yellow trichomes on the lateral lobes of column
Perianth usually blue, if rarely pink then trichomes on the lateral lobes of column white
At least the petals with prominent dark spots
Perianth unspotted
Mid-lobe of column deeply and broadly cleft at the tip; apex and margins more or less smooth
Mid-lobe of column narrowly and shallowly cleft at the tip; apex and margins minutely tuberculate
Perianth segments on mature plants usually >15 mm long; flowers often scented, pollinated by native bees (melittophilous)
Perianth segments usually to 10 mm long, rarely reaching 15 mm; flowers usually unscented, generally autogamous and often also cleistogamous
Plants short and stocky, usually clumping; inflorescence rarely exceeding 20 cm and often much shorter; perianth deep blue to purplish with darker striations; grasslands of western Victoria
Plants tall and often slender, rarely clumping; at least some mature plants with the inflorescence exceeding 20 cm tall; perianth pale to dark blue, not obviously striated; various habitats
Perianth segments in mature plants rarely exceeding 18 mm long
Perianth segments in most mature plants exceeding 18 mm long
Inflorescence, basal part of the leaf and bracts often a striking reddish purple in colour; whole plant sometimes glaucous; mallee habitats
Inflorescence, leaf and bracts predominantly green, sometimes with some minor purplish suffusions; plant not glaucous; more mesic habitats
Mid-lobe of column compressed dorsally, distal margin usually with two forward-pointing teeth; montane and subalpine habitats; flowers mostly December to February
Mid-lobe of column barely compressed dorsally, distal margin lacking two forward-pointing teeth; lowland habitats; flowers mostly September to October
Mid-lobe of column covered with a glaucous or glistening bloom
Mid-lobe of column lacking bloom

Mid-lobe of column narrow at the base and widest towards the apex; trichomes on the lateral lobes of column sparse, often connate at the base, 0.05–0.1 mm thick, usually bright yellow, strongly embracing the apex of the mid-lobe

Mid-lobe of column widest near the middle and narrowing only slightly above and below; trichomes on the lateral lobes of column congested, not connate at the base, <0.05 mm thick, white or creamy yellow, not strongly embracing the apex of the mid-lobe
Plants mostly <12 cm tall; flower usually solitary, rarely 2; perianth segments <10 mm long
Plants mostly >12 cm tall; flowers usually 2–6; perianth segments usually >10 mm long

Mid-lobe of column slightly inflated, black with a yellow apex, covered with a thin sparkling bloom, bilobed, the lobes 1.2–1.6 mm long; trichomes on the lateral lobes of column 1–1.2 mm long, usually white, sometimes cream; plants from swampy habitats, often in standing water at anthesis; flowering  mid-November to mid-December

Mid-lobe of column very inflated, mostly pinkish or brown grading into yellow at the apex, covered with a thick, waxy bloom, deeply bilobed, the lobes 1.5–2.5 mm long; trichomes on the lateral lobes of column 1.2–1.6 mm long, usually cream or yellow; plants from dry to moist woodland habitats, rarely in standing water at anthesis; flowering late September to mid-November
Trichomes on the lateral lobes of column usually cream or yellow, proximal trichomes often pinkish, at least basally
Trichomes on the lateral lobes of column usually entirely white, rarely mauve

Mid-lobe of column very inflated, mostly pinkish or brown grading into yellow at the apex, deeply bilobed, the lobes more or less parallel, 1.5–2.5 mm long; plants from dry to moist woodland habitats; flowering late September to mid-November

Mid-lobe of column slightly inflated, mostly dark brown or black with a distinct yellow apex, bilobed, the lobes usually diverging, 0.8–1.5 mm long; plants from moist heathland and swamp margins; flowering early November to early December

Leaf lanceolate (at least on mature plants), usually less than half the height of the inflorescence and often much shorter, blade more or less flat and thin-textured, frequently with dark reddish margins, veins and suffusions; mid-lobe of column often deeply and irregularly slit at the apex into 2 parallel lobes, usually orange-brown or bright reddish orange

Leaf linear to linear-lanceolate, usually fleshy and canaliculate mostly more than half the height of the inflorescence; mid-lobe of column sometimes v-notched but not irregularly slit at the apex, usually brown to black with a yellow tip
Mid-lobe of column not as above; trichomes white
Mid-lobe of column strongly compressed dorsally in the distal half, apical orifice small; trichomes white or mauve
Mid-lobe of column mostly glossy black; trichomes white; sterile bracts usually 2; perianth pale blue
Mid-lobe of column dark reddish brown; trichomes usually pink or mauve, rarely white; sterile bracts usually 3; perianth slaty blue to purplish
Lateral lobes of column glabrous in at least the basal ¼ to ½, with trichomes in a more or less terminal mop-like arrangement
Lateral lobes of column not glabrous at the base, with trichomes extending more or less along their entire length in a toothbrush-like arrangement
Tepals reflexing back strongly towards the ovary, particularly at air temperatures of 30 degrees Celsius or more; mid-lobe of column uniformly dark blackish green or brown throughout
Tepals spreading at about right angles to the ovary, but never reflexing strongly even on the hottest days; mid-lobe of column usually bicolorous
Leaf blade flat; leaf fistula at ground level; column mid-lobe not inflated
Leaf blade at least partly channelled, often fleshy; leaf fistula well above ground level; column mid-lobe inflated
Sterile bract always single; ovary very pale, yellow-green; exterior surface of sepals lilac with pale edges
Sterile bracts usually 2; ovary not very pale, yellow-green, exterior surface of sepals not lilac with pale edges
Flowers usually 1–3, most often pale blue; lateral lobes 0.5–1 mm long, bent sharply upwards at c. 90º near the middle; post-anther lobe entire or emarginate
Flowers usually 4–10, most often mauve or deep purplish blue; lateral lobes 1.2–1.5 mm long, curved gently upwards; post-anther lobe usually deeply bilobed at the apex

Mature flower buds inflated, about 10 mm in diameter, subacute at apex; exterior of sepals pink with darker striations; column mid-lobe orifice widely gaping, thetwo apical halves often compressed; trichomes of lateral lobes often sparse or lacking

leaf usually > 10 mm wide; mature flower buds not
Mature buds inflated, < 8 mm in diameter, acute at apex; exterior of sepals ranging from brown to grey and pale-edged; column mid-lobe orifice hardly gaping, the two apical halves not compressed; trichomes of the lateral lobes dense;
Perianth segments rarely more than 12 mm long; mature plants rather small and slender; flowers rarely more than 8 even on mature plants; plants often forming clumps; mostly from grasslands
Perianth segments often more than 12 mm long; mature plants tall and stout; flowers more than 8 on at least some mature plants; plants not clumping; from various habitats
Leaf very thick, fleshy and brittle, as long as or longer than inflorescence
Leaf moderately fleshy, flexible, shorter than inflorescence
Mid-lobe of column deeply v-notched, black with a yellow apex; perianth white or very pale blue; sterile bract usually solitary; near-coastal habitats
Mid-lobe of column emarginate, brown with a yellow apex; perianth usually blue or purplish; sterile bracts usually 2; various habitats

Lower pedicels often partially decurrent on rachis; sepals mostly green on external surface; base of upper sterile bract often only half encircling the scape; sterile bracts to 15 cm long; fertile bracts to 35 mm long
Pedicels never decurrent on rachis; sepals mostly purplish on external surface; base of upper sterile bract usually scape-encircling; sterile bracts to 8.5 cm long; fertile bracts to 22 mm long
Mid-lobe of column prominent, extending well beyond point of insertion of the lateral lobes
Mid-lobe of column not well-developed or absent
Column with a pair of auxiliary lobes between the lateral lobes and mid-lobe
Column lacking a pair of auxiliary lobes
Plant robust with a large fleshy leaf and several large leaf-like sterile bracts; perianth variously coloured
Plant slender with a small canaliculate leaf and 1 or 2 small non-leafy sterile bracts; perianth azure blue
Trichomes on lateral lobes of column yellow; perianth pink, spotted or unspotted
Trichomes on lateral lobes of column white; perianth usually blue, spotted or unspotted
Perianth unspotted; surface of mid-lobe of column smooth
Perianth usually spotted; surface of mid-lobe of column rough
Perianth with a few darker blue spots at least on the petals
Perianth unspotted
Mid-lobe of column flap-like, lateral margins not or only slightly recurved; perianth segments 15–25 mm long; flowers opening readily
Mid-lobe of column semi-cylindric, lateral margins strongly recurved; perianth segments to 15 mm long; flowers opening tardily
Perianth unspotted
At least the petals with prominent dark spots
Mid-lobe of column with rows of long finger-like glands
Mid-lobe of column absent or smooth or with few short erect calli
Auxiliary lobes of column with deeply and irregularly toothed margins; trichomes on lateral lobes of column usually yellow
Auxiliary lobes of column not as above; trichomes on lateral lobes of column usually white
Perianth segments usually >13 mm long; flowers usually >10; robust plants to 1 m tall, mainly from mountain forests
Perianth segments to 13 mm long; flowers 1-8; slender plants to 55 cm tall, mainly from heathlands and swamp margins
Auxiliary lobes of column often >1 mm long; perianth segments narrow and overlapping only at base, deep blue to purplish or pinkish on inner surface; plants mainly from swamp margins

Leaf apex with a pungent tip; corolla tube less than 3.5 mm long; mature leaves serrulate
Leaf apex with a blunt callus tip; corolla tube 4–6 mm long; mature leaves usually entire
Sepals ovate, 1.5–2 (–2.5) mm long, half to two-thirds the length of the corolla tube; corolla lobes 1.2–2.5 mm long; low suckering shrub rarely exceeding 30 cm high
Sepals lanceolate to lanceolate-ovate, 2.8–3.5 mm long, about as long as the corolla tube; corolla lobes 2.5–4 mm long; erect or spreading shrub to c. lm high

Staminal filaments broad and distinctly flattened, ± fleshy; stamens not or barely exserted from corolla tube; corolla red or orange
Staminal filaments slender, terete to slightly flattened; stamens distinctly exserted beyond corolla tube; corolla white, yellow or pinkish
Prostrate or decumbent shrub; leaves 8–32 mm long; sepals 7–13.5 mm long; corolla tube 12.5–20 mm long, the interior surface with a ring of hairs towards the base; Grampians to eastern Victoria
Erect shrub; leaves 3.2–9 mm long; sepals 2.4–3.2 mm long; corolla tube 3–4.3 mm long, the interior surface glabrous in the lower half; Big Desert
Leaves distinctly concave on upper surface
Leaves flat or convex
Leaves obovate to ovate or suborbicular; obtuse at apex (but sometimes shortly mucronate); western
Leaves narrow, tapered at base, acute (rarely obtuse) and often pointed at apex; eastern, except widespread L. ericoides
Leaves tapered at base; flowers pendent
Leaves truncate to cordate at base; flowers erect
Leaves ovate to broadly ovate, less than 2 mm wide, lower surface with very short hairs between veins; flowers normally solitary (sometimes paired)
Leaves broadly ovate to orbicular, 3–12 mm wide, wider than long, both surfaces glabrous; flowers normally paired (sometimes solitary or in 3s)
Leaves erect, flat, sometimes slightly twisted, mostly longer than 15 mm; ovary 2-locular; localized on poorly drained, near-coastal heaths in the far east
Leaves spreading to ascending, usually distinctly convex (if leaves ever flat then habitat not as above), rarely to 15 mm long
Flowers solitary or paired (rarely in clusters of 3)
Flowers several in short, erect axillary spikes
Corolla lobes up to half as long as tube; corolla tube clearly exceeding sepals
Corolla lobes subequal to or distinctly longer than tube; corolla tube not exceeding sepals
Corolla tube 2.5–4.5 mm long; lobes about half as long as tube; trailing to decumbent shrub
Corolla tube 5–7 mm long; lobes only about one-quarter as long as tube; erect shrub
Flowers erect; style only 0.5–0.9 mm long, not reaching throat of corolla tube
Flowers pendent; style 4–7 mm long, exceeding throat of corolla tube
Leaves dull, usually roughened or variously hairy, margins strongly recurved to revolute; usually on sandy soils
Leaves smooth and shining above, glabrous, margins rather weakly recurved; apparently confined to gorge tracts of Snowy River

Leaf apex with a blunt callus tip
Flowers in c. 3–14-flowered spikes less than 10 mm long; at least some leaves longer than 5 mm
Flowers in c. 15–30-flowered spikes 15–30 mm long; leaves 1.5–5 mm long
Spreading shrub c. 30–130 cm high, stems not rooting; corolla tube less than 3 mm long; ovary and fruit glabrous
Prostrate to decumbent shrub to c. 15 cm high, stems rooting; corolla tube more than 5 mm long; ovary and fruit pubescent

Underside of leaves pale green, the veins separated by very narrow deep grooves; leaves glabrous or scabrous towards base on upper side, margins smooth to scabrous-ciliolate, hairs less than 0.2 mm long; style 0.7–1.3 mm long

leads.lead_text: Leaf apex usually pungent with a mucro 0.2–1.7 mm long; leaves usually more than 6 mm long, but if shorter then narrow-oblong, lanceolate or elliptic when flattened; small shrubs to small trees
Leaf apex with a blunt callous point; leaves 1.8–6 mm long, broadly elliptic-ovate to broadly oblong when flattened; shrub to 30 cm high, confined to Brumby Point on Nunniong Plateau

Flowers solitary in bract axils of current season\'s growth and/or in racemes in the upper leaf axils of previous season\'s growth; racemes (when present) with distinctly pedicellate flowers subtended for the most part by scarious caducous bracts most of which are more than 1.3 mm long (the distal-most sometimes persistent and becoming leaf-like); ripe fruit red-orange

At least some of the inflorescences produced in the bract axils of current growth spicate; racemes always absent; individual flowers subtended by small persistent bracts less than 1.3 mm long; fruit greyish, yellow or red-orange when ripe

Leaves 9–23 mm long, 2.4–6.5 mm wide; corolla tube of male flowers (0.8–)l-1.5 mm long; female corolla tube 0.5–1 mm long; anthers (1.1–) 1.2–1.9 mm long; all or most flowering axes not continuing terminal vegetative growth beyond the flowering region; plant of near-coastal areas, flowering Jun.-Sep

Leaves 3.8–11 mm long, 1.4–2.8 mm wide; corolla tube of male flowers 0.4–0.8 mm long; female corolla tube 0.4–0.6 mm long; anthers 0.8–1.2 (–1.3) mm long; all or most flowering axes continuing terminal vegetative growth beyond the flowering region (while plants flowering); plant of montane-subalpine areas, flowering Nov.-Jan

Lowermost spikes lacking or rarely with 1 sterile bract; lowermost spikes with peduncle (0.4–) 0.8–3.2 mm long; leaves usually 2.3–5 mm wide; non-lignotuberous shrubs or small trees frequently higher than 2m

Lowermost spikes with 1–4 (usually 2) inconspicuous basal or subbasal sterile bracts; lowermost spikes with peduncle wanting or occasionally to 0.6 mm long; leaves usually 1.3–2.6 mm wide; lignotuberous shrub to 2 m high
Corolla of male flowers 2.5–3 mm long; female corolla 1.6–2.2 mm long; anthers 1.3–1.8 mm long; distal leaves with petioles glabrous abaxially; fruit red-orange when fully ripe; Grampians endemic

Corolla of male flowers 1.5–2.2 mm long; female corolla 1.2–1.8 mm long; anthers 0.6–1.1 mm long; distal leaves with petioles usually puberulent abaxially; fruit translucent greyish when fully ripe; scattered in southern Victoria

leads.lead_text: Leaves distinctly concave
Leaves flat or convex, margins often recurved
Leaf-bases conspicuously cordate, ± stem-clasping at base, palmately 5–7-veined; localized in the north-west on mallee sandhills
Leaf-bases tapered to obtuse, rarely slightly cordate, ± parallel-veined; very widespread, except in further north-west
Procumbent shrubs; leaf margins with relatively long, thready hairs, leaf surfaces otherwise glabrous; uncommon species of moist subalpine or alpine, treeless heaths and grasslands
Erect shrubs; leaves glabrous, or with hairs either short (less than 0.5 mm long) or not confined to margins
Corolla lobes distinctly shorter than to subequal to tube; montane to subalpine shrubs
Corolla lobes longer than or equal to tube; lowland or lower montane species
Leaves small (up to 12 mm long) with margins recurved to some extent, or if flat, then leaves spirally twisted to some degree
Leaves at least 12 mm (and normally 15 mm) long, more or less flat, never spirally twisting
Leaf surfaces pubescent; sepals distinctly hairy, obtuse to broadly acute
Leaves glabrous, or very shortly ciliate on margins only; sepals glabrous or nearly so, acute

Flower spikes very short (up to c. 7 mm long), usually 2–5-flowered; sepals 2.2–3 mm long, dark-tipped; ovary 2- or 3-locular; leaves to 6 mm long; mainly eastern, with outlying populations in and near the Brisbane Ranges
Flower spikes generally 1 cm long or more, mostly 7–13-flowered; sepals 1.6–2.2 mm long, not dark-tipped; ovary 3–5-celled; leaves commonly 1 cm long or more; Grampians only
Leaves usually with margins recurved, not spirally twisted, usually widely spreading or reflexed, at least on lower parts of branches; eastern
Leaves flat in cross-section, but spirally twisted to some degree, erect to ascending on stem; western
Leaves rather rigid, prominently lined on both surfaces by 3–7 translucent veins; endemic on mountains of the Grampians and nearby ranges to the east
Leaves mostly thin, the veins neither particularly conspicuous nor translucent; mostly foothills and near coasts, not in Grampians
Leaves distinctly coumarin-scented; flowers 15 or more in spikes mostly longer than 30 mm; slender shrubs to c. 2 m high, of near-coastal heaths
Leaves not coumarin-scented (practically odourless); flowers mostly fewer than 15 on spikes mostly less than 30 mm long; shrubs often with spreading branches, often higher than 2 m
Leaves usually widest about midway; flowers distinctly separated on spike; ripe fruit red (rarely merely yellowish); ovary 2 (rarely 3)-locular; lowland forests, rarely truly coastal
Leaves widest above midway; flowers crowded on spike; ripe fruit white; ovary 4–5-locular; mainly coastal

Stamens 4 or 5
Leaf-bases entirely sheathing stem; staminal filaments free from corolla and inserted at base of ovary
Leaves petiolate, sessile or stem-clasping, but bases never entirely sheathing stem; staminal filaments fused to corolla

Corolla not separating into lobes but splitting transversely near base, the upper hood-like part (operculum) shed, the lower cup-like part persisting; anthers free, glabrous; montane to alpine watercourses and bogs
Corolla lobes separating at anthesis, not forming a deciduous operculum; anthers cohering around the style, densely hairy; lowland (rarely montane) wet heathlands
[link through]
Style inserted in a deep depression between the carpels; fruit a capsule opening by 5 valves
Style not inserted in a deep depression between the carpels; fruit a drupe or sometimes the endocarp separating into pyrenes
Axillary inflorescences single-flowered, spicate or racemose, individual flowers subtended by a solitary persistent or caducous (sometimes leaf-like) bract and two bracteoles

Axillary inflorescences all or mostly single-flowered (rarely some 2- or 3-flowered) with subtending bracts and bracteoles collectively more than 3; bracts and bracteoles often difficult to distinguish from one another and grading in size to the sepals
Staminal filaments slender, terete to slightly flattened
Staminal filaments broad and distinctly flattened, ± fleshy
Inner surface of corolla tube glabrous except for 5 reflexed fringed ovate scales inserted above the middle; corolla lobes obtuse to subacute, imbricate in bud
Inner surface of corolla tube with hairs scattered or in tufts or a ring towards the base, lacking reflexed scales above the middle; corolla lobes acute-acuminate, valvate in bud

Inner surface of corolla tube with tufts or a ring of papilla-like glandular hairs towards the base; style less than 1 mm long; filaments becoming free from the corolla near the base of the tube; veins on undersurface of leaf several, parallel, unbranched and separated by deep grooves

Inner surface of corolla tube with hairs scattered, in tufts or in a ring towards the base, but hairs not glandular and papilla-like; style longer than 5 mm; filaments becoming free from corolla well above base of tube; midvein only visible on underside of leaf, or if several veins apparent then some branched and/or not separated by deep grooves
[link through]
Flowers solitary or 2–3, in a short spike; external surface of corolla glabrous; bracteoles less than 5 mm long, c. half the length of calyx
Flowers solitary; external surface of corolla minutely hairy or glabrous; bracteoles more than 6 mm long, c. two-thirds to three-quarters the length of calyx
Anthers much exserted from corolla tube on long erect filaments; filaments much longer than the anthers; style longer than corolla tube
Anthers enclosed within to shortly exserted from corolla tube on short filaments; filaments shorter than or equal in length to the anthers; style shorter than corolla tube
Hard endocarp of fruit not separating into pyrenes; pungent-leaved shrub 0.5–3 m high; near-coastal
Hard endocarp of fruit separating into pyrenes; blunt-leaved mat-forming shrub less than 15 cm high; higher alps
[link through]
[link through]
Bracteoles distant from base of calyx; inner surface of corolla tube glabrous in lower third to half, pilose above

Bracteoles inserted immediately below base of calyx; inner surface of corolla tube glabrous, or if hairs present, then confined to apex (i.e. in throat) and often in 5 tufts between the staminal filaments
[link through]

Throat of corolla tube partially or fully closed by 5 tufts of dense spreading hairs originating from near the junction of the corolla tube and lobes, the corolla lobes above wholly glabrous to minutely papillose or with an isolated subterminal comb-like tuft of long erect stiff hairs; flowers strictly in spikes borne on branchlets at least 1 year old; anthers much exserted from corolla tube on erect or strongly reflexed filaments; fruit 2–11-locular, endocarp ± separating into pyrenes

Throat of corolla tube not closed by hairs, or if partially closed then the corolla lobes above neither wholly glabrous to minutely papillose nor with an isolated subterminal comb-like tuft of long erect stiff hairs; flowers solitary or in spikes or racemes on current season?s or 1 year old (rarely older) branchlets; anthers enclosed or exserted from corolla tube; fruit 1–5-locular, endocarp not separating into pyrenes
Corolla lobes usually green, with a subterminal comb-like tuft of long erect stiff hairs; ovary and fruit 3–7-locular; widespread
Corolla lobes usually maroon, lacking a subterminal tuft of hairs; ovary and fruit 8–11-locular; decumbent shrub of montane to subalpine sites in the east
[link through]
Ovary 1-locular; corolla tube glabrous internally; corolla lobes glabrous, minutely papillose or rarely with a few very sparse inconspicuous hairs internally
Ovary 2–5-locular; corolla tube usually with hairs in the throat between the anthers; corolla lobes papillose or sparsely to densely bearded internally
Corolla lobes distinctly imbricate in bud, minutely papillose internally
Corolla lobes valvate in bud, sparsely to densely bearded internally (glabrous to minutely papillose in alpine L. montanus)
Flowers unisexual or at least functionally so; corolla lobes shorter or subequal to tube; anthers without sterile tip; alpine and subalpine areas

Flowers bisexual; corolla lobes usually longer or equal to tube, if ever much shorter than tube then flowers on distinctly decurved spike; anthers with or without a sterile tip; mostly from lowland and montane areas
Flowers all axillary, either solitary or in 2s or 3s on a short spike; anthers without a sterile tip
Flowers terminal and sometimes axillary, in spikes (sometimes condensed) mostly of >3 flowers; anthers with a sterile tip
Leaves narrow-linear, to 1 cm long; margins closely revolute; sepals and petals each 4; corolla persisent
Leaves obovate to ovate or lanceolate, 2 cm long or more; margins plane (but usually serrate); sepals and petals each 5; corolla deciduous
Fruit a globular berry, c. 2 cm diam., rough and orange-red at maturity; stems with gland-tipped hairs; tall shrub or small tree escaped from cultivation
Fruit a capsule, enclosed at maturity by the white or pinkish, enlarged and thickened calyx; stems with acicular bristles; weak montane shrub to c. 1.6 m high
