Midvein on undersurface of leaf either concealed by the revolute margins, or exposed and bearing a dense appressed indumentum similar to that on the adjacent lamina; midvein on undersurface often reducing in prominence toward leaf apex; pistil 6–7.5 mm long; tepals white to cream, tinged with brown hairs on limb

Midvein on undersurface of leaf always exposed, either glabrous or bearing an open appressed indumentum (less dense than on adjacent lamina); midvein on undersurface uniform in prominence from base to apex; pistil 5–13 mm long; tepals white to cream (sometimes with brown hairs) or pink to mauve or deep reddish-purple

Perianth red-purple; white hairs of the inner perianth surface conspicuously displayed at anthesis; dorsal tepals each 1–2 mm wide; conflorescence dense, semi-secund; longest floral rachises usually 6–20 mm long; style with minute hairs and papillae over the apical 0.5–1.5 (–6) mm

Perianth white, cream, pink, or light mauve; hairs of the inner surface of the perianth not conspicuous at anthesis; dorsal tepals each 0.5–1 mm wide; longest floral rachises usually 2–8 mm long; style usually with minute hairs and papillae over the apical 0.2–0.8 mm (G. linearifolia complex)
Inner surface of perianth glabrous, or occasionally with only a few scattered hairs (usually less than 0.2 mm long) surmounting a cushion-like pulvinus ± opposite the ovary
Inner surface of perianth with a dense to scanty beard (hairs 0.2–1.0 mm long) ± opposite the ovary, at least on the ventral tepals
Conflorescence pedunculate (peduncle 1–15 mm long)
Conflorescence sessile
Most leaves 2.5–5 (–8) cm long; leaf undersurface enclosed except for midvein; eastern Victoria
Most leaves less than 2.5 cm long; leaf undersurface usually with some subsericeous lamina exposed on either side of the midvein; confined to the Grampians region

Leaves mostly less than 2.5 cm long; leaf cross-section usually oblong, with the margins refracted more or less vertically downward from the plane of the (usually flat, occasionally slightly convex) upper surface
Leaves (2–) 2.5–8 cm long; leaf cross-section obliquely elliptic, with the margins refracted at greater than or equal to 120° relative to the distinctly convex upper surface
Inner surface of perianth with a scanty beard, usually without hairs above; stipe of ovary usually less than 1 mm long; usually riparian
Inner surface of perianth with a profuse beard, with conspicuous hairs scattered above; stipe of ovary at least 1 mm long; sandy soils in heath or open woodland
Leaves needle-like, 10–22 mm long, 0.5–0.6 mm wide, angularly deltoid to trigonous in cross-section, lower surface usually concealed
Leaves never needle-like, > 1.5 mm wide, 20–135 mm long, leaves usually flat (apart from shortly revolute or recurved margins), lower surface usually exposed
Leaf apices pungent, 20–42 mm long, 2–6 mm wide, narrowly elliptic
Leaf apices obtuse to acute 20–100(–135) mm long, 6–35(–50) mm wide, leaf shape various (if ever narrowly elliptic then leaves either > 42 mm or > 8 mm wide)
Outer surface of perianth red
Outer surface of perianth apricot-coloured

Conflorescences axillary or occasionally cauline; branches strongly angular in cross-section, the longitudinal ribs prominent, branches usually with strongly ascending to erect branches; unit conflorescence a loose, often subsecund, subglobose cluster

Conflorescences terminal on short lateral branchlets or axillary; with spreading to ascending branches; branches terete, subterete or moderately angular in cross-section near apex of shoot in cross-section, ribbing absent or hidden or only slightly raised; unit conflorescence subcylindric, subconical, or a loose subglobose cluster
Leaf upper surface distinctly granulose; branchlets subvillous; leaf lower surface loosely subvillous to villous

Leaf upper surface smooth (occasionally microscopically asperulous (40X magnification) in Grevillea miqueliana subsp. miqueliana and G. victoriae subsp. nivalis), smooth to touch, never granulose), glabrous to variably pubescent; branchlets variably pubescent; leaf lower surface variably pubescent

Flower buds at all developmental stages wholly reddish-ferruginous; perianth outer surface below the limb densely subvillous, epidermis usually not visible or occasionally partially visible; tepal inner surface uniformly pinkish-red
Very early flower buds with the perianth (below the limb) usually pale silvery-lilac, maturing to pink or pinkish red, perianth-limb dirty brownish-grey; perianth inner surface bichromatic
Branchlets densely subvillous, densely tomentose or subtomentose; leaf lower surface indumentum various; pollen-presenter lateral or oblique to the syle, convex or concave in cross-section
Branchlet densely sericeous or subsericeous; leaf lower surface indumentum usually sericeous; pollen-presenter oblique to the style, flat or slightly convex in cross-section
Pollen-presenter lateral to style-end; face of pollen-presenter usually strongly concave (rarely flattened) in cross-section, base concurrent with the style
Pollen-presenter strongly oblique to style-end; face of pollen-presenter convex in cross-section, base not concurrent with style

Leaf undersurface indumentum subsericeous or occasionally densely subtomentose (epidermis not visible); the inner surface of the recurved portion of the perianth below the limb in open flower  monochromatic

Leaf undersurface indumentum loosely sericeous or with scattered mutually aligned appressed hairs (epidermis usually clearly visible), or loosely to moderarely subtomentose (epidermis visible), or loosely subvillous (epidermis visible); the inner surface surface of the recurved  portion of the perianth below the limb in an open flower monochromatic or bichromatic
Leaf length to width ratio (3.6:1–)4.0–6.0:1(–8.0:1); floral bracts 1.0–1.5(–2) mm long; outer surface of ventral tepals uniformly coloured, without a central blotch
Leaf length to width ratio 1.5–4.0:1; floral bracts 2.0–4.2 mm long; outer surface of ventral tepals usually with a central blotch and usually red or pinkish-red towards base and apex of the perianth

Very early flower buds wth a purplish-pink, lilac or pale pink perianth below the limb, limb pale brown or dirty greyish brown; the inner surface of the recurved portion of the perianth below the limb in an open flower usually bichromatic

Very early flower buds wholly ferruginous or perianth below the limb occasionally reddish or limb occasionally tan-coloured; the inner surface of the recurved portion of the perianth below the limb in an open flower monochromatic, the outer surface of ventral tepals uniformly coloured, without a central blotch
Leaf undersurface with short curled to strongly wavy hairs; flower buds reflexed at > 90°
Leaf undersurface always with straight or nearly straight hairs; flower buds either not reflexed or if reflexed then at or < 90°
Perianth-limb subacute in most flowers; flower buds reflexed at or <  90°; ovary sometimes with minute spreading hairs
Perianth-limb obtuse (rarely subacute in G. brevifolia at Merryangaah Peak in NSW); flower buds not reflexed or reflexed at or less than 90°; ovary always glabrous
Pollen-presenter lateral to style-end, base concurrent with the style; perianth outer surface below the limb red reddish-pink, pink, orange, yellowish or cream
Pollen-presenter oblique to style-end, base not concurrent with the style; perianth outer surface below the limb red or reddish-pink
Leaves (8–) 21–38(–49) mm x 6–16(–20) mm wide; leaf length to width ratio 2:1; floral rachis (7–)15–20(–35) mm long; unit conflorescence with (14–)20–22(–30) flowers
Leaves (20–)35–120(–200) mm x (7–)10–35(–50) mm wide; leaf length to width ratio 2:1–5:1(6:1); floral rachis (8–)17–66(–87) mm long; unit conflorescence with (16–)22–48(–68) flowers
Perianth-limb acute or drawn into a long, finely-pointed tip; style green; leaves 1–57.5 cm long, 0.3–51.5 cm wide
Perianth obtuse; style pink-red; leaves 20–105 mm long, 20–55 mm wide
Inner surface of perianth with hairs (sometimes few)
Inner surface of perianth glabrous

Hairs on ovary appressed (rarely ascending), regularly aligned; floral bracts to 1.0 mm long, deciduous in bud; style-end tapered smoothly into style, with dorsal side of style-end convex; hairs on outer surface of perianth appressed

Hairs on ovary ± spreading in several directions; floral bracts 1.3–4.0 mm long, usually persistent at or near anthesis; style-end abruptly contracted into the style with dorsal side of style-end concave; hairs on outer surface of perianth ascending to spreading
Outer surface of perianth glabrous
Outer surface of perianth with hairs (sometimes few and/or confined to limb segments at apex of tepals)
Pistils 8–10.5 mm long; style purplish, perianth cream; lower surface of mature leaves glabrous (sparsely hairy when immature)
Pistils 13–23 mm long; style red to pink, or rarely light green to yellow; lower surface of mature leaves sometimes enclosed by revolute margins, hairy or rarely glabrous
Style pubescent to villous; ovary subsessile, villous; upper surface of leaf usually villous or loosely so; leaves usually thick-textured (sometimes sausage-like when margins very revolute)

Style glabrous or only sparsely hairy; stipe of ovary ventrally gibbous; ovary usually only hairy in the basal half, glabrous or nearly so above; upper surface of leaf glabrous or with few hairs; leaves thin-textured; leaf apex usually tapering evenly into a weak to subpungent point

Unit conflorescences cylindric 50–120 mm long; perianth greyish white on outer surface, creamish white to light yellow on inner surface; leaves linear, 6–18 cm long, less than 2 mm wide; lower lamina usually completely obscured (except midvein) by the revolute margins; plants confined to mallee scrub, open shrubland, or Triodia communities, on yellow or red sands in the north-west Victoria

Unit conflorescences less than 5 cm long; perianth red, pink, orange, yellow or brown, or cream with one of these colours; leaves simple and entire, usually more than 5 mm wide, if ever sublinear then less than c. 4 cm long; lower lamina exposed or enclosed; plants occuring in various areas of Victoria
Ovary with only occasional, minute, patent hairs, virtually glabrous; leaves usually 19–28(–43) mm wide
Ovary with a sericeous or villous indumentum; leaves 1.5–15 mm wide (rarely to 35 mm wide in Grevillea floribunda)
Ovary stipitate, stipe 1.2–2.5 mm long; leaves often rigid and pungent-pointed
Ovary sessile; leaves never pungent-pointed
Nectary spreading and prominent, ± linguiform (tongue-like), projecting 1–3 mm beyond the torus into the basal pouch of the perianth
Nectary U- to V-shaped or cushion-like, erect or projecting less than 1 mm into the perianth pouch

Floral bracts conspicuous (especially on young conflorescences), 2.5–7 mm long, 2–5.5 mm wide, persistent to anthesis or after; leaves linear to narrowly oblong-elliptic, usually 30–75 mm long, 1-mm wide

Floral bracts inconspicuous, up to 2.5 mm long and 2 mm wide, usually deciduous in early-to mid-bud stage (rarely persistent, not conspicuous); leaves broadly linear to oblong-elliptic or ovate to almost round, 5–80 mm long, 5–18 mm wide
Floral rachises (distal from most basal pedicel scar) more than 10 mm long; outer surface of perianth with a dense indumentum of rust-coloured hairs; tepals usually persistent to fruiting stage
Floral rachises less than 10 mm long; outer surface of perianth with a sparse to dense indumentum of whitish to rust-coloured hairs; tepals deciduous soon after anthesis
Nectary relatively conspicuous and prominent, extending more than 1 mm above rim of torus; perianth usually red and yellow; habit suckering
Nectary inconspicuous, extending less than 1 mm above rim of torus; perianth yellow or gold; habit not suckering
Ovary glabrous
Ovary with at least some hairs (sparse to dense)
Floral rachises 12–16 cm long, long secund; tree 15–40 m high
Floral rachises 2–5 cm long, subglobose; shrub 0.3–3 m high
Pistil 3.5–5.3 mm long
Pistil 12–27.5 mm long

Unit conflorescences cylindric (can be shortly cylindric in Grevillea pachylostyla, and then conflorescences to 50 mm long, and ovary stipe 0.3–0.5 mm long), 50–120 mm long; perianth greyish white on outer surface, creamish white to light yellow on inner surface; leaves linear, with up to 6 linear lobes, 6–18 cm long, less than 2 mm wide; lower lamina usually completely obscured (except midvein) by the revolute margins; plants confined to mallee scrub, open shrubland, or Triodia communities, on yellow or red sands in the north-west Victoria

Unit conflorescences secund, 30–85 mm long; perianth red, pink, orange, yellow or brown, or cream with one of these colours; leaves usually more than 5 mm wide, if ever sublinear then less than c. 60 mm long; lower lamina exposed or enclosed; plants occuring in various areas of Victoria
Leaf undersurface indumentum moderately dense, with predominantly longitudinally aligned, straight, appressed or slightly ascending hairs, hairs not wavy or curled
Leaf undersurface indumentum sparse to dense, with curled or slightly to strongly wavy hairs (only slightly wavy in G. infecunda, G. repens and G. steiglitziana)
Floral rachis tomentose (shaggy) with ascending ± straight hairs; anthers poorly developed and with sparse pollen; floral bracts 2–3 mm long, usually persistent at anthesis
Floral rachis with straight silky-appressed hairs; anthers well-developed and with abundant pollen; floral bracts not more than 2.5 mm long, deciduous in bud
Leaf undersurface indumentum dense, entire surface hidden by hairs; leaves with primary lobes only, shallow to deep, lobes 1–3 per margin; bracts 0.3–0.9 mm long; perianth 7–10 mm long

Leaf undersurface indumentum sparse or almost glabrous, or with occasionally with numerous scattered hairs but with much of the surface visible between the hairs, the hairs very slightly wavy or straight or both on same leaf; leaves either more or less regularly spinose-denticulate or shallowly lobed (< 8 mm deep) with 5–15(–22) teeth or very shallow lobes per margin, or leaves usually more or less bipinnatifid; bracts 0.7–2.6 mm long; perianth 6–8 mm long
Lobes of leaves < 4 mm wide, narrowly linear to subulate, margins flat to recurved to revolute
Lobes of leaves usually  > 4 mm wide, narrowly to broadly triangular or rounded-oblong, not linear to subulate, margins almost flat to slightly recurved
Plants prostrate; pedicels 3–6 mm long; pistil 16–19 mm long; leaves entire or pungently denticulate, or primary lobes only; bracts falling before anthesis
Plants erect to spreading; pedicels 1–3 mm long; pistil 15–27 mm long; leaves bipinnatifid; usually some bracts persistent at anthesis
Robust erect shrub or small tree 4–8 m high; leaves 50–270 mm long, coarsely lobed (lobes 10–65 mm long); conflorescence 50–100 mm long; growing in moist gullies

Spreading shrubs to 4 m high, but usually < 1.5 m high; leaves usually less than 50 mm long, juvenile leaves with 1-teeth or lobes (each less than 10 mm long); conflorescence less than 30 mm long; growing in sandy heaths
Ovary stipe 0.3–1.1 mm long; unit conflorescences many-flowered (20–90 flowers per conflorescence); flowers predominantly white to cream (although styles sometimes reddening with age)
Ovary stipe 1.8–4.4 mm long; unit conflorescences few- to many-flowered, sometimes pale but styles pink to red;

Most primary leaf-lobes further divided or toothed; conflorescence shortly cylindric or weakly secund, usually decurved-pendent; branchlets and floral rachis usually subsericeous with straight, ± appressed hairs)

Most primary leaf-lobes undivided; conflorescence strongly secund, projecting horizontally and erect (straight) on the peduncle; style cream, not changing colour after anthesis; branchlets and floral rachis with short woolly-pubescent indumentum of curled and twisted hairs
Stem indumentum sericeous or subsericeous, or stem glabrous
Stem Indumentum villous or tomentose
Rachis of unit conflorescence tomentose to villous with ascending to spreading hairs
Rachis of unit conflorescence glabrous or with a sparse to dense silky, appressed indumentum
Pistil  12–16.5 mm long; anthers well-developed and with abundant pollen; leaf undersurface indumentum sparse with curled hairs or occasionally tomentose; conflorescence bicoloured
Pistil 18–26 mm long; anthers poorly developed and with sparse pollen; leaf undersurface indumentum with slightly wavy hairs; conflorescence uniformly coloured
Leaf undersurface indumentum with hairs twisted, strongly wavy or curled; leaves with primary lobes only, shallow to deep, lobes 1–3 per margin; bracts 0.3–0.9 mm long;

Leaf undersurface indumentum sparse or almost glabrous, or with occasionally with numerous scattered hairs, the hairs very slightly wavy or straight or both on same leaf; leaves either more or less regularly spinose-denticulate or shallowly lobed (< 8 mm deep) with 5–15(–22) teeth or very shallow lobes per margin, or leaves usually more or less bipinnatifid; bracts 0.7–2.6 mm long
Leaf undersurface indumentum more or less dense, hidden by hairs or almost so; anthers poorly developed and with sparse pollen
Leaf undersurface indumentum sparse with much of the surface visible between the hairs, or glabrous; anthers well-developed and with abundant pollen
Plants prostrate; pedicels 3–6 mm long; pistil 16–19 mm long; leaves entire or pungently denticulate, or primary lobes only; bracts falling before anthesis
Plants erect to spreading; pedicels 1–3 mm long; pistil 15–27 mm long; leaves bipinnatifid; usually some bracts persistent at anthesis
Pistil 21–26 mm long
Pistil 12–18.5 mm long
Leaf undersurface indumentum glabrous or with only scattered or patchily distributed suberect curled or wavy hairs, especially along veins; leaves mostly bipinnatifid
Leaf undersurface indumentum usually moderately densely hairy, the hairs strongly curled or slightly wavy; leaves usually with primary division only
Leaf undersurface indumentum with strongly curled hairs (in Victorian plants); anthers well-developed and with abundant pollen
Leaf undersurface indumentum with slightly wavy hairs; anthers poorly developed and with sparse pollen

Mature leaves entire, elliptic, usually < 35 mm long and up to 6 mm wide, juvenile leaves with 2–4 variable triangular teeth; style-end scarcely wider than style (pollen presenter weakly conical and atrophied); anthers absent or atrophied

Mature leaves lobed,  usually cuneate to rhombic or long oblong-elliptic (rarely shortly elliptic), or deeply divided and holly- or oak-like, usually > 35 mm long and > 6 mm wide; juvenile leaves lobed; style-end distinctly wider than style, discoid or hoof-shaped
Most floral bracts 5–7 (–12.5) mm long, and some bracts usually retained in inflorescences at anthesis; perianth loosely tomentose to villous
All floral bracts less than 4.5 mm long, variably persistent; perianth loosely sericeous, subsericeous, or tomentose
Peduncles glabrous or almost so or except near the apex,  slender 0.4–0.5(–0.7) mm wide and wiry (10–)20–30 mm long
Peduncles tomentose or loosely so, or rarely with only scattered spreading hairs, peduncle usually relatively stout (0.6–)0.8–1.2(–1.5) mm wide, 5–15(–20) mm long
Leaf undersurface indumentum with slightly wavy, appressed and or ascending hairs; anthers poorly developed and with sparse pollen
Leaf undersurface indumentum with erect, suberect and or ascending twisted or curled hairs, or glabrous; anthers well-developed and with abundant pollen
Leaves coarsely dentate to pinnatifid; primary leaf lobes simple; flowers changing from green to pink at anthesis such that the conflorescence appears bicoloured
Leaves pinnatisect or sometimes pinnatifid; at least some primary leaf-lobes further divided or toothed; conflorescences not appearing bicoloured
Largest floral bracts 2–4.5 mm long; upper surface of leaves glabrous; pistil 15.5–17 mm long
Floral bracts 1–2 mm long; upper surface of leaves hairy or glabrous; pistil 13.5–15.5 mm long

Leaves with primary lobes broadly toothed or simple; simple primary lobes 5–15 mm wide; upper surface of mature leaves with an open to sparse indumentum of minute, appressed, curled to wavy hairs, rarely glabrous; peduncle 0.8–1 mm wide
Leaves with some primary lobes bearing narrowly triangular secondary lobes; simple primary lobes less than 5 mm wide; upper surface of mature leaves glabrous; peduncle 0.6–0.8 mm wide

leads.lead_text: Leaves all flat or trigonous
Leaves terete or flattened terete, or sometimes with a few flattened leaves also present
Leaves linear, 1–4 mm wide, twisted through 90Â° at base
Leaves more than 4 mm wide, twisted through 90Â° at base or not

Lignotuberous; inflorescence of 10–36 flowers; leaves 3–12 mm wide; mainly drier heaths and mallee scrub, from Otway Range west to South Australian border; flowers Sep.-Oct., vegetative growth starting Nov
Non-lignotuberous; inflorescence of 6–18 flowers; leaves 1–4 mm wide; heathlands and forests east of Otway Range; flowers Aug.-Sep., vegetative growth starting late Aug. to early Sep
Leaves with 3 or more prominent longitudinal veins
Leaf venation obscure, somewhat pinnate with a single faint longitudinal vein
Inflorescence a spherical head, usually with more than 70 flowers per head; perianth turning pink or reddish; fruit with or without a distinct keel along lower suture line; leaves somewhat petiolate
Flowers and fruits not as above; leaves not appearing petiolate
Leaves 6–30 mm wide with 3–7 prominent longitudinal veins; fruit with a distinct keel along lower suture line
Leaves 23–60 mm wide, usually with 3 prominent longitudinal veins; fruit lacking a keel along the lower suture line
Leaf margins with spine-tipped teeth
Leaf margins entire
Leaves elliptic to broadly elliptic, 15–55 mm wide; branchlets densely tomentose
Leaves linear to narrowly elliptic or narrowly obovate, usually 3–30 mm wide; branchlets densely tomentose or glabrescent
Fruits 2.5–3.5 cm long, more than 1.7 cm wide, curved downwards; pedicel pubescent; leaves not twisted through 90Â° at base; granite areas of far east
Fruits 1.5–2.6 cm long, less than 1.7 cm wide, erect; pedicel glabrous; leaves twisted through 90Â° at base; western Victoria, usually on sandy soils
Leaves auriculate, margins distinctly toothed (at least in distal half)
Leaves not auriculate, margins entire (rarely with a single pair of teeth in H. oleifolia)
Leaves less than 8 cm long, rarely toothed; pedicel and perianth glabrous; pollen presenter conical
Leaves more than 8 cm long, always entire; pedicel and perianth pubescent or glabrous; pollen presenter lateral or an oblique disc
Inflorescence with up to 10 flowers; pedicel and base of perianth pubescent with white hairs; pollen presenter lateral; fruit smooth or with minute brown warts
Inflorescence 16–28-flowered; pedicel and perianth glabrous; pollen presenter oblique; fruit with large, black, flat-topped warts
Leaves not divided; buds curved; inflorescence with fewer than 40 flowers; pollen presenter an oblique disc or erect cone
Leaves divided into 2–8 segments, rarely simple; buds straight; inflorescence with more than 40 flowers; pollen presenter an erect cone; fruits distinctly horned; naturalized from cultivation
Leaves grooved below (at least at base)
Leaves not grooved below
Leaves terete; flowers white or pink; perianth more than 3 mm long; pistil more than 7 mm long; fruit with horns, these often worn down
Leaves often somewhat flattened; flowers yellow; perianth 1.3–2.2 mm long; pistil 3–4.5 mm long; fruit lacking horns
Perianth pubescent; leaves flexible, angle between stem and leaves acute
Perianth glabrous; leaves rigid, usually widely spreading from stem
Pistil 8.5–12 mm long; perianth white or pink; pedicel appressed pubescent; leaves spreading widely from stem, rigid; lignotuberous
Pistil (4.5–) 5–7 (–7.5) mm long; perianth white; pedicel villous to hirsute; leaves spreading widely to narrowly angled to stem, flexible or rigid; not lignotuberous
Leaf apex bent
Leaf apex straight

Rachis (often visible even if not flowering) 6–14 mm long, white-pubescent; inflorescence with 18–45 flowers; pedicel and perianth glabrous; not all leaves with bent leaf-apex; flowers mostly Oct.-Dec
Rachis (often visible even if not flowering) 1–3 cm long, brown-pubescent; inflorescence with 6–22 flowers; pedicel and perianth pubescent; all leaves usually with bent leaf-apex; flowers Sep.-Oct
Suckering shrub, stems mostly to c. 50 cm high; fruit not formed; Upper Buchan River
Plants not suckering; fruit produced, often persisent on plants for many years; widespread
Fruit S-shaped; seed curved; pedicel and perianth pubescent with white hairs
Fruit not S-shaped; seed not curved; pedicel and perianth variously glabrous or pubescent (rarely both pubescent)
Leaves 2–15 cm long, curved; pistil recurved; fruit 2.2–4.5 cm long; flowers Jul.-Nov
Leaves 1–6 cm long, straight; pistil straight; fruit 1.5–2.2 cm long; flowers Aug.-Oct
Fruit more than 9 mm wide or if less, not dagger-shaped, lacking toothed ring below middle and not with a long narrow apex; flowers glabrous or only pedicels pubescent
Fruit less than 9 mm wide, dagger-shaped with toothed ring below middle and long narrowed apex; flowers densely pubescent
Pedicel and perianth glabrous; pollen presenter oblique or erect; fruits usually ± smooth, not rounded-tuberculate
Pedicel pubescent, perianth glabrous or with a few hairs similar to those on pedicel; pollen presenter oblique; fruits often rounded-tuberculate
Floral rachis less than 2 mm long, red-brown pubescent (H. microcarpa) or white-pubescent (H. mitchellii); fruit less than 25 mm long, less than 13 mm wide; shrubs, rarely exceeding 2 m
Floral rachis 6–14 mm long, white-pubescent; fruit 17–32 mm long, 10–20 mm wide; shrub or small tree to 8 m in north-west

Fruit inserted more or less at right-angles to stalk, with horns; seed occupying almost whole valve; pollen presenter an oblique disc; flowers 6–12 per inflorescence; shrub 0.6–2 m high; mostly wet heaths in alps and subalps (at low altitudes along rivers in the far east); flowers Sep.-Feb
Fruit inserted more or less in line with stalk, without horns; seed not occupying whole valve; pollen presenter conical; flowers 16–36 per inflorescence; drier areas in the west; flowers Oct.-Jan
Leaves 5–13 cm long, rigid; flowers relatively large, pistil 8–10.5 mm long; subalpine woodlands; flowers Oct.-Dec
Leaves 0.8–5 cm long, flexible; flowers tiny, pistil 3–4.5 mm long; lowland swampy heaths; flowers May-Aug

leads.lead_text: Style straightening or remaining weakly curved at anthesis, yellowish; perianth creamy-yellow to brownish; cones short-cylindric, ovoid or globose; leaves not as above

Style remaining hooked below apex after anthesis, purplish-black (rarely yellow or reddish); perianth golden-yellow or golden-brown; cones usually long-cylindric; leaves linear or narrowly oblanceolate
Mature leaves entire
Mature leaves dentate
Leaves elliptic to obovate or oblanceolate, often whorled
Leaves linear, oblong or lanceolate, scattered

Leaves either less than 15 mm long or glabrous above

Lateral veins apparent beneath (although sometimes partly obscured by dense tomentum); largest leaves longer than 18 mm
Indumentum of leaf internerves beneath of stellate hairs only
Indumentum of leaf internerves beneath including some simple hairs
Simple hairs dense, largely or entirely obscuring the underlying stellate hair layer
Simple hairs sparse to moderate, not covering more than c. 50% of underlying stellate hair layer

Flowers apetalous

Flowers apetalous

Leaves acutely tapered to base and apex, simple hairs very sparse and inconspicuous; margins recurved, not undulate

Flowers zygomorphic, the 2 upper petals differently shaped from, and mostly larger than, the 3 lower ones; uppermost sepal produced downwards into a nectary spur adnate to the pedicel (sometimes indistinct, and appearing as a small swelling on the pedicel); fertile stamens 3–8; mericarps obtuse to acute but not sharp-pointed at base, awns loosely spiralled at maturity

leads.lead_text: Leaves palmatisect or almost ternate with 3–5 primary lobes; primary lobes (particularly centre lobe) pinnatisect to c. bipinnatisect (usually 2 or more pairs of secondary lobes); garden-escapes
Leaves palmatifid to palmatisect with 3–9 primary lobes; primary lobes bifid, trifid or variously lobed but never truly pinnatisect (or never more than 2 pairs of c. opposite secondary lobes)
Petals 18–22 mm long; mericarps without long hair-like fibres
Petals to 15 mm long; tufts of long hair-like fibres attached at top of mericarp either side of dorsal suture near awn attachment
Flowers small, petals 5–9 mm long; foliage not malodorous; anthers yellow; mericarps with dense wrinkle-like ridges (see note after genus description)
Flowers large, petals 8–14 mm long; foliage malodorous; anthers orange to purple; mericarps with sparse, (usually) fine ridges
Plants glabrous to glabrescent (sometimes with isolated hairs or with inconspicuous indumentum of tiny appressed hairs)
Plants (particularly peduncles, pedicels and leaf surfaces) with a conspicuous (sparse to dense) indumentum
Plants glabrous or with minute retrorse and strongly-appressed hairs on stems and petioles; leaf surfaces usually with tiny appressed or curved hairs
Petioles and stems with very few scattered, retrorse or recurved to subappressed hairs, stems often glabrescent with age; leaf surfaces with isolated to scattered hairs

Basal leaves persisting throughout year; plants freely rooting from nodes along elongate flowering stem, or plant rosetted, without elongate flowering stems (or with very short stems never exceeding basal leaves); roots thickened and fibrous, often matted, sometimes with woody taproot; swamps and poorly-drained sites, often alpine or subalpine

Basal leaves usually senescing before or during stem elongation; plants not (or rarely) rooting from nodes; taproot napiform or thickened and tapering, sometimes with lateral branching but never fibrous and matted; habitat various but not swamp-inhabiting

Plants green to dark green; senescent leaves bright red to orange; flowers large (to 3 cm diam.), pink with darker veins and usually with long pedicel/peduncle (to 25 cm); sepals pubescent; flowering stems lax, with internodes often exceeding 20 cm long, extensively rooting from nodes; seeds with very small yet distinct isodiametric alveolae; East Gippsland, not alpine or subalpine

Plants usually greyish; senescent leaves never bright red to orange; flowers small (to 9 mm diam.), pale pink, usually sessile; sepals pilose; flowering stems (if present) never exceeding basal leaves; seeds smooth, with very shallow indistinct alveolae; alps and subalps

Pedicels/peduncles never with long glandular hairs; sepals often vertically infolded or concave in fruit; seeds slightly rugose with small, shallow, c. isodiametric alveolae; usually robust, much-branched plants of damp, weedy sites

Pedicels/peduncles with occasional long, patent glandular hairs (sometimes deciduous with age); sepals never folded deeply inwards in fruit; seeds smooth with very shallow c. oblong alveolae; fine, trailing to scrambling plant of damp, sheltered areas of north-east
At least inner sepals with broad hyaline margins; sepals usually reflexed in spent fruits; mericarps sparsely hairy, without distinctly ciliate suture margins; seeds with small, elongate alveolae
Sepals without obvious hyaline margins; sepals rarely reflexed in spent fruit; mericarps pubescent with distinctly ciliate suture margins; seeds with large, isodia- metric alveolae

Plants rosetted, if flowering stem ever developed, then never exceeding basal leaves; sepals hirsute to villous with long whitish hairs and apical mucro 1.3–2 mm long; higher-montane forests, subalpine and alpine grasslands and herbfields

Plants forming elongate flowering stems far exceeding basal leaves (rosetted only during overwintering stage); sepals variously hairy, not densely hirsute or villous, mucro rarely exceeding 1 mm long; habitats various, never truly alpine
Pedicel/peduncle to c. 8 cm long at anthesis (rarely subsessile); pedicel/ peduncle indumentum antrorse to c. patent; petals bright pink, exceeding sepals
Flowers usually sessile at anthesis (pedicels elongating in fruit); pedicel/peduncle indumentum usually dense, retrorse; petals narrow, red-purple, not exceeding sepals
Indumentum of stems strongly retrorse-appressed
Indumentum of stems variously spreading to somewhat retrorse (but not strongly appressed)

Leaves shallowly or deeply incised, lobes not narrow-linear, never appearing 'tangled'; sepal mucro very short (under 0.5 mm) or absent; at least pedicel and peduncle with occasional long patent glandular hairs; apparently confined to moist sheltered sites

Leaves deeply dissected, lobes narrow-linear, usually appearing 'tangled'; sepal mucro distinct (usually 0.5–1 mm long); indumentum not including long glandular hairs; usually dry sites in grasslands and grassy woodlands
Flowers bright pink to magenta (sometimes fading to pink); anthers without blue dehiscence lines; indumentum always retrorse and strongly appressed on petioles, stems and (usually) pedicel/peduncle

Flowers pale pink; anthers with faint blue dehiscence lines; indumentum sometimes retrorse-appressed on late-season growth but lower stems, basal petioles and pedicel/peduncle pubescent with very short recurved to long, patent hairs
Indumentum, particularly on pedicel and peduncle, tomentose, puberulous or pubescent, sometimes greyish, with dense, very short, soft, often recurved hairs
Indumentum, particularly on pedicel and peduncle, conspicuously spreading, recurved or retrorse, not consistently very short and dense

Flowers never more than 18 mm diam.; inflorescence always 1-flowered (rarely 2- or 3-flowered through monochasial growth); inner sepals sometimes with narrow-translucent margins but never with retuse apices; mericarp without ciliate suture margins

Flowers large (18–25 mm diam.), mostly twinned, but often single and twinned on same plant; at least inner sepals with broad-translucent margins and more or less retuse apices; mericarp with shortly ciliate suture margins
Stems (or at least petioles) pilose to villous, including at least some long patent hairs
Stems with short to long, retrorse to recurved (but not patent) hairs
Leaf-lobes usually narrow to narrow-linear; anther dehiscence lines pale to dark blue-purple
Leaf-lobes broad, never narrow-linear; anther dehiscence lines obscure, not coloured

Petals bright pink to magenta (sometimes fading to pink but never pale pink or white), discolorous, veins rather obscure; sepal mucro usually longer than 0.5 mm; stems with hairs predominantly spreading at right angles
Petals pale pink to white, concolorous, with 3–5 translucent veins; sepal mucro usually shorter than 0.5 mm; older stems with retrorse to appressed indumentum

Mericarps glabrous and strongly wrinkled; seed retained within mericarp on ripening; petals dark pink-magenta, incised or bilobed; indumentum villous with shining hairs; annual or biennial with short, narrow taproot

Mericarps puberulous to pubescent, rarely with longer hairs toward awn, smooth; seed released from mericarp on ripening; petals white to pale pink, c. obtuse, never incised or bilobed; hairs not shining; perennial with napiform to ellipsoid taproot

Plants annual or biennial with narrow taproot and/or fibrous roots; petals magenta, deeply incised or bilobed; stipules usually reddish; at least upper stems covered in long glandular and eglandular hairs; fruit rostrum with long glandular hairs; garden-escape, often growing on wasteland

Plants perennial with swollen napiform to ellipsoid taproot; petals mid-pink to whitish, never deeply incised or bilobed; stipules never reddish; stems and inflo- rescences without long glandular hairs; fruit rostrum eglandular

Sepal mucro less than 0.5 mm long; roots napiform to ellipsoid, not branched (rarely forked); mericarps with long-ciliate suture margins; anther dehiscence lines obscure; upper surfaces of leaves (and stems) not tuberculate

Sepal mucro at least 0.5 mm long; roots thickened, branched or tapering below but not napiform; mericarps without ciliate suture margins; anther dehiscence lines fine, purplish or bluish; upper surfaces of leaves (and stems) often tuberculate

Sepals elliptic and/or obovate, at least the two inner ones obovate with broad hyaline margins, mucro usually 1–1.5 mm long; seed reddish-brown with small, shallow, elongate alveolae; stems usually glabrescent or glabrous; upper surfaces of leaves glabrescent to sparsely hispid

Sepals ovate to lanceolate, margins narrow, white to translucent (never broad and hyaline), mucro usually less than 1 mm long; seed dark brown with large, deep, isodiametric alveolae; stems densely hispid or sometimes glabrescent; upper surfaces of leaves hispid

Leaves distinctly lobed to pinnate; stylar column longer than 3 cm in fruit

Leaves pinnate (i.e. divided into distinct leaflets, without a wing of connecting tissue along rachis) with more than 3 leaflets; petals white or pink
Indumentum of calyx (and usually pedicels) mostly glandular; largest leaves with more than 3 lobes
Indumentum of calyx and pedicel entirely or mostly eglandular; largest leaves usually 3-lobed to trifoliolate
Pits on mericarp at base of awns deep, glabrous, divided by 2 or more acute or narrowly winged papery folds; awn usually longer than 8.5 cm

Leaves deeply ternately dissected or palmatisect, coarsely hirsute to scabrous, strongly fragrant
Leaves shallowly lobed to almost entire (if ever lobed c. halfway to midrib, then lobes rather broad and obtuse); plants villous to pubescent or glabrous, hairs (when present) soft
Plants herbaceous; if petals ever 1 cm long then roots tuberous or extensively rhizomatous; not or hardly odorous, native plants
Plants shrubby, lacking tuberous roots or extensive rhizomes; petals 1 cm long or more; odorous garden-escapes
Petals 12–20 mm long, deep rosy magenta; leaves mostly radical; roots tuberous
Petals to 12 mm long, white to pink; taproots often fleshy but not tuberous, or plants extensively rhizomatous

Fertile stamens 3–5 (–6); larger petals 2–6 mm long, or if ever to 8 mm long, then sepals obtuse; plants neither ramifying nor rhizomatous

Indumentum of stems, peduncles and pedicels of mostly long, eglandular hairs (sometimes few sessile or shortly stalked glands present); sepal spur 1–4 (–8) mm long; plants taprooted or rarely, shortly rhizomatous, not colony-forming; leaves radical and cauline; very widespread

Calyx indumentum short, fine and dense; sepals obtuse (but sometimes minutely apiculate); larger petals c. 8 mm long; rare, alpine fire-follower
Calyx with scattered hairs; sepals acute; larger petals 2–6 mm long; mostly lowland species
Sepal hairs all short, coarse and scattered; nectary spur 0.5–1 mm long; larger petals 2–4 mm long; annual or short-lived perennial (often appearing following fire)
Sepal hairs long, spreading (often mixed with shorter hairs); nectary spur 1–3.5 mm long; larger petals 5–6 mm long; perennial
Stems, peduncles and pedicels lacking glandular hairs
Stems, peduncles and pedicels with glandular hairs
Leaves lobed c. halfway to midrib
Leaves entire or shallowly 3–9-lobed
Leaves strigose with spreading hairs mostly on veins or more or less glabrous, often with a dark ring around the middle above; margins strongly and acutely toothed
Leaves velvety, without a dark ring around the middle above; margins crenate

Leaves 6–18 mm wide, narrowly elliptic; midvein of lower surface usually evident through indumentum

Leaves either narrowly ovate (widest near base) or oblong-elliptic (c. straight-sided); leaf apex obtuse

Leaves narrowly oblanceolate (widest above middle), often a few slightly spathulate (widest just below the obtuse apex); upper surface of leaf with openly distributed very erect and narrow-spiculate protuberances, each usually subtended by a short wrinkle, surface glossy between

Leaves narrowly elliptic, narrowly oblong-elliptic, or narrowly ovate, widest at middle or near base, or straight-sided; upper surface of leaf with more or less densely distributed granules and/or robust subtriangular protuberances, surface between dull
Leaves 13–35 (–45) mm long, narrowly ovate or narrowly oblong-elliptic; larger protuberances of leaf surfaces mainly towards the margins
Leaves (20–) 35–70 (–120) mm long, narrowly oblong-elliptic; larger protuberances of leaf surfaces more or less uniformly distributed
Leaf upper surface with many conspicuous coarse short obtuse wrinkles, often each surmounted by a short subtriangular asperity
Leaf upper surface lacking conspicuous wrinkles but with densely to openly distributed fine granules or larger asperities
Leaf upper surface with very small fine granules only, lacking larger c. erect subtriangular to spiculate protuberances
Leaf upper surface with at least some large c. erect subtriangular to spiculate protuberances, often also with smaller granules
Leaf upper surface with the midvein shallowly channelled; inflorescence axes and pedicels densely and closely white-lanate
Leaf upper surface with the midvein deeply channelled; inflorescence axes and pedicels closely to loosely brown- or grey-floccose
Petals of terminal and lateral umbels of inflorescence discolorous (those of the terminal umbels pale yellow-green, those of the lateral umbels white to cream); inflorescence (100–) 200–300 mm long

Petals of terminal and lateral umbels of inflorescence concolorous, either white to cream or pale yellow-green (petals of the terminal umbels sometimes a darker shade of same colour); inflorescence 30–70 (–170) mm long

Fruit lacking locelli; leaf upper surface with fine granules and large subtriangular to spiculate protuberances, or the latter only

Leaves never spathulate at apex; leaf upper surface with dense to openly distributed, robust subtriangular protuberances, often also finer granules
Leaf upper surface with smaller granules more frequent than larger protuberances; inflorescence 30–70 (–170) mm long; petals white to cream or pale yellowish-green
Leaf upper surface with larger protuberances more frequent than smaller granules; inflorescence 60–260 mm long; petals white to cream, occasionally tinged purplish

Leaves petiolate or narrowly tapering into a cuneate or attenuate subsessile base
Stems mostly glabrous except in younger parts
Stems scabrous-pubescent or hispidulous throughout

Bracts conspicuously longer than calyx; corolla-tube c. 3 times longer than calyx
Calyx to c. 3 mm long; corolla limb 1.5–5 mm diam.; ultimate divisions of leaves c. triangular or ovate
Calyx long-tubular, 6–9 mm long; corolla limb 8–10 mm diam.; ultimate divisions of leaves narrow-linear
Calyx distinctly 5-toothed; erect or ascending perennial; corolla-tube 2–5 mm long
Calyx 4-toothed; procumbent annual; corolla-tube 1.5–2 mm long
Lower leaves deeply pinnately lobed, pinnatifid or pinnatisect; spikes 10–35(–40) cm long, not contracted
Lower leaves serrate-dentate, neither pinnatifid nor pinnatisect; spikes (1–)2–8(–10) cm long, somewhat contracted
Arrangement of flowers in spikes distant in lower half of rachis; hairs on rachis, bracts and calyx closely appressed; bracts ovate, often shorter than calyx; lamina with both rounded and acute teeth
Arrangement of flowers in spikes close to each other along rachis; hairs on rachis, bracts and calyx spreading; bracts narrow-lanceolate, equal to or longer than calyx; lamina with acute teeth

Calyx 5–10-toothed, not divided into 2 lips
Calyx with adaxial lip emarginate to undivided
Calyx with adaxial lip deeply 3-lobed or truncate with 3 sharp, almost obsolete teeth-like lobes

Calyx with abaxial lip emarginate or undivided

Calyx with pedicel attached centrally to the base of the calyx tube; corolla lobes more or less equal in length
Woody subshrubs to trees; adaxial calyx-lip without a prominent swelling
Perennial herbs; adaxial calyx-lip with a hollow prominent swelling
Fertile stamens 2 (minute staminodes sometimes present); anthers with locules separated by an elongated connective, 1 locule often sterile
Fertile stamens 4; anthers 2- or 1-locular; connective not elongated
Flowers in terminal spike-like inflorescences, subtended by large broadly ovate overlapping bracts; corolla-tube scarcely longer than calyx; stamens straight
Flowers in axillary pseudowhorls, without differentiated bracts (but with small bracteoles); corolla distinctly exceeding calyx; stamens curved
Leaves more or less odourless; bracteoles bristle-like, long-ciliate; calyx-lobes all long-acuminate; corolla pink to magenta
Leaves strongly lemon-scented; bracteoles ovate to obovate; adaxial lip of calyx with 3 short broadly triangular teeth; corolla white or pinkish

[link through]
Corolla more or less equally 4-lobed to indistinctly 2-lipped
Corolla distinctly 1- or 2-lipped
Flowers in compact, spike-like inflorescences, with overlapping mauve bracts vir- tually covering the sessile 3-flowered cymes (Lavender)
Flowers in axillary cymose whorls or pseudowhorls, in the axils of leaf-like bracts or solitary in leaf-axils; bracts not overlapping

Stamens 2; staminodes 2; leaves stiff, with margins sharply toothed
Stamens 4; leaves mostly soft, with margins entire or variously toothed, but never sharply toothed (Mints)

Corolla 1-lipped or apparently so (either adaxial lip slit so that the abaxial lip appears 5-lobed, or adaxial lip much-reduced and inconspicuous)
Corolla 2-lipped
Corolla blue to purple, rarely pinkish to white; adaxial lip inconspicuous; abaxial lip 3-lobed; leaves (other than in inflorescence) often congested and rosette-like at base
Corolla white; adaxial lip slit so that the abaxial lip appears 5-lobed; leaves cauline

Leaves trifoliolate
Leaves simple (but sometimes deeply lobed)
[link through]
Leaves in whorls of 3–5
Leaves opposite
Calyx 8–10-toothed
Calyx 5-toothed, sometimes only minutely toothed
[link through]
Calyx expanded and bonnet-like, much longer than corolla; teeth minute
Calyx not expanded, shorter or as long as corolla; teeth well developed
[link through]
Corolla with adaxial lip hooded
Corolla with adaxial lip broadly oblong, flat, erect, 2-lobed, not hooded

Upper leaves sessile, amplexicaule, subtending and embracing the flowers, c. equal to lower petiolate leaves
Upper leaves subtending flowers petiolate, not embracing the flowers, noticeably reduced in size
Perennial herb to 2 m high; inflorescences usually more than 12-flowered per leaf- axil; calyx 7–13 mm long
Annual herb to 0.4 m high; inflorescences mostly 3-flowered per bract or leaf-axil; calyx 5–7 mm long

Corolla bluish-mauve, rarely pink or pale blue, with darker purple spots on upper lip; leaf margin not ciliate; calyx with occasional multicellular hairs

leads.lead_text: Flower-clusters in distal leaf-axils, with distinctly visible internodes between the fertile nodes; calyx 13-veined (except M. pulegium 10-veined)

Flower-clusters terminal, forming a spike-like inflorescence, clusters subtended by narrow bracts, not subtended by leaves, with internodes frequently not visible between the fertile nodes; calyx 10-veined
Margins of calyx-lobes villous to pilose on inner surface; flowers 3–8 per axil
Margins of calyx-lobes glabrous or with short, usually erect hairs on inner surface, not conspicuously more densely hairy than outer surface of calyx tube; flowers few-many per axil

Branches and calyx hairy; flowers in 3–8-flowered clusters per leaf-axil; leaves ovate, often angular-ovate, rarely narrowly ovate or elliptic, 6–20 mm long, 4–12 mm wide; margin entire or sometimes with distant shallow serrations

Branches almost glabrous; calyx almost or quite glabrous on outer surface; flowers in 3-flowered clusters per leaf-axil; leaves narrowly elliptic to linear-elliptic, 5–35 mm long, 2–7 mm wide; margin entire
Pedicels usually subequal to or longer than calyces; flowers 2–8 (–12) per axil; leaves obtuse to subacute; pedicels usually subequal to or longer than calyces
Pedicels much shorter than calyces; flowers mostly crowded in dense clusters, 8-many flowers per axil, or if ever fewer than 6 flowers per axil, then leaves acute
Leaves narrowly ovate, 12–60 mm long, 8–20 mm wide, margin with 2–7 serrations, apex acute; calyx 13-veined; corolla white or pink
Leaves obovate, elliptic to almost orbicular, 6–30 mm long, 4–20 mm wide, margin entire or with small blunt serrations, apex obtuse or rounded; calyx 10-veined; corolla usually pale-mauve to lilac
Basal leaves petiolate; plants not producing fruits; calyx-lobes c. half as long as calyx-tube
Basal leaves sessile; plants producing fruits; calyx-lobes half as long to c. equal to calyx-tube
Leaves very obtuse to rounded at apex, indumentum of lower surface including some branched hairs
Leaves acute at apex, or if ever obtuse, hairs of lower surface all simple
Leaves villous beneath, hirsute above; inflorescence usually interrupted
Leaves (at least of mature growth) glabrous to sparsely hairy; inflorescence usually uninterrupted

Branches with short simple retrorse hairs only; leaf-base cuneate to tapering, mar- gin crenate or almost entire
Branches with long multicellular, spreading to patent hairs, with or without short simple retrorse hairs; leaf-base truncate or cor-date, margin pinnatifid to pinnatisect or incised
Leaf margin crenate; inflorescence usually much-branched; corolla 3.5–5 mm long
Leaf margin almost entire, with shallow distant serrations; inflorescence unbranched; corolla 7–10 mm long

leads.lead_text: Leaves in whorls of 5 or 6, crowded together (internodes short), alpine to subalpine plant of eastern Victoria
Leaves in whorls of 3 or 4, sometimes opposite
Leaves less than 2.5 mm wide, usually scabrous, margin recurved to strongly revolute

Leaves at least 2.5 mm wide, glabrous or almost so, margin not or only slightly recurved (lamina c. flat, often slightly incurved), or if leaves less than 2.5 mm wide then margin never recurved (in W. crassifolia and W. longifolia)
Calyx-lobes less than half as long as tube; leaves sessile, rigid; flowers white; intricate or divaricate shrub of mallee communities
Calyx-lobes usually at least half as long as tube; leaves with petiole 0.3–2 mm long (rarely sessile), c. soft-textured; flowers mostly c. mauve
Spreading shrub to c. 0.5 m high; calyx-lobes 0.6–0.7 times length of tube; corolla c. 10 mm long; endemic in Snowy River gorge area
Slender, erect shrub with suberect to spreading branches to 2 m high; calyx-lobes 0.3–1.3 (–1.7) times length of tube; corolla 6.5–8.5 mm long; scattered from mallee areas to far east
Leaf broad-oblong to -elliptic or subcircular, 1.3–1.8 times as long as wide; calyx- lobes (0.3–) 0.6 times tube; shrub of subalpine areas
Leaf narrow, linear, ovate, elliptic to slightly oblong, 3–18 times as long as wide; shrubs of lower altitudes
Calyx-lobes triangular to narrowly triangular, 3–3.7 mm long; leaf narrowly ovate to narrowly elliptic, 3–4 (–11) mm wide
Calyx-lobes triangular, 1.5–2.8 mm long; leaf linear or narrowly elliptic to slightly oblong,1–2.5 mm wide
Calyx with outer surface moderately to densely hairy; leaves narrowly elliptic to slightly oblong, 5–15 mm long, length-to-width ratio 3–6; corolla 12–14 mm long
Calyx with outer surface sparsely hairy to glabrescent, rarely moderately hairy; leaves linear, 12–35 mm long, length-to-width ratio 10–18; corolla 8–10 mm long

leads.lead_text: Calyx-lobes unequal in length; corolla mauve to blue-purple, pinkish, or white, never red, yellow, or metallic blue-green; corolla-tube short, broad distally; abaxial lobe longer and more spreading than the erect adaxial lobes; fruit enclosed by inward folded abaxial calyx-lobe; adaxial calyx-lobe usually recurved (section Prostanthera)

Calyx-lobes more or less equal in length; corolla red (rarely pinkish), yellow, metallic blue-green, never white, mauve to purplish; corolla-tube long, slightly expanded distally; median adaxial and abaxial lobes more or less equal; fruit not enclosed by the calyx-lobes (section Klanderia)
Flowers arranged in obviously terminal racemose or paniculate inflorescences, the floral leaves all or mostly reduced to membranous, usually deciduous, bracteoles
Flowers all appearing axillary, with floral leaves similar to (but sometimes smaller than) leaves on the branchlets
Leaves entire, glabrous (rarely with a few hairs along midrib) with margin entire
Leaves with margin variously toothed, or if ever entire or apparently entire (from recurved margins) then surfaces distinctly hairy
Leaves non-aromatic or only slightly so; lamina narrow- to broad-ovate or oblong, appearing c. linear when margin strongly revolute
Leaves strongly aromatic (when crushed); lamina almost circular
Leaves sessile, to 2 mm wide; calyx 4–5.5 mm long
Leaves petiolate, 3–10 mm wide; calyx 2–3 mm long
Leaves flat
Leaves with margin recurved or revolute
Leaf-apex obtuse to rounded; corolla dark mauve to purple, occasionally pinkish, with markings absent; anther appendages to 0.5 mm long or absent
Leaf-apex acute to acuminate; corolla white to pale mauve with purple spots in throat; anther appendages distinct, c. 1.5 mm long

Erect shrub (to c. 3 m high); petiole to 10 mm long; anther locules with a basal tuft of narrowly triangular trichomes or hairs; leaf-lamina ovate, broadly ovate to obovate or c. circular, to 30 mm long and 15 mm wide

Erect shrub to small tree (1–5 m high); petiole (8–) 10–15 mm long; anther locules with small point basally, lacking trichomes or hairs; leaf-lamina ovate to narrowly ovate, rarely elliptic, 12–50 (–60) mm long, 9–25 (–30) mm wide, with margin usually toothed (rarely entire)
Leaf-lamina ovate, 15–30 mm long, 8–12 mm wide; anther locules with a tuft of basal narrowly triangular trichomes; erect openly branched shrub (2–2.5 m high)
Leaf-lamina broadly ovate to obovate or c. circular, 3–20 mm long, 3–15 mm wide; anther locules with tuft of basal hairs; erect compact to spreading shrub (0.5–3 m high)
Leaves hairy on both surfaces
Leaves glabrous, except for a few short stiff hairs near margin
Leaf-lamina appearing narrowly ovate to narrowly elliptic when margin revolute, rarely appearing ovate, 1.5–6 mm wide; base shortly attenuate; margin entire
Leaf-lamina ovate, 6–13 mm wide; base obtuse to rounded; margin crenate
Leaves convex or with margin recurved to revolute, if ever more or less flat then lamina ovate to obovate
Leaves flat or channelled above, or margins strongly incurved, lamina linear to very narrowly ovate
Leaves more or less terete, oblong (often narrowly so) or linear
Leaves narrowly to broadly ovate, c. orbicular or obovate, never lobed; margin often strongly recurved or revolute
Branches with hairs restricted to area between lateral ridges
Branches densely hairy throughout
Spines absent
Spines present
Leaves narrowly ovate to ovate or obovate, if broadly ovate then usually appearing narrowly ovate because margin revolute (in P. decussata)
Leaves c. orbicular, usually appearing angular-ovate (rhomboid)
Leaves glabrous
Leaves often with upper surface almost glabrous, but always with at least a few short tooth-like hairs near margin
Leaves obovate, 4–8 mm long; bracteoles not persistent, 3–3.5 mm long; strongly aromatic shrub; branches densely covered with short, more or less spreading hairs
Leaves narrowly ovate, 5–15 mm long; bracteoles persistent, c. 2.5 mm long; slightly aromatic; branches sparsely covered with short, appressed hairs between ridges
Stem hairs retrorse to spreading; pedicels less than 3 mm long; calyx greater than 5.5 mm long
Stem hairs antrorse to spreading and/or stems almost glabrous; pedicels usually greater than 3 mm long; calyx less than 5 mm long
Leaves linear, conduplicate or incurved; appearing terete
Leaves flat or slightly channelled above; margin slightly incurved or slightly recurved
Leaf-lamina ovate to narrowly ovate, sometimes suborbicular, never terete or linear-obovate
Leaf-lamina c. linear-terete to -obovate
Leaf-lamina 10–50 mm long; petiole (1.5–) 2–5 (–8) mm long; venation visible, often faint
Leaf-lamina (1–) 1.5–3 (–3.8) mm long; petiole absent or to 0.3 (–0.5) mm long; venation not visible
Bracteoles 10–18 mm long; inner surface of calyx-lobes hairy; leaves non-aromatic
Bracteoles 4–6.5 mm long; inner surface of calyx-lobes glabrous; leaves aromatic

Leaves entire to toothed, or if ever pinnatisect, then division more than 1 mm wide; cypselas wingless

Cypselas with marginal ridges developed and often prominent, flattened faces with or without ribbing

Pappus barbellate; cypselas slightly compressed

Flattened faces of cypselas ribbed

Cypselas 6–11 mm long; stems unbranched above base; plants perennial
Facial ribs of cypselas convergent below the summit of the cypsela body and none or few of the ribs continued through to the summit; marginal ribs commonly fused with adjacent facial ribs

Cypselas glabrous toward base (apart from callus tuft), upper part rather sparsely hairy, devoid of glandular hairs

Marginal ribs of cypselas covered with hairs similar to those of cypsela faces (but hairs sometimes smaller), glands or glandular hairs often present on cypsela faces
Leaves oblanceolate to elliptic, sometimes with a pair of teeth or lobes toward apex; inner involucral bracts acuminate; cypselas with all facial ribs continued to base

Cypselas with narrow subclavate or straight blunt hairs between and/or on ribs; Melbourne area and eastern Victoria

Eglandular hairs on upper part of cypsela faces entire or minutely and acutely bifid; hairs on marginal ridges of similar length to those of faces (but sometimes incurved); vegetative parts weakly glandular or eglandular
Leaves once or twice trilobed or trisected above a very narrow, petiole-like base, not or hardly folded; involucres less than 6 mm long

Leaves cuneate, oblanceolate or obovate (rarely spathulate and then more or less evenly tapered to base), usually longitudinally folded, entire or with a pair of short lobes toward tip; involucres mostly more than 6 mm long
Indumentum of straight or slightly curved or crisped, spreading to appressed, stiffish hairs, if ever somewhat cottony never completely covering stems, leaves or bracts

Leaves alternate (but sometimes in small clusters)

Margins entire

Indumentum (branchlets and leaf undersurfaces) of stellate or centrifixed (T-shaped or Y-shaped) hairs
Hairs stellate
Hairs T-shaped or Y-shaped

Indumentum of closely appressed T-shaped hairs
Indumentum of somewhat spreading to woolly Y-shaped hairs

Leaves crenate to distantly serrate, pubescent and/or scabrous above, loosely covered beneath by brownish hairs; far East Gippsland only
Involucre more than 14 mm diam.; leaves elliptic to spathulate, entire or lobed in the distal half, upper surface grey-green and moderately to densely stellate-hairy
Involucre less than 14 mm diam., or if more than 14 mm diam. then leaves not as above
Capitula sessile; leaves c. spahtulate; very rare, in upper Tambo River catchment only
Capitula pedunculate; leaves elliptic, oblong or obovate; localised in Snowfields on and near Bogong High Plains
Involucral bracts subequal; capitula often solitary and terminal; lateral veins of leaves not apparent; wiry shrub usually of wet lowland heaths

Involucral bracts graduating (i.e. outer significantly shorter than inner); capitula usually in corymbs or panicles (but solitary and sessile in O. brevipedunculata); lateral veins of leaves apparent; rarely occurring in wet heathlands
Leaves tuberculate on the upper surface; lower surface with indumentum of coarse, golden or dark yellowish hairs
Upper leaf surface glabrous or variously hairy with stellate or apparently simple hairs, but lacking tubercles; lower surface with close, dense white, grey or pale yellowish hairs

Leaves deeply wrinkled due to strongly impressed veins; upper surface with large (more than 0.2 mm long) tubercules; leave shape very variable, from oblong to broadly elliptic; margins sinuate, coarsely toothed or lobed, rarely entire; scattered in eastern Victoria with an isolated population at Mt Buangor
Leaves not deeply wrinkled; upper surface with small (less than 0.2 mm long), often deciduous tubercles; leaves usually narrow-ovate and regualrly toothed; restricted to the Otways
Leaves greyish above; capitula solitary and sessile; restricted to upper subalpine and alpine areas
Leaves usually green above; capitula pedunculate, usually in panicles; widespread from near sea-level to alps

Leaves lanceolate to narrow-ovate, usually thin-textured with strongly impressed veins; not distinctly glandular, lacking a foetid odour when crushed; margins usually entire or sinuate, rarely serrate

Leaves narrow-ovate, ovate, oblong or obovate, rarely lanceolate, usually thick-textured with veins not or only slighlty impressed; distinctly glandular on one or both surfaces (glands often hidden by hairs) and producing a foetid odour when crushed; margins lobed or toothed, rarely entire
Branchlets (and usually leaf undersurfaces) whitish-cottony, sometimes also with simple bristles and/or glands
Branchlets and leaf undersurfaces lacking (or with only sparse) cottony hairs, either glabrous (but sometimes viscid or resinous) or with simple bristles (sometimes glandular)
Capitula sessile in leaf-axils; ligules of ray florets often not developed
Capitula terminal and/or pedunculate (sometimes appearing axillary when terminating very short lateral branchlets); ligules of ray florets conspicuous, distinctly exceeding the involucre
Leaves (8–) 10–25 mm long, the undersurface distinctly white-cottony; strictly coastal shrub
Leaves to 8 mm long, the undersurface almost or quite obscured by the revolute margins; mostly inland areas, rare along coasts
Leaves to 4.5 mm long, produced in dense clusters along branchlets; coastal
Leaves to 8 mm long, scattered to loosely clustered along branchlets; mostly inland, but approaching coast in Anglesea area
Ligules of ray florets well developed (3–5 per capitulum), 1.5–2.5 mm long
Ligules of ray florets not developed or vestigial, not exceeding styles of florets

Capitula terminal on very short lateral branches, or pedunculate from axils; leaves linear to narrow-elliptic (if ever ovate then less than 3 mm long and densely clustered), with undersurfaces largely concealed by revolute margins; involucral bracts pubescent or glabrous
Capitula terminal on normal branches; leaves obovate to elliptic (1.5–) 3–15 mm long, with undersurfaces apparent, not clustered along branches; at least the outer involucral bracts pubescent

Leaves 3–22 mm long, not produced in distinct clusters along branches; capitula usually pedunculate from upper axils; indumentum either including erect bristles, or almost entirely gummed down from resinous exudate

Leaves to 3 (rarely to 4.5) mm long, distinctly clustered along branches on very reduced lateral branches; capitula terminal (sessile or subsessile) on lateral branches; indumentum neither including bristles nor gummed down by a resinous exudate
Indumentum bristly, the cottony hairs (sparse to dense) not gummed down; widespread shrub, but not in mallee areas
Indumentum not including bristles, the cottony hairs almost entirely gummed down by a resinous exudate (but usually remaining apparent in axils); very rare shrub of far north-west mallee
Leaf clusters loose, the largest leaves 2–3 mm long; widespread but not truly coastal
Leaf clusters very compact, the largest leaves to 2 mm long, or if ever to 4.5 mm long then plants coastal

Ray florets with ligules 3–6 mm long

Leaves very convex, appearing almost globular, usually less than 1 mm long, the outer ones of each cluster closely appressed to branchlets; leaf clusters usually under 1.5 mm diam., sometimes virtually contiguous and obscuring the stem
Leaves not appearing almost globular, mostly 1–2 (–4.5) mm long, not appressed to branchlets; leaf clusters mostly more than 1.5 mm diam., not contiguous
Leaves to 2 mm long; inland areas
Leaves to 4.5 mm long; coastal
Indumentum of branchlets and leaf undersurfaces closely matted, often yellowish, resinous and slightly viscid; dry rocky areas of East Gippsland
Indumentum of branchlets and leaf undersurfaces loose-cottony, white, not viscid; north and west from Port Phillip
Leaves to 8 mm long. Ray florets 7–12, white or mauve; disc florets 6–13; northwest and Bacchus Marsh areas
Leaves to c. 15 mm long. Ray florets 8–25, white; disc florets 14–50; north-central to north-west
Plants glabrous or slightly cottony, often resinous, sometimes viscid
Plants with leaves and/or stems mainly bristly or scabrous-pubescent, sometimes glandular and or with cottony hair

Leaves various, margins plane to revolute or slightly thickened; capitula solitary or in leafy panicles; involucral bracts and leaves lacking nodular swellings; shrubs typically of dry ground
Slender shrub to c. 2.5 m high, single-stemmed from base; leaves 8–55 mm long; widespread in (mostly) southern districts
Subshrub to c. 70 cm high, with several short-lived stems from a perennial rootstock; leaves 3–14 (–24) mm long; rare in south-west
Pappus no longer than body of cypsela; viscid shrub with linear leaves 8–25 mm long; apparently confined to dry rocky country along Mitchell River in East Gippsland
Pappus c. twice as long as body of cypsela; western or northern Victoria or coastal
Leaves flat (but sometimes linear); margins plane to slightly recurved
Leaves terete (or appearing so from revolute margins), or compressed-terete, virtually as thick as wide in cross-section
Inflorescence a corymb; leaves linear to narrow-obovate
Inflorescence a single terminal capitulum; leaves obovate to cuneate

Stems terete; leaves acute, quite entire. Ray florets mauve, pink or white; cypselas glabrous or sparsely hairy between ribs; bushy viscid shrub of coasts
Ray florets 12–24 per capitulum, rich mauve to purple; cypselas glabrous
Ray florets 7–13 per capitulum, white to pale mauve; cypselas sericeous
Capitula 31–45 mm diam.; ray florets 18–25 mm long, pale mauve or white
Capitula 13–32 mm diam.; ray florets 4–12 mm long, white
Branchlets somewhat cottony (usually obvious in leaf-axils) but often gummed down by resinous exudate; leaves somewhat spreading, margins revolute; capitula shortly but distinctly pedunculate
Branchlets quite glabrous (but resinous); leaves subappressed to branches (rarely spreading), margins plane to slightly upcurved; capitula sessile, rarely in few-flowered corymbs

Capitula solitary and terminal (rarely in loose clusters) on main branches, 20–50 mm diam

Stems with dense stalked glandular hair and sessile glands; lower leaf surface lacking or with very sparse cottony hair; capitula sessile, solitary, terminal on main shoots and short lateral branches; ligules blue-mauve; montane and subalpine areas mostly above 1000 m alt.

Stems with eglandular setae, rarely with short stalked glandular overtopped by longer eglandular setae; lower leaf surface with sparse to moderate cottony hair; capitula  pedunculate from leaf axils, terminal on short lateral shoots, rarely terminal on main stems; ligules usually white, sometimes blue-mauve; coastal or inland, usually below 1000 m alt.
Younger branchlets and peduncles densely beset with short, erect, gland-tipped hairs; rare, fruitily aromatic shrub of eastern ranges
Plants non-glandular

Leaves linear, under 3 mm wide, margins revolute, coarsely ciliate especially toward base; peduncles relatively long (mostly 8–30 cm) and naked; involucral bracts graduating; scattered in heathland from mallee areas to Wilsons Promontory
Leaves obovate or elliptic, mostly wider than 3 mm, flat; peduncles under 5 cm long, or if longer then bracteate; involucral bracts subequal; mallee only
Leaves entire, narrow-obovate or -elliptic; indumentum of subappressed strigose hairs; involucre 5–7 mm long
Leaves serrate, obovate with somewhat stem-clasping bases; indumentum of coarse, spreading bristles; involucre 7–10 mm long

Leaves usually more than 2 (up to 5) cm wide, stiff and flat, oblanceolate to narrowly oblanceolate or elliptic; pellicle of upper leaf surface very thin and weak, soon breaking up into fine, more or less deciduous webby fragments; leaf underside with a dense compact tomentum covered by a very thin silvery pellicle which soon breaks up into microscopic hair-like fragments, satiny to the touch; generally robust plants, sometimes forming tufts up to 1 m wide

Thin scaly rhizomes absent; rootstock branched and more or less woody, erect or ascending, or creeping and rooting to form often extensive patches; if tomentum of leaf underside short, with the midrib conspicuous, then tomentum hairs terete (under high magnification) and intermediate involucral bracts narrowly ovate- acuminate to narrowly triangular-acuminate

Tufted herbs with thin spreading scaly rhizomes; leaf underside with very short tomentum, the midrib usually raised and conspicuous; tomentum hairs flattened (under high magnification); intermediate involucral bracts narrowly triangular to narrowly triangular-subulate

Intermediate involucral bracts narrowly ovate- to narrowly triangular-acuminate, usually weakly tomentose at least distally, soon glabrescent and usually reddish-purple over most of the back, the margins densely woolly-fimbriate; leaves narrowly oblanceolate to narrowly elliptic or linear; pellicle soon rupturing beneath to reveal the short more or less woolly tomentum on the leaf underside, the raised midrib usually conspicuous; tomentum hairs terete (under high magnification)

Intermediate involucral bracts narrowly triangular to narrowly triangular-subulate, more or less tomentose (but usually glabrescent at least in the lower third), reddish-purple distally, the margins more or less fimbriate; leaves subulate to linear-subulate, sometimes expanded and narrowly oblanceolate; pellicle usually tardily rupturing beneath to reveal the long, woolly tomentum which fills the cavity on the leaf underside, usually obscuring the raised midrib; tomentum hairs flattened (under high magnification)

Ligules yellow

Involucre rather broadly campanulate with 18–22 bracts; at least the lower leaves with several deeply incised, forward-pointing teeth

Involucral bracts and bracteoles not glandular; cypselas not as above

Inflorescence of up to c. 30 capitula; bracteoles of most capitula mostly more than 5; leaves not initially rosetted; cypselas uniform, either glabrous or hairy

Leaves with 0–40 marginal points per side, sometimes developing strap-like basal segments; mid-stem leaves with rachis less than 0.8 mm wide with length:width ratio greater than 15 when dried; cypselas (1.6–)2–4.5 mm long; mostly in south and east
Involucre 9–12.5 mm long; inflorescence often a single capitulum; decumbent to suberect rhizomatous perennial of sandy coasts
Involucre less than 8 mm long; inflorescence usually of several capitula
Involucral bracts 13 or fewer; ligulate florets to 6 mm long
Involucral bracts more than 13 in at least most capitula; ligulate florets (5–) 6–15 mm long

Cypselas glabrous or shortly hairy in longitudinal rows; pappus deciduous

Involucral bracts no more than 14, not black-tipped

Leaves of major branches to 50 mm wide; reticulate venation clearly defined on one or both surfaces

Margins of leaves of the major branches entire (margin of stem leaves may be dentate), revolute; bracteoles with length:width ratio mostly less than 2; peduncles glabrous at anthesis

Leaves densely appressed woolly on lower surface only, inflorescence branchlets, peduncles and bracts sparsely woolly; bracteoles less than 4 mm long

Female florets disc florets with 2–5 lobes; cypselas glabrous or with short papillose hairs; inflorescence of 10 to several hundred capitula
Involucral bracts 12 or 13 in majority of capitula; female florets 8–13; cypselas of female florets 3–6 mm long, slightly lageniform
Involucral bracts 7–10, or occasionally to 13, in a majority of capitula; female florets predominantly 4–8; cypselas of female florets 2–3.5 mm long, not lageniform
Cypselas glabrous, lustrous
Cypselas with papillose hairs or if glabrous then not lustrous
Stem creeping to erect, renewed annually from a short rhizome; subalpine
Stem erect, not renewed from a rhizome; lowland swamps

Involucres 1.0–3.0 mm wide, comprising 7–14 bracts
Cypselas lageniform, 3.0–6.0 mm long
Cypselas cylindric, 2.0–3.0 mm long
Leaves conspicuously retrorsely lobed
Leaves unlobed, or if lobed, segments not conspicuously retrorse
Capitula with up to 50% of florets female or at least with only female structures emergent from corolla tube and reduced corolla lobes
Capitula with 70–80% of florets female, very rarely with 50% of florets female

Cypselas 2.0–3.0 mm long; involucre 5.0–7.5 mm long

leads.lead_text: Lemma with a moderately dense to dense covering of hairs, with or without a row of hairs below the sinus and another above the callus

Lemma with hairs in distinct transverse rows (although these sometimes incomplete), otherwise glabrous or occasionally with scattered hairs between the rows, or lemma glabrous except for marginal tufts of hairs
Hairs of lemma more or less uniform in length
Hairs of lemma elongating gradually from the base to the sinus or the upper row of hairs distinctly longer than the remainder
Central awn of lemma not or barely longer than lateral lobes, palea broad, obtuse, not or barely exceeding sinus
Central awn of lemma distinctly longer (by at least 2 mm) than lateral lobes, palea narrow and exceeding sinus by 2 mm or more

Lemma mostly 4–5 mm long, central awn strongly twisted in lower 3–5 mm; robust, caespitose grass usually with finely inrolled leaves (channelled in alpine forms), 20–40 cm long, and culms often exceeding 1 m

Lemma mostly 2.5–4 mm long, central awn weakly (once or twice) twisted in lower 1.5–2.5 mm; rhizomatous grass producing sparse tufts of channelled to inrolled leaves to 15 cm long, and culms to 60 cm high
Hairs of lemma uniformly short (0.5–1.2 mm) except for a conspicuously longer upper series (c. 3 mm long); lemma less than 3 mm long with narrow lateral lobes
Hairs of lemma mostly longer than 1.2 mm long, increasing in length incrementally from basal to upper series, or, if the upper series suddenly longer, lateral lobes broad; lemma more than 3 mm long
Culms mostly 4–6-noded; hairs of greater part of lemma c. 1 mm long; lateral lobes of lemma exceeding the upper series of hairs by 2–4 mm; typically of drier, raised, often rocky sites

Culms mostly 3-noded; hairs of greater part of lemma c. 0.5 mm long; lateral lobes of lemma not or hardly exceeding the upper series of hairs (rarely exceeding hairs by 2–3 mm); typically of damp or sandy lowland sites

Lateral lobes of lemma no longer than lemma body, and usually not longer than upper hairs of lemma; lemma surface granular (but sometimes obscured by hairs); plants usually less than 40 cm high, with compact, ovate panicles, to c. 4 cm long

Lateral lobes of lemma longer than lemma body (rarely subequal in rare, northern R. richardsonii) and exceeding upper hairs of lemma; lemma surface smooth; plants usually more than 40 cm high with linear to lanceolate inflorescences, usually 5 cm long or more
Palea exceeding sinus of lemma by up to 2.5 mm, never reaching midway on the lateral lemma lobes
Palea exceeding sinus of lemma by 3 mm or more, or if less, then palea approaching or exceeding midway along the lateral lemma lobes
Palea broadly obovate, obtuse, exceeding the sinus of the lemma by no more than 1 mm; lateral lobes of lemma rather broad, membranous at base, scarcely or very shortly setiform at the tips

Palea lanceolate to narrowly ovate, tapered to a narrow but truncate, often twisted apex, distinctly exceeding sinus (by 1–2.5 mm); lateral lobes of lemma attenuate into the distinct but often short setae
Base of central awn copper-coloured and strongly twisted near base; inflorescence mostly 6–12 cm long; glumes 12–18 mm long; culms often more than 50 cm high
Base of central awn pale and twisted no more than twice near base; inflorescence mostly 2–6 cm long; glumes 7–13 mm long; culms mostly less than 50 cm high
Lemma 4–5.5 mm long, lateral lobes of lemma with setiform tips, at least 5 mm long in all, central awn strongly twisted in basal 4–6 mm; palea reaching to about halfway along lateral lemma lobes
Lemma 3–4 mm long, lateral lobes without setiform tips, less than 5 mm long, central awn weakly twisted in basal c. 2 mm; palea approaching tips of lateral lobes
Lemma with a complete row of hairs below the sinus (rarely with one or two tufts suppressed in some forms of R. setaceum)

Lemma with only dorsal and/or marginal tufts of hairs below the sinus (rarely with an almost complete upper series in R. racemosum and R. pilosum) or with hairs lacking (excluding the callus region which may be hairy)
Lemma less than 3 mm long (rarely to 3.5 mm long in the variable R. setaceum)
Lemma 3 mm long or more

Body of lemma rather broad (at least half as wide as long), triangular or more or less ovate in outline, lateral lobes with short (2–4 mm) setae; palea obovate, barely exceeding sinus; rather rare grass, mostly in and around the goldfields

Body of lemma narrow, oblong to narrow-triangular in outline, lateral lobes with very fine setae 4–9 mm long (or the lobes 3–4 mm overall); palea narrow-elliptic to lanceolate, shortly exceeding sinus; very common widespread and variable species

Lemma hairs confined to the lemma margins and a transverse row just below the base of the awn, or rarely also with just a few hairs along a transverse line just above the callus; consequently affording a completely uninterrupted view of most of the particularly shiny lemma surface
Lemma with a row or expanse of hairs just above the callus, the hairs interrupting the view of most of the dorsal surface of the lemma (perhaps only slightly)

Lemma with a complete row of hair tufts just above the callus; at least one other character not matching the above
Palea narrow, exceeding sinus of lemma by 2 mm or more and approaching setiform part of lateral lobes; lemma often with scattered hairs between the upper and lower series
Palea various, exceeding sinus by up to 2.5 mm but never approaching setiform part of lateral lobes; lemma usually quite glabrous between upper and lower series
Culms to c. 30 cm high; inflorescence dense, 2–5 cm long; leaves rigid, folded; subalpine to alpine grass of exposed crags
Culms mostly more than 40 cm high; inflorescence rather loose, to 15 cm long; leaves not rigid, closely inrolled; lowland to foothills grass, never subalpine or alpine

Margins of lateral lobes without conspicuous triangular lobes, rarely a minute 'shoulder' present at the base of the setiform part of the lobe

Body of lemma remaining pale (rarely maturing to golden brown in some forms of R. caespitosum); lower branches of inflorescence not long or reflexed at anthesis

Body of lemma firm, shining, without raised nerves; palea exceeding sinus by up to c. 1 mm, rather abruptly tapered to the obtuse apex; typically of damper sites and subalps

Base of central awn pale and twisted no more than twice near base; inflorescence mostly 2–6 cm long; glumes 7–13 mm long; culms mostly less than 50 cm high

Glumes only slightly longer than aggregated florets; palea glabrous between keels; inflorescence ovate; mostly rocky sites in alps and subalps

Lateral lobes of lemma at least as long as lemma body which is more than 2.5 mm long (or rarely only 2 mm long in R. pilosum), lemma body with at least some hair

Some tufts of hairs present on dorsal surface of lemma as well as callus
